10:37.annotated: And it was not [possible] for this Qur’ān to be produced by other than Allāh, but [it is] a confirmation of what was before it and a detailed explanation of the [former] Scripture, about which there is no doubt,[1] from the Lord of the worlds.

footnotes.text: This phrase refers back to the Qur’ān.

10:47.annotated: And for every nation is a messenger. So when their messenger comes,[1] it will be judged between them in justice, and they will not be wronged.

footnotes.text: To witness on the Day of Judgement.  Another meaning is "Once a messenger has come [to them in this world]..."

10:50.annotated: Say, "Have you considered: if His punishment should come to you by night or by day - for which [aspect] of it would the criminals be impatient?"[1]

footnotes.text: "Impatience" refers to the disbelievers' ridicule of the Prophet (ﷺ) by telling him to produce Allāh's punishment as proof of his truthfulness.

10:51.annotated: Then is it that when it has [actually] occurred you will believe in it? Now?[1] And you were [once] for it impatient.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., when it is too late to benefit from belief.
Challenging those who warned of it to bring it on immediately.

10:60.annotated: And what will be the supposition of those who invent falsehood about Allāh on the Day of Resurrection?[1] Indeed, Allāh is the possessor of bounty for the people, but most of them are not grateful.

footnotes.text: i.e., what do they think He will do with them.

10:61.annotated: And, [O Muḥammad], you are not [engaged] in any matter and do not recite any of the Qur’ān and you [people] do not do any deed except that We are witness over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight[1] within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater but that it is in a clear register.

footnotes.text: Or "the weight of a small ant."

10:67.annotated: It is He who made for you the night to rest therein and the day, giving sight.[1] Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.

footnotes.text: i.e., making things visible.

10:68.annotated: They[1] have said, "Allāh has taken a son." Exalted is He; He is the [one] Free of need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. You have no authority[2] for this [claim]. Do you say about Allāh that which you do not know?

footnotes.text: The Christians and others.
Or "evidence."

10:71.annotated: And recite to them the news of Noah, when he said to his people, "O my people, if my residence and my reminding of the signs of Allāh has become burdensome upon you - then I have relied upon Allāh. So resolve upon your plan and [call upon] your associates. Then let not your plan be obscure to you.[1] Then carry it out upon me and do not give me respite.

footnotes.text: i.e., Do not let it be a source of doubt or anxiety to you but let it be clear, open and defined.

10:74.annotated: Then We sent after him messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs. But they were not to believe in that which they had denied before.[1] Thus We seal over the hearts of the transgressors.

footnotes.text: i.e., the succeeding generations were persistent in disbelief.

10:87.annotated: And We inspired to Moses and his brother, "Settle your people in Egypt in houses and make your houses [facing the] qiblah[1] and establish prayer and give good tidings to the believers."

footnotes.text: In order that they might pray therein unseen by their enemy.

10:89.annotated: [Allāh] said, "Your supplication has been answered."[1] So remain on a right course and follow not the way of those who do not know."

footnotes.text: Literally, "the supplication of both of you," i.e., that of Moses and of Aaron, who joined by saying, "Āmeen" ("O Allāh, respond").

10:92.annotated: So today We will save you in body[1] that you may be to those who succeed you a sign. And indeed, many among the people, of Our signs, are heedless.

footnotes.text: i.e., his dead body will be preserved and not destroyed.

10:95.annotated: And never be of those who deny the signs of Allāh and [thus] be among the losers.[1]

footnotes.text: Among the interpretations of the last two verses is that they were meant to stir the Prophet (ﷺ) to declare and confirm his certainty, which he did.  Another is that although the words are addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ), they are directed to all people.

10:100.annotated: And it is not for a soul [i.e., anyone] to believe except by permission of Allāh, and He will place defilement[1] upon those who will not use reason.

footnotes.text: Among its meanings are filth, wrath, punishment, disbelief, confusion and error.

10:103.annotated: Then We will save Our messengers and those who have believed. Thus, it is an obligation upon Us that We save the believers.[1]

footnotes.text: From Allāh's punishment.

10:106.annotated: And do not invoke[1] besides Allāh that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be of the wrongdoers.'"[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., worship.
See footnote to 10:95.

11:1.annotated: Alif, Lām, Rā.[1] [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Aware[2]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.
Refer to footnotes of 6:18.

11:6.annotated: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allāh is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage.[1] All is in a clear register.

footnotes.text: Before birth and after death.

11:8.annotated: And if We hold back from them the punishment for a limited time, they will surely say,[1] "What detains it?" Unquestionably, on the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to ridicule.

footnotes.text: In ridicule and disbelief.

11:12.annotated: Then would you possibly leave [out] some of what is revealed to you,[1] or is your breast constrained by it because they say, "Why has there not been sent down to him a treasure or come with him an angel?" But you are only a warner. And Allāh is Disposer of all things.

footnotes.text: Knowing of the Prophet's difficulties, Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) urges him to patience, certain that he would not fail to convey the message in its entirety.

11:14.annotated: And if they do not respond to you - then know that it [i.e., the Qur’ān] was revealed with the knowledge of Allāh[1] and that there is no deity except Him. Then,[2] would you [not] be Muslims?

footnotes.text: i.e., that knowledge which no one possesses except Him (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).
After having been convinced by such evidence.

11:15.annotated: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments - We fully repay them for their deeds therein,[1] and they therein will not be deprived.

footnotes.text: i.e., during worldly life.

11:16.annotated: Those are the ones for whom there is not in the Hereafter but the Fire. And lost is what they did therein,[1] and worthless is what they used to do.

footnotes.text: i.e., during worldly life.

11:17.annotated: So is one who [stands] upon a clear evidence from his Lord [like the aforementioned]? And a witness[1] from Him follows it,[2] and before it was the Scripture of Moses to lead and as mercy. Those [believers in the former revelations] believe in it [i.e., the Qur’ān]. But whoever disbelieves in it from the [various] factions - the Fire is his promised destination. So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.

footnotes.text: Referring to Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) or to the angel Gabriel.
Testifying to its truth.  Additionally, it can mean "recites it," i.e., the Qur’ān.

11:20.annotated: Those were not causing failure [to Allāh] on earth, nor did they have besides Allāh any protectors. For them the punishment will be multiplied. They were not able to hear, nor did they see.[1]

footnotes.text: They refused to listen to the truth or to perceive it.

11:27.annotated: So the eminent among those who disbelieved from his people said, "We do not see you but as a man like ourselves, and we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest of us [and] at first suggestion.[1] And we do not see in you over us any merit; rather, we think you are liars."

footnotes.text: i.e., without any thought or hesitation.

11:40.annotated: [So it was], until when Our command came and the oven overflowed,[1] We said, "Load upon it [i.e., the ship] of each [creature] two mates and your family, except those about whom the word [i.e., decree] has preceded, and [include] whoever has believed." But none had believed with him, except a few.

footnotes.text: As a sign to Noah of the imminence of the flood.  The tannūr is a large, rounded oven.  The word can also mean the earth's lowlands.

11:57.annotated: But if you turn away, then I have already conveyed that with which I was sent to you. My Lord will give succession to a people other than you, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed my Lord is, over all things, Guardian."[1]

footnotes.text: Protecting and preserving the existence and attributes of His creations.

11:66.annotated: So when Our command came, We saved Ṣāliḥ and those who believed with him, by mercy from Us, and [saved them] from the disgrace of that day.[1] Indeed, it is your Lord who is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.

footnotes.text: The day of Thamūd's destruction.

11:67.annotated: And the shriek[1] seized those who had wronged, and they became within their homes [corpses] fallen prone

footnotes.text: A piercing cry or blast from the sky.

11:70.annotated: But when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he distrusted them and felt from them apprehension.[1] They said, "Fear not. We have been sent to the people of Lot."

footnotes.text: Traditionally, if a guest refused to eat, it meant that he harbored ill will toward the host or intended him harm.

11:71.annotated: And his wife was standing, and she smiled.[1] Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob.

footnotes.text: In pleasure at the news of the forthcoming punishment of the evil people who denied Prophet Lot (upon him be peace).

11:72.annotated: She said, "Woe to me![1] Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!"

footnotes.text: An expression of surprise and amazement.

11:74.annotated: And when the fright had left Abraham and the good tidings had reached him, he began to argue [i.e., plead] with Us[1] concerning the people of Lot.

footnotes.text: i.e., with Our angels.

11:75.annotated: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving[1] and [frequently] returning [to Allāh].

footnotes.text: i.e., sighing or moaning during supplication out of grief for people and fear of Allāh.

11:77.annotated: And when Our messengers, [the angels], came to Lot, he was anguished for them and felt for them great discomfort[1] and said, "This is a trying day."

footnotes.text: Prophet Lot feared for the safety and honor of his guests.

11:78.annotated: And his people came hastening to him, and before [this] they had been doing evil deeds.[1] He said, "O my people, these are my daughters;[2] they are purer for you. So fear Allāh and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a man of reason?"

footnotes.text: Referring to their practice of sodomy and homosexual rape of males.
i.e., the women of his community who were available for marriage.

11:81.annotated: They [the angels] said, "O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [therefore], they will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night[1] and let not any among you look back - except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by that which strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?"

footnotes.text: i.e., sometime before dawn.

11:87.annotated: They said, "O Shuʿayb, does your prayer [i.e., religion] command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning!"[1]

footnotes.text: This is a sarcastic description implying the opposite.

11:88.annotated: He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision from Him...?[1] And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I have forbidden you; I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allāh. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I return.[2]

footnotes.text: The conclusion of the sentence is estimated as "...would it not be my duty to warn you against corruption and disobedience?"
i.e., I turn to Allāh frequently in supplication and repentance.

11:96.annotated: And We did certainly send Moses with Our signs and a clear authority[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., evidences from Allāh.

11:99.annotated: And they were followed in this [world] with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection. And wretched is the gift[1] which is given.

footnotes.text: i.e., the curse which follows them in both worlds.

11:100.annotated: That is from the news of the cities, which We relate to you; of them, some are [still] standing and some are [as] a harvest [mowed down].[1]

footnotes.text: Their structures have been completely destroyed.

11:106.annotated: As for those who were [destined to be] wretched, they will be in the Fire. For them therein is [violent] exhaling and inhaling.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., their sighs and sobs, resembling the bray of a donkey.

11:110.annotated: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement. And if not for a word[1] that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed they are, concerning it [i.e., the Qur’ān], in disquieting doubt.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 10:19.

11:116.annotated: So why were there not[1] among the generations before you those of enduring discrimination forbidding corruption on earth - except a few of those We saved from among them? But those who wronged pursued what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.

footnotes.text: Meaning "If only there had been..."

12:1.annotated: Alif, Lām, Rā.[1] These are the verses of the clear Book.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.

12:2.annotated: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān[1] that you might understand.

footnotes.text: i.e., revealed in the Arabic language.

12:4.annotated: [Of these stories mention] when Joseph said to his father,[1] "O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me."

footnotes.text: The prophet Jacob (upon whom be peace).

12:8.annotated: When they said, "Joseph and his brother[1] are more beloved to our father than we, while we are a clan. Indeed, our father is in clear error.

footnotes.text: Benjamin, who was born of the same mother as Joseph.

12:9.annotated: Kill Joseph or cast him out to [another] land; the countenance [i.e., attention] of your father will [then] be only for you, and you will be after that a righteous people."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., You can repent thereafter.

12:15.annotated: So when they took him [out] and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well...[1] But We inspired to him, "You will surely inform them [someday] about this affair of theirs while they do not perceive [your identity]."

footnotes.text: The conclusion of this sentence is estimated to be "...they tormented him."

12:18.annotated: And they brought upon his shirt false blood.[1] [Jacob] said, "Rather, your souls have enticed you to something, so patience is most fitting. And Allāh is the one sought for help against that which you describe."

footnotes.text: They had stained Joseph's shirt with the blood of a lamb but had forgotten to tear it, thereby arousing their father's suspicion.

12:19.annotated: And there came a company of travelers; then they sent their water drawer, and he let down his bucket. He said, "Good news! Here is a boy." And they concealed him, [taking him] as merchandise;[1] and Allāh was Knowing of what they did.

footnotes.text: To be sold as a slave.

12:21.annotated: And the one from Egypt[1] who bought him said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable. Perhaps he will benefit us, or we will adopt him as a son." And thus, We established Joseph in the land that We might teach him the interpretation of events [i.e., dreams]. And Allāh is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.

footnotes.text: The minister in charge of supplies, whose title was al-ʿAzeez.

12:23.annotated: And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him. She closed the doors and said, "Come, you." He said, "[I seek] the refuge of Allāh. Indeed, he[1] is my master, who has made good my residence. Indeed, wrongdoers will not succeed."

footnotes.text: Her husband, al-ʿAzeez.

12:29.annotated: Joseph, ignore this.[1] And, [my wife], ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful."

footnotes.text: i.e., conceal it and act as if it had not taken place.

12:31.annotated: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet and gave each one of them a knife and said [to Joseph], "Come out before them." And when they saw him, they greatly admired him and cut their hands[1] and said, "Perfect is Allāh![2] This is not a man; this is none but a noble angel."

footnotes.text: So distracted were they at the sight of him.
In His ability to create such beauty.

12:35.annotated: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs[1] that he [i.e., al-ʿAzeez] should surely imprison him for a time.[2]

footnotes.text: Proofs of his innocence.
Until the scandal be forgotten.

12:39.annotated: O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One,[1] the Prevailing?[2]

footnotes.text: Single, individual and unique in His attributes and His deeds.
He who subdues doubts and false arguments with clear evidences and who subdues and imposes His will upon all creation.

12:40.annotated: You worship not besides Him except [mere] names you have named them,[1] you and your fathers, for which Allāh has sent down no evidence. Legislation is not but for Allāh. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

footnotes.text: The false objects of worship which you have called "gods."

12:51.annotated: Said [the king to the women], "What was your condition when you sought to seduce Joseph?" They said, "Perfect is Allāh![1] We know about him no evil." The wife of al-ʿAzeez said, "Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful.

footnotes.text: In His ability to create such purity of character.

12:53.annotated: And I do not acquit myself. Indeed, the soul is a persistent enjoiner of evil, except those upon which my Lord has mercy. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful."[1]

footnotes.text: Although Ibn Katheer attributes the words of verses 52-53 to the wife of al-ʿAzeez, others have concluded that they were spoken by Joseph, thereby justifying his request for an inquiry and acknowledging Allāh's mercy to him.

12:58.annotated: And the brothers of Joseph came [seeking food], and they entered upon him; and he recognized them, but he was to them unknown.[1]

footnotes.text: Due to the change in his appearance over the years.

12:59.annotated: And when he had furnished them with their supplies, he said, "Bring me a brother of yours from your father.[1] Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of accommodators?

footnotes.text: i.e., Benjamin, who had been kept at home by his father Jacob.

12:62.annotated: And [Joseph] said to his servants, "Put their merchandise[1] into their saddlebags so they might recognize it when they have gone back to their people that perhaps they will [again] return."

footnotes.text: The goods which they had brought to trade for food supplies.

12:65.annotated: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what [more] could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. And we will obtain supplies [i.e., food] for our family and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."[1]

footnotes.text: For them.  Or one obtained by us with ease.

12:66.annotated: [Jacob] said, "Never will I send him with you until you give me a promise [i.e., oath] by Allāh that you will bring him [back] to me, unless you should be surrounded [i.e., overcome by enemies]." And when they had given their promise, he said, "Allāh, over what we say, is Entrusted."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., sufficient to witness and deal with the matter.

12:74.annotated: They [the accusers] said, "Then what would be its recompense[1] if you should be liars?"

footnotes.text: The punishment for theft.

12:75.annotated: [The brothers] said, "Its recompense is that he in whose bag it is found - he [himself] will be its recompense.[1] Thus do we recompense the wrongdoers."

footnotes.text: According to their law, a convicted thief was made a slave of the one from whom he had stolen.

12:76.annotated: So he began [the search] with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the religion [i.e., law] of the king except that Allāh willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, but over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.[1]

footnotes.text: Ending with the ultimate knowledge of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

12:77.annotated: They said, "If he steals - a brother of his has stolen before." But Joseph kept it within himself and did not reveal it to them.[1] He said, "You are worse in position, and Allāh is most knowing of what you describe."

footnotes.text: He did not answer that he himself had been stolen by them from his father.

12:78.annotated: They said, "O ʿAzeez,[1] indeed he has a father [who is] an old man, so take one of us in place of him. Indeed, we see you as a doer of good."

footnotes.text: Addressing Joseph, who now held the title of "al-ʿAzeez."

12:80.annotated: So when they had despaired of him, they secluded themselves in private consultation. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken upon you an oath by Allāh and [that] before you failed in [your duty to] Joseph? So I will never leave [this] land until my father permits me or Allāh decides for me,[1] and He is the best of judges.

footnotes.text: i.e., in my favor by bringing about the release of Benjamin.

12:81.annotated: Return to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not witnesses of the unseen.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., We could not have known when we gave you the oath that he would steal and be apprehended.

12:84.annotated: And he turned away from them and said, "Oh, my sorrow over Joseph," and his eyes became white[1] from grief, for he was [of that] a suppressor.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., he lost his sight.
He did not express the extent of his grief or his anger at what he suspected his sons had done but was patient, depending only upon Allāh for help.

12:94.annotated: And when the caravan departed [from Egypt], their father said,[1] "Indeed, I find the smell of Joseph [and would say that he was alive] if you did not think me weakened in mind."

footnotes.text: To those present with him, either some of his sons or other relatives.

12:96.annotated: And when the bearer of good tidings[1] arrived, he cast it over his face, and he returned [once again] seeing. He said, "Did I not tell you that I know from Allāh that which you do not know?"

footnotes.text: He who carried Joseph's shirt from among the brothers.

12:100.annotated: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration.[1] And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle[2] in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise.

footnotes.text: That of greeting and respect, which was lawful until the time of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).  Prostration to any person or object other than Allāh was then prohibited conclusively.
Perceptive of unapparent matters within which is benefit to His servants.

12:109.annotated: And We sent not before you [as messengers] except men to whom We revealed from among the people of cities. So have they[1] not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? And the home of the Hereafter is best for those who fear Allāh; then will you not reason?

footnotes.text: Those who deny Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).

13:1.annotated: Alif, Lām, Meem, Rā.[1] These are the verses of the Book; and what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.

13:2.annotated: It is Allāh who erected the heavens without pillars that you [can] see; then He established Himself above the Throne[1] and made subject[2] the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you may, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain.

footnotes.text: See footnotes to 2:19 and 7:54.
For the benefit of mankind.

13:4.annotated: And within the land are neighboring plots and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, [growing] several from a root or otherwise,[1] watered with one water; but We make some of them exceed others in [quality of] fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.

footnotes.text: i.e., only one from a root.

13:5.annotated: And if you are astonished,[1] [O Muḥammad] - then astonishing is their saying, "When we are dust, will we indeed be [brought] into a new creation?" Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles[2] upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.

footnotes.text: At those who deny resurrection.
Iron collars to which their hands are chained.

13:6.annotated: They impatiently urge you to bring about evil before good,[1] while there has already occurred before them similar punishments [to what they demand]. And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.

footnotes.text: They said, challenging the Prophet (ﷺ) in ridicule, "Bring on the punishment, if you are truthful," rather than asking for mercy and forgiveness from Allāh.

13:8.annotated: Allāh knows what every female carries[1] and what the wombs lose [prematurely] or exceed.[2] And everything with Him is by due measure.

footnotes.text: With absolute knowledge inclusive of every aspect of the fetus' existence.
Beyond their normal period of pregnancy and/or the number of fetuses therein.

13:11.annotated: For him [i.e., each one] are successive [angels][1] before and behind him who protect him by the decree of Allāh.[2] Indeed, Allāh will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allāh intends for a people ill,[3] there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any patron.

footnotes.text: Replacing each other by turn.
The phrase may also be rendered "...who guard him from [everything except] the decree of Allāh."
i.e., punishment or destruction because of their sins.

13:14.annotated: To Him [alone] is the supplication of truth. And those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them with a thing, except as one who stretches his hands toward water [from afar, calling it] to reach his mouth, but it will not reach it [thus].[1] And the supplication of the disbelievers is not but in error [i.e., futility].

footnotes.text: The analogy indicates that false deities will never respond to them at all.

13:16.annotated: Say, "Who is Lord of the heavens and earth?" Say, "Allāh." Say, "Have you then taken besides Him allies not possessing [even] for themselves any benefit or any harm?" Say, "Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allāh partners who created like His creation so that the creation [of each] seemed similar to them?"[1] Say, "Allāh is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing."[2]

footnotes.text: The obvious conclusion is that the claimed partners, having no ability to create, cannot be compared to Allāh in any way.
Refer to footnotes in 12:39.

13:21.annotated: And those who join that which Allāh has ordered to be joined[1] and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of [their] account,

footnotes.text: i.e., they uphold the ties of relationship.

13:22.annotated: And those who are patient, seeking the face [i.e., acceptance] of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly and prevent evil with good - those will have the good consequence of [this] home[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the world and its trials, its good consequence being Paradise.

13:25.annotated: But those who break the covenant of Allāh after contracting it and sever that which Allāh has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth - for them is the curse, and they will have the worst home.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., Hell.  Another meaning is (in contrast to verse 22), "...and they will have the bad consequence of [this] home," also referring to Hell.

13:31.annotated: And if there was any Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] by which the mountains would be removed or the earth would be broken apart or the dead would be made to speak,[1] [it would be this Qur’ān], but to Allāh belongs the affair entirely. Then have those who believed not accepted that had Allāh willed, He would have guided the people, all of them? And those who disbelieve do not cease to be struck, for what they have done, by calamity - or it will descend near their home - until there comes the promise of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh does not fail in [His] promise.

footnotes.text: As suggested by the disbelievers.

13:33.annotated: Then is He who is a maintainer of every soul, [knowing] what it has earned, [like any other]? But to Allāh they have attributed partners. Say, "Name them. Or do you inform Him of that[1] which He knows not upon the earth or of what is apparent [i.e., alleged] of speech?"[2] Rather, their [own] plan has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they have been averted from the way. And whomever Allāh sends astray - there will be for him no guide.

footnotes.text: i.e., other "deities."
i.e., your attributing of divinity to other than Allāh.

13:37.annotated: And thus We have revealed it as an Arabic legislation.[1] And if you should follow their inclinations after what has come to you of knowledge, you would not have against Allāh any ally or any protector.

footnotes.text: i.e., revealed in the Arabic language.

13:39.annotated: Allāh eliminates what He wills or confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.[1]

footnotes.text: The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), in which is inscribed the original of every scripture revealed by Allāh.

13:41.annotated: Have they not seen that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders?[1] And Allāh decides; there is no adjuster of His decision. And He is swift in account.

footnotes.text: Referring to the spread of Islām through Allāh's Prophet (ﷺ) and the diminishing of those areas controlled by the polytheists.

13:43.annotated: And those who have disbelieved say, "You are not a messenger." Say, [O Muḥammad], "Sufficient is Allāh as Witness between me and you, and [the witness of] whoever has knowledge of the Scripture."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those who recognize the truth through their knowledge of previous scriptures.

14:1.annotated: Alif, Lām, Rā.[1] [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy -

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.

14:4.annotated: And We did not send any messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to state clearly for them, and Allāh sends astray [thereby] whom He wills[1] and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

footnotes.text: i.e., those who refuse His guidance.

14:5.annotated: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs, [saying], "Bring out your people from darknesses into the light and remind them of the days[1] of Allāh." Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.

footnotes.text: Days of blessings bestowed upon the Children of Israel.  Also interpreted as days of punishment and destruction of the former nations.

14:9.annotated: Has there not reached you the news of those before you - the people of Noah and ʿAad and Thamūd and those after them? No one knows them [i.e., their number] but Allāh. Their messengers brought them clear proofs, but they returned their hands to their mouths[1] and said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are, about that to which you invite us, in disquieting doubt."

footnotes.text: Several explanations have been given as to the meaning.  Based upon the conclusion of the verse, Ibn Katheer preferred that this was a gesture of denial and rejection.

14:14.annotated: And We will surely cause you to dwell in the land after them. That is for he who fears My position[1] and fears My threat."

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "the standing [for account] before Me."

14:16.annotated: Before him[1] is Hell, and he will be given a drink of purulent water.[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "after him [in time]," meaning ahead of him.
That which oozes from the skins of Hell's inhabitants.

14:22.annotated: And Satan will say when the matter has been concluded, "Indeed, Allāh had promised you the promise of truth. And I promised you, but I betrayed you. But I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me; but blame yourselves. I cannot be called to your aid, nor can you be called to my aid. Indeed, I deny your association of me [with Allāh] before.[1] Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment."

footnotes.text: By your obedience to me instead of Him during life on earth.

14:27.annotated: Allāh keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word,[1] in worldly life and in the Hereafter.[2] And Allāh sends astray the wrongdoers. And Allāh does what He wills.

footnotes.text: The testimony that there is no deity except Allāh and that Muḥammad (ﷺ) is the messenger of Allāh.
When questioned in their graves by the angels after death.

14:28.annotated: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of Allāh for disbelief[1] and settled their people [in] the home of ruin?

footnotes.text: They met Allāh's blessing with denial instead of gratitude.

14:32.annotated: It is Allāh who created the heavens and the earth and sent down rain from the sky and produced thereby some fruits as provision for you and subjected for you[1] the ships to sail through the sea by His command and subjected for you the rivers.

footnotes.text: i.e., made serviceable to you.

14:34.annotated: And He gave you from all you asked of Him.[1] And if you should count the favor [i.e., blessings] of Allāh, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, mankind is [generally] most unjust and ungrateful.[2]

footnotes.text: Something of what you asked and all of what you continually require, according to His wisdom.
i.e., disbelieving and denying of Allāh's favor.

14:36.annotated: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many among the people. So whoever follows me - then he is of me;[1] and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are [yet] Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: i.e., of my religion.

14:43.annotated: Racing ahead, their heads raised up, their glance does not come back to them,[1] and their hearts are void.

footnotes.text: This is their state at the time of resurrection from the graves.  Their heads are upraised in fixed stares of terror, unable even to glance back.

14:44.annotated: And, [O Muḥammad], warn the people of a Day when the punishment will come to them and those who did wrong will say, "Our Lord, delay us for a short term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers." [But it will be said], "Had you not sworn, before, that for you there would be no cessation?[1]

footnotes.text: Of the blessings which Allāh had bestowed upon you during life on earth.

14:46.annotated: And they had planned their plan, but with Allāh is [recorded] their plan, even if their plan had been [sufficient] to do away with the mountains.[1]

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "...and their plan was not [sufficient] to do away with the mountains," i.e., it had no effect against Allāh's will.

14:47.annotated: So never think that Allāh will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allāh is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote for 3:(5)

15:1.annotated: Alif, Lām, Rā.[1] These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur’ān [i.e., recitation].

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.

15:2.annotated: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish[1] that they had been Muslims.

footnotes.text: On the Day of Judgement or at the time of death.

15:6.annotated: And they say, "O you upon whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "possessed by jinn."

15:8.annotated: We do not send down the angels except with truth;[1] and they [i.e., the disbelievers] would not then be reprieved.

footnotes.text: i.e., with a message or, as the conclusion of the verse suggests, to carry out a promised punishment.

15:20.annotated: And We have made for you therein means of living and [for] those for whom you are not providers.[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh has put at your service other men and animals for which He provides.  An additional meaning is that Allāh provides means for your living and for all other creatures as well.

15:22.annotated: And We have sent the fertilizing winds[1] and sent down water from the sky and given you drink from it. And you are not its retainers.

footnotes.text: Causing precipitation in rainclouds or carrying pollen.  Another meaning is "pregnant winds," i.e., those carrying rainclouds.

15:23.annotated: And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) remains after all creation has passed away.

15:29.annotated: And when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul,[1] then fall down to him in prostration."

footnotes.text: The element of life and soul which Allāh created for that body, not His own spirit or part of Himself (as some mistakenly believe).

15:31.annotated: Except Iblees;[1] he refused to be with those who prostrated.

footnotes.text: Who was of the jinn.  See 18:50.

15:34.annotated: [Allāh] said, "Then depart from it,[1] for indeed, you are expelled.

footnotes.text: Your position in the heavens.

15:47.annotated: And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment,[1] [so they will be] brothers, on thrones facing each other.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 7:43.

15:60.annotated: Except his wife." We [i.e., Allāh] decreed that she is of those who remain behind.[1]

footnotes.text: For having collaborated with the evildoers.

15:67.annotated: And the people of the city came rejoicing.[1]

footnotes.text: At the news of Lot's visitors.

15:71.annotated: [Lot] said, "These are my daughters[1] - if you would be doers [of lawful marriage]."

footnotes.text: i.e., the women of his community who were lawful for marriage.

15:73.annotated: So the shriek[1] seized them at sunrise.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 11:67.

15:80.annotated: And certainly did the companions of al-Ḥijr[1] [i.e., the Thamūd] deny the messengers.

footnotes.text: The valley of stone.

15:87.annotated: And We have certainly given you, [O Muḥammad], seven of the often repeated [verses][1] and the great Qur’ān.

footnotes.text: Referring to Sūrah al-Fātiḥah.

15:90.annotated: Just as We had revealed [scriptures] to the separators[1]

footnotes.text: Those who separated from the teachings of their prophets.  Another meaning is "As We sent down [punishment] on the sworn opponents [to Allāh's message]."

15:91.annotated: Who have made the Qur’ān into portions.[1]

footnotes.text: Accepting part and rejecting part according to their own inclinations.

15:94.annotated: Then declare what you are commanded[1] and turn away from the polytheists.[2]

footnotes.text: The implication is "Thereby you will distinguish or separate the disbelievers from the believers."
Any who persist in association of others with Allāh.

16:1.annotated: The command of Allāh is coming,[1] so be not impatient for it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.

footnotes.text: Literally, "has come," indicating the certainty and nearness of the Last Hour.

16:4.annotated: He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once[1] he is a clear adversary.

footnotes.text: As soon as he becomes strong and independent.

16:5.annotated: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth[1] and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat.

footnotes.text: i.e., in clothing, tents, furnishings, etc.

16:9.annotated: And upon Allāh[1] is the direction of the [right] way, and among them [i.e., the various paths] are those deviating. And if He willed, He could have guided you all.

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) has taken it upon Himself to guide man to the right path.  The meaning has also been interpreted as "To Allāh..."

16:16.annotated: And landmarks. And by the stars they are [also] guided.[1]

footnotes.text: Through the desert or the sea at night.

16:21.annotated: They are [in fact] dead,[1] not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.

footnotes.text: i.e., inanimate or without understanding.

16:26.annotated: Those before them had already plotted, but Allāh came at [i.e., uprooted] their building from the foundations, so the roof fell upon them from above them,[1] and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.

footnotes.text: i.e., Allāh caused their plan to fail and exposed their plot.

16:28.annotated: The ones whom the angels take in death [while] wronging themselves,[1] and [who] then offer submission, [saying], "We were not doing any evil." But, yes! Indeed, Allāh is Knowing of what you used to do.

footnotes.text: i.e., having made punishment due to them for their numerous sins and crimes.

16:36.annotated: And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allāh and avoid ṭāghūt."[1] And among them were those whom Allāh guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So proceed [i.e., travel] through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.

footnotes.text: False objects of worship.

16:37.annotated: [Even] if you should strive for their guidance, [O Muḥammad], indeed, Allāh does not guide those He sends astray,[1] and they will have no helpers.

footnotes.text: As a result of their choice to reject guidance.

16:47.annotated: Or that He would not seize them gradually [in a state of dread]?[1] But indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., being aware of what is about to strike them after having seen those near them succumb.
Postponing deserved punishment and giving opportunities for repentance.

16:51.annotated: And Allāh has said, "Do not take for yourselves two[1] deities. He [i.e., Allāh] is but one God, so fear only Me."

footnotes.text: Meaning more than one.

16:56.annotated: And they assign to what they do not know[1] [i.e., false deities] a portion of that which We have provided them. By Allāh, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.

footnotes.text: i.e., that of which they have no knowledge; rather, they have mere assumption based upon tradition or the claims of misguided men.

16:57.annotated: And they attribute to Allāh daughters[1] - exalted is He - and for them is what they desire [i.e., sons].

footnotes.text: By claiming that the angels are His daughters.

16:60.annotated: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the description [i.e., an attribute] of evil;[1] and for Allāh is the highest attribute. And He is Exalted in Might, the Wise.

footnotes.text: Such as that described in the previous two verses.

16:62.annotated: And they attribute to Allāh that which they dislike [i.e., daughters], and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best [from Him]. Assuredly, they will have the Fire, and they will be [therein] neglected.[1]

footnotes.text: Another meaning is "...and they will be made to precede [all others thereto]."

16:67.annotated: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision.[1] Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.

footnotes.text: This verse was revealed before the prohibition of intoxicants.  It alludes to the fact that there are both evil and good possibilities in certain things.

16:69.annotated: Then eat from all the fruits[1] and follow the ways of your Lord laid down [for you]." There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.

footnotes.text: i.e., delicious substances found by the bee.

16:71.annotated: And Allāh has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored [i.e., given more] would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess [i.e., slaves] so they would be equal to them therein.[1] Then is it the favor of Allāh they reject?

footnotes.text: The argument presented in this verse is that if they cannot consider their own possessions equal to themselves, then how can they consider Allāh's creations as being equal to Him?

16:74.annotated: So do not assert similarities to Allāh.[1] Indeed, Allāh knows and you do not know.

footnotes.text: As there is nothing comparable to Him.

16:89.annotated: And [mention] the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness over them from themselves [i.e., their prophet]. And We will bring you, [O Muḥammad], as a witness over these [i.e., your nation]. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.[1]

footnotes.text: Those who have submitted themselves to Allāh.

16:92.annotated: And do not be like she who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong [by] taking your oaths as [means of] deceit between you because one community is more plentiful [in number or wealth] than another community.[1] Allāh only tries you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.

footnotes.text: i.e., do not swear falsely or break a treaty or contract merely for a worldly advantage.

16:93.annotated: And if Allāh had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.[1] And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.

footnotes.text: According to His knowledge of each soul's preference.

16:94.annotated: And do not take your oaths as [means of] deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was [once] firm, and you would taste evil [in this world] for what [people] you diverted from the way of Allāh,[1] and you would have [in the Hereafter] a great punishment.

footnotes.text: Referring to those who would be dissuaded from Islām as a result of a Muslim's deceit and treachery.

16:103.annotated: And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)]." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign,[1] and this [recitation, i.e., Qur’ān] is [in] a clear Arabic language.

footnotes.text: Having seen the Prophet (ﷺ) speaking with a foreign man on occasion, the Quraysh accused him of repeating the man's words.

16:106.annotated: Whoever disbelieves in [i.e., denies] Allāh after his belief...[1] except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith. But those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from Allāh, and for them is a great punishment;

footnotes.text: Based upon the conclusion of this verse, the omitted phrase concerning the apostate is understood to be "...has earned the wrath of Allāh..."

16:115.annotated: He has only forbidden to you dead animals,[1] blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allāh. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit] - then indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: Those not slaughtered or hunted expressly for food.

16:118.annotated: And to those who are Jews We have prohibited that which We related to you before.[1] And We did not wrong them [thereby], but they were wronging themselves.

16:120.annotated: Indeed, Abraham was a [comprehensive] leader,[1] devoutly obedient to Allāh, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allāh.

footnotes.text: i.e., embodying all the excellent qualities which make one an example to be followed.

16:126.annotated: And if you punish [an enemy, O believers], punish with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed.[1] But if you are patient - it is better for those who are patient.

footnotes.text: Not exceeding it.

17:1.annotated: Exalted[1] is He who took His Servant [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)] by night from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām to al-Masjid al-Aqṣā,[2] whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing,[3] the Seeing.[4]

footnotes.text: Above any imperfection or failure to do as He wills.
In Jerusalem.
Who hears every sound, distinguishes every voice, understands every word, and accepts and responds to supplications.
After Seeing add ftnt:  Who sees and understands all things apparent and unapparent, visible and invisible.

17:2.annotated: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel that you not take other than Me as Disposer of affairs,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., trust in Allāh, knowing that He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) is responsible for every occurrence.

17:4.annotated: And We conveyed[1] to the Children of Israel in the Scripture that, "You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach [a degree of] great haughtiness."

footnotes.text: Foretold out of divine knowledge of what they would do.

17:5.annotated: So when the [time of] promise came for the first of them,[1] We sent against you servants of Ours - those of great military might, and they probed [even] into the homes,[2] and it was a promise fulfilled.

footnotes.text: i.e., the promised punishment for the first of their two transgressions.
Violating their sanctity, to kill and plunder.

17:11.annotated: And man supplicates for evil [when angry] as he supplicates for good, and man is ever hasty.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., impatient, emotional, and acting without forethought.

17:12.annotated: And We have made the night and day two signs, and We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible[1] that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account [of time]. And everything We have set out in detail.

footnotes.text: Or "giving sight."

17:13.annotated: And [for] every person We have imposed his fate upon his neck,[1] and We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will encounter spread open.

footnotes.text: i.e., after having instructed him, We have made him responsible for his own destiny.

17:16.annotated: And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent[1] but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word [i.e., deserved decree] comes into effect upon it, and We destroy it with [complete] destruction.

footnotes.text: To obey Allāh.

17:18.annotated: Whoever should desire the immediate[1] - We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will [enter to] burn, censured and banished.

footnotes.text: i.e., worldly gratifications.

17:23.annotated: And your Lord has decreed that you worship not except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age [while] with you, say not to them [so much as], "uff,"[1] and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word.

footnotes.text: An expression of disapproval or irritation.

17:25.annotated: Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves. If you should be righteous [in intention] - then indeed He is ever, to the often returning [to Him], Forgiving.[1]

footnotes.text: For those who intend righteousness, hastening to repent from sins and errors committed through human weakness, Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) promises forgiveness.

17:26.annotated: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., on that which is unlawful or in disobedience to Allāh.

17:28.annotated: And if you [must] turn away from them [i.e., the needy] awaiting mercy from your Lord which you expect,[1] then speak to them a gentle word.

footnotes.text: i.e., if you have not the means to give them at present.

17:29.annotated: And do not make your hand [as] chained to your neck[1] or extend it completely[2] and [thereby] become blamed and insolvent.

footnotes.text: i.e., refusing to spend.
i.e., being extravagant.

17:32.annotated: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse.[1] Indeed, it is ever an immorality and is evil as a way.

footnotes.text: i.e., avoid all situations that might possibly lead to it.

17:33.annotated: And do not kill the soul [i.e., person] which Allāh has forbidden, except by right.[1] And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority,[2] but let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life. Indeed, he has been supported [by the law].

footnotes.text: i.e., through legal justice or during jihād.
Grounds for legal action.

17:34.annotated: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in the way that is best,[1] until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.

footnotes.text: i.e., to improve or increase it.

17:36.annotated: And do not pursue[1] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

footnotes.text: i.e., do not assume and do not say.

17:37.annotated: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height.[1]

footnotes.text: Man, for all his arrogance, is yet a weak and small creature.

17:42.annotated: Say, [O Muḥammad], "If there had been with Him [other] gods, as they say, then they [each] would have sought to the Owner of the Throne a way."[1]

footnotes.text: To please Him, recognizing His superiority.  Another interpretation is "...they would seek a way" to depose Him (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) and take over His Throne.

17:44.annotated: The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them exalt Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allāh] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing[1] and Forgiving.

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote in 2:225.

17:45.annotated: And when you recite the Qur’ān, We put between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed partition.[1]

footnotes.text: Preventing guidance from reaching them.

17:48.annotated: Look how they strike for you comparisons;[1] but they have strayed, so they cannot [find] a way.

footnotes.text: Describing the Prophet (ﷺ) as a poet, a madman or one under the influence of sorcery.
i.e., even if you should be stones or iron.

17:51.annotated: Or [any] creation of that which is great[1] within your breasts." And they will say, "Who will restore us?" Say, "He who brought you forth the first time." Then they will nod their heads toward you[2] and say, "When is that?" Say, "Perhaps it will be soon -

footnotes.text: Such as the heavens and earth.
In disbelief and ridicule.

17:57.annotated: Those whom they invoke[1] seek means of access to their Lord, [striving as to] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared.

footnotes.text: Among the righteous of Allāh's creation, such as angels, prophets, deceased scholars, etc.

17:58.annotated: And there is no city but that We will destroy it[1] before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That has ever been in the Register[2] inscribed.

footnotes.text: Because of the sins of its inhabitants.
The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), which is with Allāh.

17:60.annotated: And [remember, O Muḥammad], when We told you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people."[1] And We did not make the sight which We showed you[2] except as a trial for the people, as was the accursed tree [mentioned] in the Qur’ān. And We threaten [i.e., warn] them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.

footnotes.text: In His knowledge and power, meaning that Allāh would protect him (ﷺ) from their harm.
During the miʿrāj (ascension) into the heavens.

17:61.annotated: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblees.[1] He said, "Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?"

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:34.

17:62.annotated: [Iblees] said, "Do You see this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me [i.e., my death] until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy[1] his descendants, except for a few."

footnotes.text: By tempting them and leading them astray.

17:65.annotated: Indeed, over My [believing] servants there is for you no authority. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote in 3: 173.

17:69.annotated: Or do you feel secure that He will not send you back into it [i.e., the sea] another time and send upon you a hurricane of wind and drown you for what you denied?[1] Then you would not find for yourselves against Us an avenger.[2]

footnotes.text: Or "for your disbelief."
Or "someone to demand restitution."

17:71.annotated: [Mention, O Muḥammad], the Day We will call forth every people with their record [of deeds].[1] Then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and injustice will not be done to them, [even] as much as a thread [inside the date seed].

footnotes.text: Other meanings are "with their leader" or "with that which they had followed."

17:72.annotated: And whoever is blind[1] in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.

footnotes.text: i.e., refusing to see the truth.

17:76.annotated: And indeed, they were about to provoke [i.e., drive] you from the land [i.e., Makkah] to evict you therefrom. And then [when they do], they will not remain [there] after you, except for a little.[1]

footnotes.text: Only ten years after the Prophet's emigration, Makkah was completely cleared of his enemies.

17:78.annotated: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun [from its meridian] until the darkness of the night[1] and [also] the Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] of dawn.[2] Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.

footnotes.text: i.e., the period which includes the ẓuhr, aṣr, maghrib, and ʿishā’ prayers.
i.e., the fajr prayer, in which the recitation of the Qur’ān is prolonged.

17:79.annotated: And from [part of] the night, pray[1] with it [i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān] as additional [worship] for you; it is expected that[2] your Lord will resurrect you to a praised station.[3]

footnotes.text: Literally, "arise from sleep for prayer."
This is a promise from Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) to Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).
The position of intercession by permission of Allāh and the highest degree in Paradise.

17:80.annotated: And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance[1] and to exit a sound exit[2] and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."

footnotes.text: Into Madīnah at the time of emigration, or into the grave.
From Makkah, or from the grave at the time of resurrection.

17:95.annotated: Say, "If there were upon the earth angels walking securely,[1] We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel [as a] messenger."

footnotes.text: i.e., who were settled and established there, as is man.

17:97.annotated: And whoever Allāh guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whoever He sends astray[1] - you will never find for them protectors besides Him, and We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection [fallen] on their faces - blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; every time it subsides, We increase [for] them blazing fire.

footnotes.text: As a result of his own preference.

17:102.annotated: [Moses] said, "You have already known that none has sent down these [signs] except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence, and indeed I think,[1] O Pharaoh, that you are destroyed."

footnotes.text: i.e., I am certain.

17:107.annotated: Say, "Believe in it or do not believe." Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it[1] - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration,

footnotes.text: i.e., the righteous among the People of the Scriptures who recognize the truth contained in the Qur’ān.

18:1.annotated: [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, who has sent down upon His Servant [Muḥammad (ﷺ)] the Book and has not made therein any deviance.[1]

footnotes.text: From the truth or the straight path.

18:5.annotated: They have no knowledge of it,[1] nor had their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths; they speak not except a lie.

footnotes.text: i.e., they could not have had knowledge of something which is not true.

18:9.annotated: Or have you thought that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder?[1]

footnotes.text: Rather, it is only one of the many wonders of Allāh.

18:19.annotated: And similarly,[1] We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker from among them, "How long have you remained [here]?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you.

footnotes.text: By the will of Allāh.

18:21.annotated: And similarly, We caused them to be found that they [who found them] would know that the promise of Allāh is truth and that of the Hour there is no doubt. [That was] when they[1] disputed among themselves about their affair and [then] said, "Construct over them a structure. Their Lord is most knowing about them." Said those who prevailed in the matter, "We will surely take [for ourselves] over them a masjid."[2]

footnotes.text: The people of the city.
i.e., we will make this site a place of worship.

18:22.annotated: They [i.e., people] will say there were three, the fourth of them being their dog; and they will say there were five, the sixth of them being their dog - guessing at the unseen; and they will say there were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. Say, [O Muḥammad], "My Lord is most knowing of their number. None knows them except a few. So do not argue about them except with an obvious argument[1] and do not inquire about them among [the speculators] from anyone."

footnotes.text: i.e., one from the Qur’ān, which is the only sure argument.

18:25.annotated: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and exceeded by nine.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., 309 lunar years.

18:28.annotated: And keep yourself patient [by being] with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His face [i.e., acceptance]. And let not your eyes pass beyond them, desiring adornments of the worldly life, and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance and who follows his desire and whose affair is ever [in] neglect.[1]

footnotes.text: Or "in excess," exceeding the limits of Allāh.

18:35.annotated: And he entered his garden while he was unjust to himself.[1] He said, "I do not think that this will perish - ever.

footnotes.text: i.e., proud and ungrateful to Allāh.

18:42.annotated: And his fruits were encompassed [by ruin], so he began to turn his hands about [in dismay] over what he had spent on it, while it had collapsed upon its trellises, and said, "Oh, I wish I had not associated with my Lord anyone."[1]

footnotes.text: He attributed his prosperity to himself rather than to Allāh and disbelieved in the account of the Hereafter.

18:44.annotated: There[1] the authority is [completely] for Allāh, the Truth. He is best in reward and best in outcome.

footnotes.text: i.e., at such a time or on the Day of Judgement.

18:45.annotated: And present to them the example of the life of this world, [its being] like rain which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it[1] and [then] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allāh is ever, over all things, Perfect in Ability.

footnotes.text: Absorbs it, growing lush and thick.

18:46.annotated: Wealth and children are [but] adornment of the worldly life. But the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord[1] for reward and better for [one's] hope.

footnotes.text: i.e., in His sight or evaluation.

18:47.annotated: And [warn of] the Day when We will remove the mountains and you will see the earth exposed,[1] and We will gather them and not leave behind from them anyone.

footnotes.text: i.e., flattened and bare.

18:55.annotated: And nothing has prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them and from asking forgiveness of their Lord except that there [must] befall them the [accustomed] precedent of the former peoples[1] or that the punishment should come [directly] before them.

footnotes.text: Who denied the truth brought by Allāh's messengers.

18:86.annotated: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun [i.e., the west], he found it [as if] setting in a body of dark water,[1] and he found near it a people. We [i.e., Allāh] said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish [them] or else adopt among them [a way of] goodness."

footnotes.text: Another meaning is "a body of hot water."

18:87.annotated: He said, "As for one who wrongs,[1] we will punish him. Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment [i.e., Hellfire].

footnotes.text: Persists in disbelief and rebellion.

18:91.annotated: Thus.[1] And We had encompassed [all] that he had in knowledge.

footnotes.text: Such was the affair of Dhul-Qarnayn.

18:94.annotated: They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog[1] are [great] corrupters in the land. So may we assign for you an expenditure that you might make between us and them a barrier?"

footnotes.text: Savage tribes who had ravaged large parts of central Asia, committing every kind of atrocity.

18:98.annotated: [Dhul-Qarnayn] said, "This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord[1] comes [i.e., approaches], He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true."

footnotes.text: i.e., the Hour of Resurrection.

18:99.annotated: And We will leave them that day[1] surging over each other, and [then] the Horn will be blown, and We will assemble them in [one] assembly.

footnotes.text: The day the dam is destroyed.

18:101.annotated: Those whose eyes had been within a cover [removed] from My remembrance,[1] and they were not able to hear.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., Allāh's signs or the Qur’ān.
They refused to listen to the Qur’ān or to understand it.

18:107.annotated: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they will have the Gardens of Paradise[1] as a lodging,

footnotes.text: i.e., the highest part of Paradise, al-Firdaus.

18:109.annotated: Say, "If the sea were ink for [writing] the words[1] of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it in [continual] supplement."

footnotes.text: The words of Allāh's unlimited knowledge or words describing His attributes and His grandeur or praise of Him (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).
See footnote to 2:1

19:4.annotated: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled[1] with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy [i.e., disappointed].

footnotes.text: Literally, "ignited."  The spread of white hair throughout the head is likened to that of fire in the bush.

19:5.annotated: And indeed, I fear the successors[1] after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir

footnotes.text: Those relatives from the father's side who would inherit religious authority.

19:6.annotated: Who will inherit me[1] and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You]."

footnotes.text: Inherit from me religious knowledge and prophethood.

19:7.annotated: [He was told],[1] "O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any before [this] name."

footnotes.text: By Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) through the angels.

19:10.annotated: [Zechariah] said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., without illness or defect.

19:24.annotated: But he[1] called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.

footnotes.text: There is a difference of opinion among scholars as to whether "he" refers to the baby or to the angel.

19:35.annotated: It is not [befitting] for Allāh to take a son; exalted is He![1] When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

footnotes.text: i.e., far removed is He from any such need.

19:39.annotated: And warn them, [O Muḥammad], of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be concluded;[1] and [yet], they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe.

footnotes.text: i.e., "judged" or "accomplished."

19:47.annotated: [Abraham] said, "Peace [i.e., safety] will be upon you.[1] I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.

footnotes.text: Meaning "You are secure" or "I will not harm you."

19:48.annotated: And I will leave you and those you invoke other than Allāh and will invoke[1] my Lord. I expect that I will not be in invocation to my Lord unhappy [i.e., disappointed]."

footnotes.text: i.e., worship.

19:51.annotated: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.[1]

footnotes.text: A messenger (rasūl) is one who was charged by Allāh to reform society.  A prophet (nabī) is one who received revelation from Allāh, the latter being more numerous than the former.

19:52.annotated: And We called him from the side of the mount[1] at [his] right and brought him near, confiding [to him].

footnotes.text: Mount Sinai.

19:59.annotated: But there came after them successors [i.e., later generations] who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil[1] -

footnotes.text: Described as a valley in Hell or may be rendered "the consequence of error."

19:61.annotated: [Therein are] gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been eminent.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "that to which all will come."

19:64.annotated: [Gabriel said],[1] "And we [angels] descend not except by the order of your Lord. To Him belongs that before us and that behind us and what is in between. And never is your Lord forgetful -

footnotes.text: In answer to the Prophet's wish that Gabriel would visit him more often.

19:68.annotated: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell upon their knees.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., fallen on their knees from terror or dragged there unwillingly on their knees.

19:71.annotated: And there is none of you except he will come to it.[1] This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.

footnotes.text: i.e., be exposed to it.  However, the people of Paradise will not be harmed thereby.

19:73.annotated: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of [our] two parties is best in position and best in association?"[1]

footnotes.text: In regard to worldly interests.

19:76.annotated: And Allāh increases those who were guided, in guidance, and the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord[1] for reward and better for recourse.

footnotes.text: i.e., in the sight or evaluation of Allāh.

19:80.annotated: And We will inherit him [in] what he mentions,[1] and he will come to Us alone.

footnotes.text: Instead of giving him wealth and children in the Hereafter, Allāh will take from him those he had in worldly life at the time of his death.

19:84.annotated: So be not impatient over them. We only count out [i.e., allow] to them a [limited] number.[1]

footnotes.text: Of breaths, of days, or of evil deeds.

19:87.annotated: None will have [power of] intercession except he who had taken from the Most Merciful a covenant.[1]

footnotes.text: Not to worship other than Him.

19:96.annotated: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.[1]

footnotes.text: From Himself and from among each other.
See footnote to 2:1

20:5.annotated: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., having ascendancy over all creation.  See footnotes to 2:19 and 7:54

20:15.annotated: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it[1] - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.

footnotes.text: Meaning that Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) keeps knowledge of the Hour hidden from everyone except Himself.

20:16.annotated: So do not let one avert you from it[1] who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you [then] would perish.

footnotes.text: From preparation for the Hour or for the Hereafter.

20:39.annotated: [Saying], 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me[1] that you would be brought up under My eye [i.e., observation and care].

footnotes.text: Allāh put love of Moses into the hearts of the people.

20:40.annotated: [And We favored you] when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone,[1] but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.

footnotes.text: The Copt who died after being struck by Moses.

20:41.annotated: And I produced you for Myself.[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh had already selected Moses and made him strong in body and character according to the requirements of his mission.

20:47.annotated: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace[1] will be upon he who follows the guidance.

footnotes.text: i.e., safety and security from Allāh's punishment.

20:58.annotated: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "marked," as to be known.  Another meaning is "a place midway [between us]" or "a level place."

20:59.annotated: [Moses] said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."[1]

footnotes.text: So that the signs of Allāh would be seen clearly.

20:70.annotated: So the magicians fell down in prostration.[1] They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."

footnotes.text: After they had seen the miracles which Allāh had given Moses and that they were realities and not merely impressions of magic.

20:72.annotated: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us.[1] So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.

footnotes.text: This phrase has also been interpreted as an oath, i.e., "...by Him who created us."

20:73.annotated: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And Allāh is better and more enduring."[1]

footnotes.text: In reward and in punishment.

20:76.annotated: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.[1]

footnotes.text: From all uncleanliness, the greatest of which is worship and obedience to other than Allāh.

20:78.annotated: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., not only the water but that which only Allāh knows - terror, pain, regret, etc.

20:80.annotated: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you[1] at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails,

footnotes.text: i.e., with your prophet, to receive the scripture for you.

20:85.annotated: [Allāh] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Sāmirī[1] has led them astray."

footnotes.text: Translated as "the Samaritan" (from Samaria), a hypocrite among them who led the Children of Israel into idol-worship.

20:86.annotated: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved.[1] He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise?[2] Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me?"

footnotes.text: The meaning may also be "angry and enraged."
That He would send down the Torah, containing guidance for you.

20:96.annotated: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger[1] and threw it,[2] and thus did my soul entice me."

footnotes.text: i.e., a hoof-print in the sand left by the angel Gabriel's horse.
Into the fire upon the melted ornaments in order to form the calf.
