20:97.annotated: [Moses] said, "Then go. And indeed, it is [decreed] for you in [this] life to say, 'No contact.'[1] And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it [i.e., its ashes] into the sea with a blast.

footnotes.text: i.e., Do not touch me.  As chastisement, he was to be completely shunned by all people.

20:101.annotated: [Abiding] eternally therein,[1] and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load -

footnotes.text: i.e., in the state of sin.

20:102.annotated: The Day the Horn will be blown. And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.[1]

footnotes.text: From terror, or blinded completely.

20:105.annotated: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast.[1]

footnotes.text: Once they have been reduced to dust.

20:108.annotated: That Day, they [i.e., everyone] will follow [the call of] the Caller[1] [with] no deviation therefrom, and [all] voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper [of footsteps].

footnotes.text: To the gathering for judgement.

20:110.annotated: He [i.e., Allāh] knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them,[1] but they do not encompass it [i.e., what He knows] in knowledge.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:255.

20:111.annotated: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.[1] And he will have failed who carries injustice.[2]

footnotes.text: See footnotes to 2:255.
i.e., sin or wrongdoing towards Allāh or any of His creation.

20:113.annotated: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān[1] and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it would cause them remembrance.

footnotes.text: i.e., revealed in the Arabic language.

20:114.annotated: So high [above all] is Allāh, the Sovereign,[1] the Truth.[2] And, [O Muḥammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

footnotes.text: And owner of everything in existence.
Or "the True Reality," i.e., the real and permanent existence upon which all other existence depends.

20:115.annotated: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.[1]

footnotes.text: To resist temptation.

20:116.annotated: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees;[1] he refused.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:34.

20:127.annotated: And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.[1]

footnotes.text: Than that of this world.

20:129.annotated: And if not for a word[1] that preceded from your Lord, it [i.e., punishment] would have been an obligation [due immediately],[2] and [if not for] a specified term [decreed].

footnotes.text: See footnote to 10:19.
Allāh would have punished the disbelievers in this world as He did with previous peoples.

20:133.annotated: And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?[1]

footnotes.text: Is not the Qur’ān an adequate proof of Muḥammad's prophethood and sufficient as a lasting miracle?

20:134.annotated: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him,[1] they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses [i.e., teachings] before we were humiliated and disgraced?"

footnotes.text: Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).  Also interpreted as "before it," i.e., the Qur’ān.

20:135.annotated: Say, "Each [of us] is waiting;[1] so wait. For you will know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided."

footnotes.text: For the outcome of this matter.

21:6.annotated: Not a [single] city which We destroyed believed before them,[1] so will they believe?

footnotes.text: Even though they had witnessed signs and miracles.

21:8.annotated: And We did not make them [i.e., the prophets] forms not eating food,[1] nor were they immortal [on earth].

footnotes.text: Like the angels.  Rather, they were human beings with human attributes.

21:9.annotated: Then[1] We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed and destroyed the transgressors.

footnotes.text: Once they had conveyed the message.

21:10.annotated: We have certainly sent down to you a Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] in which is your mention.[1] Then will you not reason?

footnotes.text: This implies the honor of having been mentioned or addressed.  Another meaning is "your reminder."

21:11.annotated: And how many a city which was unjust[1] have We shattered and produced after it another people.

footnotes.text: i.e., its inhabitants persisting in wrongdoing.

21:13.annotated: [Some angels said], "Do not flee but return to where you were given luxury and to your homes - perhaps you will be questioned."[1]

footnotes.text: About what happened to you.  This is said to them in sarcasm and ridicule.

21:17.annotated: Had We intended to take a diversion,[1] We could have taken it from [what is] with Us - if [indeed] We were to do so.

footnotes.text: Such as a wife or a child.

21:18.annotated: Rather, We dash the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it,[1] and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from that which you describe.[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "strikes its brain," disabling or killing it.
Of untruth concerning Allāh, particularly here, the claim that He has a son or other "partner" in divinity.

21:24.annotated: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, [O Muḥammad], "Produce your proof. This [Qur’ān] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me."[1] But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.

footnotes.text: All previous prophets called for the worship of Allāh alone.

21:26.annotated: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, they[1] are [but] honored servants.

footnotes.text: Those they claim to be "children" of Allāh, such as the angels, Ezra, Jesus, etc.

21:28.annotated: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them,[1] and they cannot intercede except on behalf of one whom He approves. And they, from fear of Him, are apprehensive.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:255.

21:32.annotated: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs,[1] are turning away.

footnotes.text: The signs present in the heavens.

21:39.annotated: If those who disbelieved but knew the time when they will not avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs and they will not be aided...[1]

footnotes.text: The completion of the sentence is understood to be "...they would not be asking in disbelief and ridicule to be shown the punishment."

21:44.annotated: But, [on the contrary], We have provided good things for these [disbelievers] and their fathers until life was prolonged for them. Then do they not see that We set upon the land, reducing it from its borders?[1] Is it they who will overcome?

footnotes.text: See footnote to 13:41.

21:47.annotated: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there is [even] the weight of a mustard seed,[1] We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountant.

footnotes.text: i.e., anything as small or insignificant as a mustard seed.

21:48.annotated: And We had already given Moses and Aaron the criterion and a light and a reminder[1] for the righteous

footnotes.text: These are three qualities of the Torah.

21:49.annotated: Who fear their Lord unseen,[1] while they are of the Hour apprehensive.

footnotes.text: Which can mean "Him being unseen" by them or "though they are unseen" by others.

21:50.annotated: And this [Qur’ān] is a blessed message which We have sent down. Then are you with it unacquainted?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., pretending ignorance, disapproving or refusing to acknowledge it?

21:51.annotated: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgement before,[1] and We were of him well-Knowing

footnotes.text: i.e., before Moses.  Allāh had guided him from early youth.

21:61.annotated: They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."[1]

footnotes.text: To what they had heard him say.  It may also mean "...that they may witness [what will be done to him as punishment]."

21:65.annotated: Then they reversed themselves,[1] [saying], "You have already known that these do not speak!"

footnotes.text: After first admitting their error, they were seized by pride and obstinacy.

21:67.annotated: Uff[1] to you and to what you worship instead of Allāh. Then will you not use reason?"

footnotes.text: An exclamation of anger and displeasure.

21:76.annotated: And [mention] Noah, when he called [to Allāh][1] before [that time], so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great affliction [i.e., the flood].

footnotes.text: i.e., supplicated against his people who had persisted in denial and animosity.  See 71:26-28.

21:78.annotated: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field - when the sheep of a people overran it [at night],[1] and We were witness to their judgement.

footnotes.text: Eating and destroying the crops.

21:79.annotated: And We gave understanding of it [i.e., the case] to Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgement and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains to exalt [Us], along with David and [also] the birds. And We were doing [that].[1]

footnotes.text: Meaning that Allāh has always been capable of accomplishing whatever He wills.

21:82.annotated: And of the devils [i.e., jinn] were those who dived for him and did work other than that. And We were of them a guardian.[1]

footnotes.text: Preventing any disobedience or deviation by them from Solomon's instructions and protecting him from being harmed by them.

21:87.annotated: And [mention] the man of the fish [i.e., Jonah], when he went off in anger[1] and thought that We would not decree [anything] upon him.[2] And he called out within the darknesses,[3] "There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers."

footnotes.text: At the disbelief of his people.
Or "would not restrict him" in the belly of the fish.
That of the night, of the sea, and of the fish's interior.

21:90.annotated: So We responded to him, and We gave to him John, and amended for him his wife. Indeed, they used to hasten to good deeds and supplicate[1] Us in hope and fear, and they were to Us humbly submissive.

footnotes.text: i.e., worship.

21:92.annotated: Indeed this, your religion, is one religion,[1] and I am your Lord, so worship Me.

footnotes.text: i.e., a collective way of life or course of conduct followed by a community.

21:93.annotated: And [yet] they divided their affair [i.e., that of their religion] among themselves,[1] [but] all to Us will return.

footnotes.text: Becoming sects and denominations.

21:94.annotated: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - no denial will there be for his effort,[1] and indeed We [i.e., Our angels], of it, are recorders.

footnotes.text: Such a person will not be deprived of his due reward.

21:95.annotated: And it is prohibited to [the people of] a city which We have destroyed that they will [ever] return[1]

footnotes.text: They cannot return to this world, nor can they repent to Allāh.

21:103.annotated: They will not be grieved by the greatest terror,[1] and the angels will meet them, [saying], "This is your Day which you have been promised" -

footnotes.text: The events of the Last Hour or of the Resurrection.

21:104.annotated: The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.[1]

footnotes.text: More literally, "Indeed, We are ever doers" of what We will.

21:105.annotated: And We have already written in the book [of Psalms][1] after the [previous] mention[2] that the land [of Paradise] is inherited by My righteous servants.

footnotes.text: Az-Zabūr can also mean "scriptures" in general.
i.e., the Torah.  The "mention" may also refer to the original inscription with Allāh, i.e., the Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

21:109.annotated: But if they turn away, then say, "I have announced to [all of] you equally.[1] And I know not whether near or far is that which you are promised.

footnotes.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) made this message known to all people, not concealing any of it from anyone or preferring any group over another.

21:111.annotated: And I know not; perhaps it[1] is a trial for you and enjoyment for a time."

footnotes.text: The postponement of punishment.

21:112.annotated: [The Prophet (ﷺ)] has said, "My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one whose help is sought against that which you describe."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., their lies and disbelief.

22:5.annotated: O people, if you should be in doubt about the Resurrection, then [consider that] indeed, We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, and then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed[1] - that We may show you.[2] And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, and then [We develop you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit [old] age so that he knows, after [once having] knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [something] of every beautiful kind.

footnotes.text: That which is incomplete. This may include what is aborted at that stage.
Our power and creative ability.

22:11.annotated: And of the people is he who worships Allāh on an edge.[1] If he is touched by good, he is reassured by it; but if he is struck by trial, he turns on his face [to unbelief]. He has lost [this] world and the Hereafter. That is what is the manifest loss.

footnotes.text: At the edge of his religion, so to speak, i.e., with uncertainty, hypocrisy or heedlessness.

22:15.annotated: Whoever should think that Allāh will not support him [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)] in this world and the Hereafter - let him extend a rope to the ceiling, then cut off [his breath],[1] and let him see: will his effort remove that which enrages [him]?

footnotes.text: i.e., strangle himself.

22:17.annotated: Indeed, those who have believed and those who were Jews and the Sabeans and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated with Allāh - Allāh will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allāh is, over all things, Witness.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote of 4:79.

22:18.annotated: Do you not see [i.e., know] that to Allāh prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many the punishment has been justified.[1] And he whom Allāh humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allāh does what He wills.

footnotes.text: And therefore decreed.

22:19.annotated: These[1] are two adversaries who have disputed over their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have cut out for them garments of fire. Poured upon their heads will be scalding water

footnotes.text: i.e., the believers and the disbelievers.

22:25.annotated: Indeed, those who have disbelieved and avert [people] from the way of Allāh and [from] al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, which We made for the people - equal are the resident therein and one from outside - and [also] whoever intends [a deed] therein[1] of deviation [in religion] by wrongdoing - We will make him taste of a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: Whether inside its boundaries or intending from afar to do evil therein.  The Ḥaram is unique in that the mere intention of sin therein (whether or not it is actually carried out) is sufficient to bring punishment from Allāh.

22:26.annotated: And [mention, O Muḥammad], when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform ṭawāf[1] and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:125.

22:28.annotated: That they may witness [i.e., attend] benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allāh on known [i.e., specific] days over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals.[1] So eat of them and feed the miserable and poor.

footnotes.text: Al-anʿām:  camels, cattle, sheep and goats.

22:30.annotated: That [has been commanded], and whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allāh - it is best for him in the sight of his Lord. And permitted to you are the grazing livestock, except what is recited to you.[1] So avoid the uncleanliness of idols and avoid false statement,

footnotes.text: See 5:3.

22:33.annotated: For you therein [i.e., the animals marked for sacrifice] are benefits for a specified term;[1] then their place of sacrifice is at the ancient House.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., they may be milked or ridden (in the case of camels) before the time of slaughter.
i.e., within the boundaries of the Ḥaram, which includes Minā.

22:34.annotated: And for every [religious] community We have appointed a rite [of sacrifice][1] that they may mention the name of Allāh over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. For your god is one God, so to Him submit. And, [O Muḥammad], give good tidings to the humble [before their Lord]

footnotes.text: i.e., the right of sacrifice has always been a part of Allāh's revealed religion.

22:39.annotated: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought,[1] because they were wronged. And indeed, Allāh is competent to give them victory.

footnotes.text: Referring here to the Prophet's companions.

22:45.annotated: And how many a city did We destroy while it was committing wrong - so it is [now] fallen into ruin[1] - and [how many] an abandoned well and [how many] a lofty palace.[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "fallen in upon its roofs," i.e., after the roofs of its buildings had caved in, the walls collapsed over them.
i.e., How many wells have been left inoperative, and how many palaces have been emptied of their occupants in the past.

22:51.annotated: But the ones who strove against Our verses, [seeking] to cause failure[1] - those are the companions of Hellfire.

footnotes.text: i.e., trying to undermine their credibility and thereby defeat the Prophet (ﷺ).

22:52.annotated: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke [or recited], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding]. But Allāh abolishes that which Satan throws in; then Allāh makes precise His verses.[1] And Allāh is Knowing and Wise.

footnotes.text: Clarifying those issues which were misunderstood to remove any doubt.

22:53.annotated: [That is] so He may make what Satan throws in [i.e., asserts] a trial for those within whose hearts is disease[1] and those hard of heart. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:10.

22:55.annotated: But those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt of it until the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren Day.[1]

footnotes.text: One which will not be followed by night and therefore will not give birth to a new day, referring to the Day of Resurrection.

22:56.annotated: [All] sovereignty that Day is for Allāh;[1] He will judge between them. So they who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Pleasure.

footnotes.text: None will compete with Him for authority at that time.

22:60.annotated: That [is so]. And whoever responds [to injustice] with the equivalent of that with which he was harmed and then is tyrannized - Allāh will surely aid him. Indeed, Allāh is Pardoning and Forgiving.[1]

footnotes.text: In spite of His ability to take vengeance. The statement contains a suggestion that the believers pardon as well.

22:61.annotated: That[1] is because Allāh causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night and because Allāh is Hearing and Seeing.

footnotes.text: i.e., Allāh's capability to give assistance or victory to the oppressed.

22:63.annotated: Do you not see that Allāh has sent down rain from the sky and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allāh is Subtle[1] and Aware.[2]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote of 6:103.
Of His creation and of the needs of His creatures.

22:70.annotated: Do you not know that Allāh knows what is in the heaven and earth? Indeed, that is in a Record.[1] Indeed that, for Allāh, is easy.

footnotes.text: The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), which is with Allāh.

22:72.annotated: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, you recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve disapproval. They are almost on the verge of assaulting those who recite to them Our verses. Say, "Then shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that?[1] [It is] the Fire which Allāh has promised those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination."

footnotes.text: i.e., worse than the rage you feel against those who recite Allāh's verses or worse than your threats against them.

22:73.annotated: O people, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allāh will never create [as much as] a fly, even if they gathered together for it [i.e., that purpose]. And if the fly should steal from them a [tiny] thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the pursuer and pursued.[1]

footnotes.text: A comparison is made here to the worshipper of a false deity and that which he worships.

22:74.annotated: They have not appraised Allāh with true appraisal.[1] Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.

footnotes.text: They have not assessed Him with the assessment due to Him, meaning that they did not take into account His perfect attributes.

22:76.annotated: He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them.[1] And to Allāh will be returned [all] matters.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:255.

23:6.annotated: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess,[1] for indeed, they will not be blamed -

footnotes.text: Female slaves or captives under their ownership.

23:11.annotated: Who will inherit al-Firdaus.[1] They will abide therein eternally.

footnotes.text: The highest part of Paradise.

23:13.annotated: Then We placed him as a sperm-drop[1] in a firm lodging [i.e., the womb].

footnotes.text: Or "as a zygote."

23:14.annotated: Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump [of flesh], and We made [from] the lump, bones, and We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allāh, the best of creators.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the most skillful and only true Creator.

23:27.annotated: So We inspired to him, "Construct the ship under Our observation and Our inspiration, and when Our command comes and the oven overflows,[1] put into it [i.e., the ship] from each [creature] two mates and your family, except him for whom the decree [of destruction] has proceeded. And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 11:40.

23:32.annotated: And We sent among them a messenger[1] from themselves, [saying], "Worship Allāh; you have no deity other than Him; then will you not fear Him?"

footnotes.text: Prophet Hūd, who was sent to the tribe of ʿAad.

23:36.annotated: How far, how far, is that which you are promised.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., how distant and improbable it is.

23:41.annotated: So the shriek[1] seized them in truth,[2] and We made them as [plant] stubble. Then away with the wrongdoing people.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 11:67.
i.e., by right or in justice.

23:44.annotated: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time there came to a nation its messenger, they denied him, so We made them follow one another [to destruction], and We made them narrations.[1] So away with a people who do not believe.

footnotes.text: i.e., history or lessons for mankind.

23:45.annotated: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., evidences from Allāh.

23:49.annotated: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture that perhaps they[1] would be guided.

footnotes.text: The Children of Israel.

23:52.annotated: And indeed this, your religion, is one religion,[1] and I am your Lord, so fear Me."

footnotes.text: See footnote to 21:92.

23:53.annotated: But they [i.e., the people] divided their religion among them into portions [i.e., sects] - each faction, in what it has,[1] rejoicing.

footnotes.text: Of beliefs, opinions, customs, etc.

23:56.annotated: Is [because] We hasten for them good things? Rather, they do not perceive.[1]

footnotes.text: That the good things given to them in this world are but a trial for them.

23:60.annotated: And they who give what they give while their hearts are fearful[1] because they will be returning to their Lord -

footnotes.text: Lest their deeds not be acceptable.

23:64.annotated: Until when We seize their affluent ones with punishment,[1] at once they are crying [to Allāh] for help.

footnotes.text: In worldly life, before the punishment of the Hereafter.  Although general, the description includes specifically the punishment of the Quraysh by famine.

23:67.annotated: In arrogance regarding it,[1] conversing by night, speaking evil.

footnotes.text: The revelation.  Or "him," i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ).

23:71.annotated: But if the Truth [i.e., Allāh] had followed their inclinations, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been ruined. Rather, We have brought them their message,[1] but they, from their message, are turning away.

footnotes.text: Or "reminder."

23:81.annotated: Rather,[1] they say like what the former peoples said.

footnotes.text: Instead of understanding or reasoning.

23:100.annotated: That I might do righteousness in that which I left behind."[1] No! It is only a word he is saying; and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.

footnotes.text: Or "in that which I neglected."

23:104.annotated: The Fire will sear their faces, and they therein will have taut smiles.[1]

footnotes.text: Their lips having been contracted by scorching until the teeth are exposed.

23:116.annotated: So exalted is Allāh, the Sovereign,[1] the Truth;[2] there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.

footnotes.text: And owner of everything in existence.
Or "the True Reality."

24:2.annotated: The [unmarried] woman or [unmarried] man found guilty of sexual intercourse[1] - lash each one of them with a hundred lashes,[2] and do not be taken by pity for them in the religion [i.e., law] of Allāh,[3] if you should believe in Allāh and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.

footnotes.text: Either by voluntary confession of the offender or the testimony of four male witnesses to having actually seen the act take place.  Otherwise, there can be no conviction.
The ruling in this verse is applicable to unmarried fornicators.  Execution by stoning is confirmed in the sunnah for convicted adulterers.
i.e., Do not let sympathy for a guilty person move you to alter anything ordained by Allāh, for in His law is protection of society as a whole.

24:3.annotated: The fornicator does not marry except a [female] fornicator or polytheist, and none marries her except a fornicator[1] or a polytheist, and that [i.e., marriage to such persons] has been made unlawful to the believers.

footnotes.text: Included in this ruling is the adulterer as well.  Such persons cannot be married to believers unless they have repented and reformed.

24:6.annotated: And those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves - then the witness of one of them[1] [shall be] four testimonies [swearing] by Allāh that indeed, he is of the truthful.

footnotes.text: The husbands who have been betrayed.

24:10.annotated: And if not for the favor of Allāh upon you and His mercy...[1] and because Allāh is Accepting of Repentance and Wise.

footnotes.text: The phrase omitted is estimated to be "...you would have surely been punished, destroyed or scandalized," or "...you would have suffered many difficult situations."

24:11.annotated: Indeed, those who came with falsehood[1] are a group among you. Do not think it bad for you; rather, it is good for you. For every person among them is what [punishment] he has earned from the sin, and he who took upon himself the greater portion thereof[2] - for him is a great punishment [i.e., Hellfire].

footnotes.text: Referring to the incident when the Prophet's wife ʿĀ’ishah was falsely accused by the hypocrites.
i.e., ʿAbdullāh bin ʿUbayy, leader of the hypocrites.

24:15.annotated: When you received it with your tongues[1] and said with your mouths that of which you had no knowledge and thought it was insignificant while it was, in the sight of Allāh, tremendous.

footnotes.text: Rather than your ears, i.e., not thinking about what you had heard but hastening to repeat it carelessly.

24:19.annotated: Indeed, those who like that immorality[1] should be spread [or publicized] among those who have believed will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allāh knows[2] and you do not know.

footnotes.text: Specifically, unlawful sexual relations.
The hidden aspects of all things:  what is beneficial and what is harmful.

24:20.annotated: And if it had not been for the favor of Allāh upon you and His mercy...[1] and because Allāh is Kind and Merciful.

footnotes.text: See footnote to verse 10.

24:26.annotated: Evil words are for evil men, and evil men are [subjected] to evil words. And good words are for good men, and good men are [an object] of good words.[1] Those [good people] are declared innocent of what they [i.e., slanderers] say. For them is forgiveness and noble provision.

footnotes.text: Another accepted interpretation is "Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women.  And good women are for good men, and good men are for good women."

24:27.annotated: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you ascertain welcome and greet[1] their inhabitants. That is best for you; perhaps you will be reminded [i.e., advised].

footnotes.text: By the words "As-salāmu ʿalaykum" ("Peace be upon you").

24:28.annotated: And if you do not find anyone therein, do not enter them until permission has been given you. And if it is said to you, "Go back,"[1] then go back; it is purer for you. And Allāh is Knowing of what you do.

footnotes.text: Or a similar expression showing that the occupants are not prepared to receive visitors (which should be respected).

24:29.annotated: There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited in which there is convenience[1] for you. And Allāh knows what you reveal and what you conceal.

footnotes.text: Some benefit such as rest, shelter, commodities, one's personal belongings, etc.

24:30.annotated: Tell the believing men to reduce [some] of their vision[1] and guard their private parts.[2] That is purer for them. Indeed, Allāh is [fully] Aware of what they do.

footnotes.text: Looking only at what is lawful and averting their eyes from what is unlawful.
From being seen and from unlawful acts.

24:31.annotated: And tell the believing women to reduce [some] of their vision[1] and guard their private parts and not expose their adornment[2] except that which [necessarily] appears thereof[3] and to wrap [a portion of] their headcovers over their chests and not expose their adornment [i.e., beauty] except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, that which their right hands possess [i.e., slaves], or those male attendants having no physical desire,[4] or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allāh in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.

footnotes.text: Looking only at what is lawful and averting their eyes from what is unlawful.
Both natural beauty, such as hair or body shape, and that with which a woman beautifies herself of clothing, jewelry, etc.
i.e., the outer garments or whatever might appear out of necessity, such as a part of the face or the hands.
Referring to an abnormal condition in which a man is devoid of sexual feeling.

24:33.annotated: But let them who find not [the means for] marriage abstain [from sexual relations] until Allāh enriches them from His bounty. And those who seek a contract [for eventual emancipation] from among whom your right hands possess[1] - then make a contract with them if you know there is within them goodness and give them from the wealth of Allāh which He has given you. And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek [thereby] the temporary interests of worldly life. And if someone should compel them, then indeed, Allāh is [to them], after their compulsion, Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: i.e., those slaves who desire to purchase their freedom from their owners for a price agreed upon by both.

24:34.annotated: And We have certainly sent down to you distinct verses[1] and examples from those who passed on before you and an admonition for those who fear Allāh.

footnotes.text: i.e., rulings and ordinances, in particular those in this sūrah.

24:35.annotated: Allāh is the Light[1] of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light[2] is like a niche within which is a lamp;[3] the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allāh guides to His light whom He wills. And Allāh presents examples for the people, and Allāh is Knowing of all things.

footnotes.text: i.e., the source and bestower of light and enlightenment.
His guidance in the heart of a believing servant.
Literally, "a burning wick," which is the essence of a lamp.

24:36.annotated: [Such niches are] in houses [i.e., mosques] which Allāh has ordered to be raised and that His name be mentioned [i.e., praised] therein; exalting Him within them in the morning and the evenings[1]

footnotes.text: The term used here can refer to either afternoon or evening.

24:53.annotated: And they swear by Allāh their strongest oaths that if you ordered them, they would go forth [in Allāh's cause]. Say, "Do not swear. [Such] obedience is known.[1] Indeed, Allāh is [fully] Aware of that which you do."

footnotes.text: i.e., the hypocrites' pretense of obedience is known to be a lie.

24:55.annotated: Allāh has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession [to authority] upon the earth just as He granted it to those before them and that He will surely establish for them [therein] their religion which He has preferred for them and that He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security, [for] they worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves[1] after that - then those are the defiantly disobedient.

footnotes.text: i.e., denies the favor of Allāh or does not live by His ordinance.

24:58.annotated: O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not [yet] reached puberty among you ask permission of you [before entering] at three times: before the dawn prayer and when you put aside your clothing [for rest] at noon and after the night prayer. [These are] three times of privacy[1] for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them beyond these [periods], for they continually circulate among you - some of you, among others. Thus does Allāh make clear to you the verses [i.e., His ordinances]; and Allāh is Knowing and Wise.

footnotes.text: Literally, "exposure" or "being uncovered."

24:61.annotated: There is not upon the blind [any] constraint nor upon the lame constraint nor upon the ill constraint nor upon yourselves when you eat from your [own] houses or the houses of your fathers or the houses of your mothers or the houses of your brothers or the houses of your sisters or the houses of your father's brothers or the houses of your father's sisters or the houses of your mother's brothers or the houses of your mother's sisters or [from houses] whose keys you possess or [from the house] of your friend. There is no blame upon you whether you eat together or separately. But when you enter houses, give greetings of peace[1] upon each other - a greeting from Allāh, blessed and good. Thus does Allāh make clear to you the verses [of ordinance] that you may understand.

footnotes.text: Saying, "As-salāmu ʿalaykum" ("Peace be upon you").

24:63.annotated: Do not make [your] calling of the Messenger among yourselves as the call of one of you to another. Already Allāh knows those of you who slip away, concealed by others. So let those beware who dissent from his [i.e., the Prophet's] order,[1] lest fitnah[2] strike them or a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: Meaning also his way or his sunnah.
Trials, affliction, dissension, strife, etc.

24:64.annotated: Unquestionably, to Allāh belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth. Already He knows that upon which you [stand][1] and [knows] the Day[2] when they will be returned to Him and He will inform them of what they have done. And Allāh is Knowing of all things.

footnotes.text: i.e., your position - the basis for your actions (whether sincere faith or hypocrisy) and the condition of your souls.
The meaning can also be rendered "...and [let them beware of] the Day..."

25:9.annotated: Look how they strike for you comparisons;[1] but they have strayed, so they cannot [find] a way.

footnotes.text: From their own imaginations in order to deny and discredit you.

25:16.annotated: For them therein is whatever they wish, [while] abiding eternally. It is ever upon your Lord a promise [worthy to be] requested.[1]

footnotes.text: Or "...a promise requested [for them by the angels]."

25:19.annotated: So they will deny you, [disbelievers], in what you say,[1] and you cannot avert [punishment] or [find] help. And whoever commits injustice[2] among you - We will make him taste a great punishment.

footnotes.text: At the time of Judgement the false objects of worship will betray their worshippers and deny them.
Specifically, association of others with Allāh.

25:21.annotated: And those who do not expect the meeting with Us say, "Why were not angels sent down to us, or [why] do we [not] see our Lord?" They have certainly become arrogant within themselves[1] and [become] insolent with great insolence.

footnotes.text: Additional meanings are "among themselves" and "over [the matter of] themselves."

25:22.annotated: The day they see the angels[1] - no good tidings will there be that day for the criminals, and [the angels] will say, "Prevented and inaccessible."[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., at the time of death.
Referring to any good tidings.

25:23.annotated: And We will approach [i.e., regard][1] what they have done of deeds and make them as dust dispersed.

footnotes.text: On the Day of Judgement.

25:25.annotated: And [mention] the Day when the heaven will split open with [emerging] clouds,[1] and the angels will be sent down in successive descent.

footnotes.text: Within which are the angels.

25:27.annotated: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands [in regret] he will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., followed the Prophet (ﷺ) on a path of guidance.

25:28.annotated: Oh, woe to me! I wish I had not taken that one[1] as a friend.

footnotes.text: The person who misguided him.

25:29.annotated: He led me away from the remembrance[1] after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., the Qur’ān or the remembrance of Allāh.
Forsaking him once he has led him into evil.

25:30.annotated: And the Messenger has said, "O my Lord, indeed my people have taken this Qur’ān as [a thing] abandoned."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., avoiding it, not listening to or understanding it, not living by it, or preferring something else to it.

25:32.annotated: And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur’ān not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is] that We may strengthen thereby your heart. And We have spaced it distinctly.[1]

footnotes.text: Also, "recited it with distinct recitation."

25:37.annotated: And the people of Noah - when they denied the messengers,[1] We drowned them, and We made them for mankind a sign. And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: Their denial of Noah was as if they had denied all those who brought the same message from Allāh.

25:38.annotated: And [We destroyed] ʿAad and Thamūd and the companions of the well[1] and many generations between them.

footnotes.text: Said to be a people who denied Prophet Shuʿayb or possibly those mentioned in Sūrah Yā Seen, 36:13-29.

25:40.annotated: And they have already come upon the town which was showered with a rain of evil [i.e., stones]. So have they not seen it? But they are not expecting resurrection.[1]

footnotes.text: So they do not benefit from lessons of the past.

25:44.annotated: Or do you think that most of them hear or reason? They are not except like livestock.[1] Rather, they are [even] more astray in [their] way.

footnotes.text: i.e., cattle or sheep, that follow without question wherever they are led.

25:45.annotated: Have you not considered your Lord - how He extends the shadow, and if He willed, He could have made it stationary? Then We made the sun for it an indication.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., showing the existence of a shadow or making it apparent by contrast.

25:46.annotated: Then We [retract and] hold it with Us for a brief grasp.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., when the sun is overhead at noon.

25:47.annotated: And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing[1] and sleep [a means for] rest and has made the day a resurrection.[2]

footnotes.text: Covering you in darkness and providing rest.
For renewal of life and activity.

25:50.annotated: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they might be reminded,[1] but most of the people refuse except disbelief.

footnotes.text: Of Allāh's ability to bring the dead to life.

25:51.annotated: And if We had willed, We could have sent into every city a warner.[1]

footnotes.text: However, Allāh willed that Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) be sent as the final messenger for all peoples of the earth until the Day of Resurrection.

25:59.annotated: He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days and then established Himself above the Throne[1] - the Most Merciful, so ask about Him one well informed [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)].

footnotes.text: See footnotes to 2:19 and 7:54.

25:63.annotated: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily,[1] and when the ignorant address them [harshly], they say [words of] peace,[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., gently, with dignity but without arrogance.
Or "safety," i.e., words free from fault or evil.

25:68.annotated: And those who do not invoke[1] with Allāh another deity or kill the soul which Allāh has forbidden [to be killed], except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty.

footnotes.text: Or "worship."

25:74.annotated: And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes[1] and make us a leader [i.e., example] for the righteous."

footnotes.text: i.e., a source of happiness due to their righteousness.

25:75.annotated: Those will be awarded the Chamber[1] for what they patiently endured, and they will be received therein with greetings and [words of] peace,

footnotes.text: The most elevated portion of Paradise.

25:77.annotated: Say, "What would my Lord care for you if not for your supplication?"[1] For you [disbelievers] have denied, so it [i.e., your denial] is going to be adherent.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., faith and worship.  An alternative meaning is "What would my Lord do with you..."
It will remain with them, causing punishment to be required and imperative upon them.
See footnote to 2:1.

26:4.annotated: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign for which their necks would remain humbled.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., they would be compelled to believe.

26:16.annotated: Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are the messengers[1] of the Lord of the worlds,

footnotes.text: The singular form in Arabic indicates that both were sent with a single message.

26:19.annotated: And [then] you did your deed which you did,[1] and you were of the ungrateful."

footnotes.text: i.e., striking the Copt, who died as a result.

26:27.annotated: [Pharaoh] said,[1] "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad."

footnotes.text: Angrily addressing those present.

26:32.annotated: So [Moses] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., clearly genuine.

26:38.annotated: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a well-known day.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the morning of the day of festival.  See 20:58-59.

26:53.annotated: Then Pharaoh sent among the cities gatherers[1]

footnotes.text: Recruiters of an army to prevent the emigration of the Children of Israel.
Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) caused them to abandon their wealth and property in pursuit of the Israelites.

26:77.annotated: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds,[1]

footnotes.text: The people worshipped idols in addition to Allāh.

26:102.annotated: Then if we only had a return [to the world] and could be of the believers..."[1]

footnotes.text: The conclusion of this verse is estimated as "...we would do this or that."

26:105.annotated: The people of Noah denied the messengers[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 25:37.

26:128.annotated: Do you construct on every elevation a sign,[1] amusing yourselves,

footnotes.text: i.e., a symbol or indication of their wealth and power.  They used to build lofty structures along the road to be seen by all who passed by.

26:155.annotated: He said, "This is a she-camel.[1] For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day.

footnotes.text: Miraculously sent to them as a sign by Allāh.

26:165.annotated: Do you approach males among the worlds[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., Are there, out of all Allāh's creatures, any besides you who commit this unnatural act?

26:171.annotated: Except an old woman[1] among those who remained behind.

footnotes.text: Lot's wife, who had collaborated with the evildoers.

26:184.annotated: And fear He who created you and the former creation."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., previous generations.

26:198.annotated: And even if We had revealed it to one among the foreigners[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the non-Arabs or those who are not fluent in the Arabic language.

26:199.annotated: And he had recited it to them [perfectly],[1] they would [still] not have been believers in it.

footnotes.text: As a miracle from Allāh.

26:210.annotated: And the devils have not brought it [i.e., the revelation] down.[1]

footnotes.text: As was asserted by the disbelievers.  Rather, it was brought by Gabriel, the Trustworthy Spirit.

26:212.annotated: Indeed they, from [its] hearing, are removed.[1]

footnotes.text: As mentioned in 72:9.

26:213.annotated: So do not invoke[1] with Allāh another deity and [thus] be among the punished.

footnotes.text: Or "worship."

26:218.annotated: Who sees you when you arise[1]

footnotes.text: From your bed at night for prayer while you are alone.

26:219.annotated: And your movement among those who prostrate.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., among those who pray with you in congregation.

26:223.annotated: They pass on what is heard,[1] and most of them are liars.

footnotes.text: This was before they were prevented, as described in 72:8-9.

26:225.annotated: Do you not see that in every valley they roam[1]

footnotes.text: Speaking lies indiscriminately and praising and disparaging others according to whim.

26:227.annotated: Except those [poets] who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allāh often and defend [the Muslims][1] after they were wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.

footnotes.text: By replying through poetry to the attacks of hostile poets.

27:1.annotated: Ṭā, Seen.[1] These are the verses of the Qur’ān [i.e., recitation] and a clear Book

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.

27:10.annotated: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it were a snake, he turned in flight and did not return.[1] [Allāh said], "O Moses, fear not. Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear.

footnotes.text: Or "did not look back."

27:19.annotated: So [Solomon] smiled, amused at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me[1] to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the ranks of] Your righteous servants."[2]

footnotes.text: More literally, "gather within me the utmost strength and ability."
Or "with Your righteous servants [into Paradise]."

27:21.annotated: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him unless he brings me clear authorization."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., a valid excuse.

27:32.annotated: She said, "O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I would not decide a matter until you witness [for] me."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., are present with me or testify in my favor.

27:44.annotated: She was told, "Enter the palace." But when she saw it, she thought it was a body of water[1] and uncovered her shins [to wade through]. He said, "Indeed, it is a palace [whose floor is] made smooth with glass." She said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, and I submit with Solomon to Allāh, Lord of the worlds."

footnotes.text: The floor was transparent, and beneath it was flowing water.

27:46.annotated: He said, "O my people, why are you impatient for evil before [i.e., instead of] good?[1] Why do you not seek forgiveness of Allāh that you may receive mercy?"

footnotes.text: By challenging Ṣāliḥ to bring on the promised punishment rather than asking for mercy from Allāh.

27:47.annotated: They said, "We consider you a bad omen, you and those with you." He said, "Your omen [i.e., fate] is with Allāh. Rather, you are a people being tested."[1]

footnotes.text: Or "being tempted [by Satan]."

27:49.annotated: They said, "Take a mutual oath by Allāh that we will kill him by night, he and his family. Then we will say to his executor,[1] 'We did not witness the destruction of his family, and indeed, we are truthful.'"

footnotes.text: i.e., the one responsible for executing his will and avenging his blood.

27:54.annotated: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, "Do you commit immorality[1] while you are seeing?[2]

footnotes.text: Homosexual acts.
i.e., openly.  Another meaning is "...while you are aware [that it is wrong]."

27:60.annotated: [More precisely], is He [not best] who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you rain from the sky, causing to grow thereby gardens of joyful beauty which you could not [otherwise] have grown the trees thereof? Is there a deity with Allāh?[1] [No], but they are a people who ascribe equals [to Him].

footnotes.text: Three meanings are implied:  "Is there another god who did all of this with Allāh?" or "Is there any deity worthy to be worshipped along with Allāh?" or "Is there a deity to be compared with Allāh?"

27:62.annotated: Is He [not best] who responds to the desperate one when he calls upon Him and removes evil and makes you inheritors of the earth?[1] Is there a deity with Allāh? Little do you remember.

footnotes.text: Generation after generation.

27:75.annotated: And there is nothing concealed[1] within the heaven and the earth except that it is in a clear Register.[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "absent [from the senses]."
The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), which is with Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

27:82.annotated: And when the word [i.e., decree] befalls them,[1] We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith].

footnotes.text: At the approach of the Hour.

27:85.annotated: And the decree will befall them[1] for the wrong they did, and they will not [be able to] speak.

footnotes.text: Allāh's decree will come into effect upon them, and His promise will be fulfilled.

27:88.annotated: And you see the mountains, thinking them motionless,[1] while they will pass as the passing of clouds. [It is] the work of Allāh, who perfected all things. Indeed, He is Aware of that which you do.

footnotes.text: Or "solid and rigid."

27:90.annotated: And whoever comes with an evil deed[1] - their faces will be overturned into the Fire, [and it will be said], "Are you recompensed except for what you used to do?"

footnotes.text: Without having repented.  It may refer generally to any sin or more specifically to association of another with Allāh.

27:91.annotated: [Say, O Muḥammad], "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city,[1] who made it sacred and to whom [belongs] all things. And I am commanded to be of the Muslims [i.e., those who submit to Allāh].

footnotes.text: Or region, meaning Makkah and its surroundings.
See footnote to 2:1.

28:6.annotated: And establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and [his minister] Hāmān and their soldiers through them[1] that which they had feared.

footnotes.text: By means of those whom they had oppressed and enslaved.

28:9.annotated: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "[He will be] a comfort of the eye [i.e., pleasure] for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son." And they perceived not.[1]

footnotes.text: What would be the result of that.

28:12.annotated: And We had prevented from him [all] wet nurses before,[1] so she said, "Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you while they are to him [for his upbringing] sincere?"

footnotes.text: Prior to that, Moses had refused to nurse from any other woman.

28:15.annotated: And he entered the city at a time of inattention by its people[1] and found therein two men fighting: one from his faction and one from among his enemy. And the one from his faction called for help to him against the one from his enemy, so Moses struck him and [unintentionally] killed him. [Moses] said, "This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a manifest, misleading enemy."

footnotes.text: i.e., during the noon period of rest.

28:19.annotated: And when he wanted to strike the one who was an enemy to both of them, he[1] said, "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed someone yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land and do not want to be of the amenders."

footnotes.text: i.e., the Israelite, thinking that Moses meant to strike him.  Some commentators have attributed the words to the Copt; however, the Israelite was the only one who knew of the previous occurrence.

28:25.annotated: Then one of the two women came to him walking with shyness. She said, "Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered for us." So when he came to him[1] and related to him the story, he said, "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."

footnotes.text: Prophet Shuʿayb, the father of the two women.

28:30.annotated: But when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley in a blessed spot - from the tree,[1] "O Moses, indeed I am Allāh, Lord of the worlds."

footnotes.text: Which was within the fire.

28:31.annotated: And [he was told], "Throw down your staff." But when he saw it writhing as if it was a snake, he turned in flight and did not return.[1] [Allāh said], "O Moses, approach and fear not. Indeed, you are of the secure.

footnotes.text: Or "did not look back."

28:37.annotated: And Moses said, "My Lord is more knowing [than we or you] of who has come with guidance from Him and to whom will be succession in the home.[1] Indeed, wrongdoers do not succeed."

footnotes.text: i.e., in this world or in the Hereafter.

28:38.annotated: And Pharaoh said, "O eminent ones, I have not known you to have a god other than me. Then ignite for me, O Hāmān, [a fire] upon the clay[1] and make for me a tower that I may look at the God of Moses. And indeed, I do think he is among the liars."

footnotes.text: From which bricks are made.

28:40.annotated: So We took him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea.[1] So see how was the end of the wrongdoers.

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) caused them to leave all their worldly wealth behind and enter the sea in pursuit of the Children of Israel.  See 26:52-66.

28:41.annotated: And We made them leaders[1] inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped.

footnotes.text: i.e., examples or precedents, followed by subsequent tyrants.

28:42.annotated: And We caused to overtake them in this world a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "those made hideous," who will be far removed from all good and mercy.

28:45.annotated: But We produced [many] generations [after Moses], and prolonged was their duration.[1] And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses, but We were senders [of this message].[2]

footnotes.text: So they forgot and neglected the ordinances of Allāh.
The Prophet (ﷺ) had no way of obtaining this information except through Allāh's revelation.

28:47.annotated: And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands put forth [of sins] and they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers?"...[1]

footnotes.text: The conclusion of the sentence is understood to be "...We would not have sent messengers," meaning that Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) sent messengers and sent Muḥammad (ﷺ) with the final scripture to mankind so that no one could claim that punishment was imposed unjustly without warning.

28:48.annotated: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given like that which was given to Moses?" Did they not disbelieve in that which was given to Moses before? They said, "[They are but] two works of magic supporting each other,[1] and indeed we are, in both, disbelievers."

footnotes.text: The reference is by the disbelievers of Quraysh to the Qur’ān and the Torah.

28:52.annotated: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they[1] are believers in it.

footnotes.text: i.e., the sincere believers among them.

28:55.annotated: And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, "For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. Peace will be upon you;[1] we seek not the ignorant."

footnotes.text: This is not the Islāmic greeting of "Peace be upon you."  Rather, it means "You are secure from being treated in a like manner by us."

28:57.annotated: And they [i.e., the Quraysh] say, "If we were to follow the guidance with you, we would be swept[1] from our land." Have We not established for them a safe sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.

footnotes.text: By the other Arab tribes.

28:58.annotated: And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly.[1] And it is We who were the inheritors.

footnotes.text: By travelers seeking temporary shelter.  The reference is to the ruins which were visible to the Quraysh during their journeys.

28:63.annotated: Those upon whom the word[1] will have come into effect will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led to error. We led them to error just as we were in error. We declare our disassociation [from them] to You. They did not used to worship [i.e., obey] us."[2]

footnotes.text: The decree for their punishment.
i.e., We did not compel them, and they did not obey us; instead, they obeyed their own desires and inclinations.

28:66.annotated: But the information[1] will be unapparent to them that Day, so they will not [be able to] ask one another.

footnotes.text: By which they might invent lies or excuses.

28:71.annotated: Say, "Have you considered:[1] if Allāh should make for you the night continuous until the Day of Resurrection, what deity other than Allāh could bring you light? Then will you not hear?"

footnotes.text: Meaning "Inform me if you really know."

28:78.annotated: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allāh had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.[1]

footnotes.text: There will be no need to enumerate their sins separately, as their quantity is obvious and more than sufficient to warrant punishment in Hell.

28:85.annotated: Indeed, [O Muḥammad], He who imposed upon you the Qur’ān will take you back to a place of return.[1] Say, "My Lord is most knowing of who brings guidance and who is in clear error."

footnotes.text: Meaning to Makkah (in this life) or to Paradise (in the Hereafter).

28:86.annotated: And you were not expecting that the Book would be conveyed to you, but [it is] a mercy from your Lord. So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.[1]

footnotes.text: In their religion by making any concessions to their beliefs.

28:88.annotated: And do not invoke with Allāh another deity. There is no deity except Him. Everything will be destroyed except His Face.[1] His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.

footnotes.text: i.e., except Himself.
See footnote to 2:1.

29:8.annotated: And We have enjoined upon man goodness to parents. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge,[1] do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.

footnotes.text: i.e., no knowledge of its divinity.  There can be no knowledge about something which is non-existent or untrue.

29:12.annotated: And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Follow our way, and we will carry your sins."[1] But they will not carry anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.

footnotes.text: The phrase may also read:  "and let us carry your sins," i.e., the responsibility for your sins.

29:13.annotated: But they will surely carry their [own] burdens and [other] burdens along with their burdens,[1] and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.

footnotes.text: Besides their own sins, they will carry those of the people they misled, although it will not lessen the burden of the latter.

29:15.annotated: But We saved him and the companions of the ship, and We made it[1] a sign for the worlds.

footnotes.text: i.e., the ship, the event or the story.

29:18.annotated: And if you [people] deny [the message] - already nations before you have denied. And there is not upon the Messenger except [the duty of] clear notification.[1]

footnotes.text: Commentators have differed over this verse - whether it is a continuation of the words of Prophet Abraham or words of comfort given by Allāh to Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ), which according to context seems more likely.

29:29.annotated: Indeed, you approach men and obstruct the road[1] and commit in your meetings [every] evil." And the answer of his people was not but that they said, "Bring us the punishment of Allāh, if you should be of the truthful."

footnotes.text: i.e., commit highway robbery and acts of aggression against travelers.

29:31.annotated: And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Abraham with the good tidings,[1] they said, "Indeed, we will destroy the people of that [i.e., Lot's] city. Indeed, its people have been wrongdoers."

footnotes.text: Of the birth of Isaac and his descendant, Jacob.

29:33.annotated: And when Our messengers [i.e., angels] came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt for them great discomfort.[1] They said, "Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is to be of those who remain behind.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 11:77.

29:42.annotated: Indeed, Allāh knows whatever thing they call upon[1] other than Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

footnotes.text: In worship.

29:66.annotated: So that they will deny what We have granted them, and they will enjoy themselves. But they are going to know.[1]

footnotes.text: Grammatically, the verse may also be read as a threat, i.e., "So let them deny what We have granted them and let them enjoy themselves, for they are going to know."

29:67.annotated: Have they not seen that We made [Makkah] a safe sanctuary, while people are being taken away[1] all around them? Then in falsehood do they believe, and in the favor of Allāh they disbelieve?

footnotes.text: i.e., killed and taken captive.

29:69.annotated: And those who strive for Us - We will surely guide them to Our ways.[1] And indeed, Allāh is with the doers of good.

footnotes.text: The various ways and means to attain the acceptance and pleasure of Allāh.
See footnote to 2:1.
By the Persians.

30:3.annotated: In the nearest land.[1] But they, after their defeat, will overcome

footnotes.text: Another meaning is "in the lowest land."

30:5.annotated: In the victory of Allāh.[1] He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.

footnotes.text: i.e., the victory given by Allāh to a people of the Scripture (Christians) over the Magians of Persia.

30:8.annotated: Do they not contemplate within themselves?[1] Allāh has not created the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.

footnotes.text: An additional meaning is "Do they not contemplate concerning themselves."

30:19.annotated: He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living and brings to life the earth after its lifelessness. And thus will you be brought out.[1]

footnotes.text: Of the graves or out of the earth at the time of resurrection.

30:28.annotated: He presents to you an example from yourselves. Do you have among those whom your right hands possess [i.e., slaves] any partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal therein [and] would fear them as your fear of one another [within a partnership]?[1] Thus do We detail the verses for a people who use reason.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 16:71.

30:30.annotated: So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah[1] of Allāh upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allāh.[2] That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

footnotes.text: The natural inborn inclination of man to worship his Creator prior to the corruption of his nature by external influences.  Thus, Islāmic monotheism is described as the religion of fiṭrah - that of the inherent nature of mankind.
i.e., let people remain true to their fiṭrah within the religion of Islām.

30:32.annotated: [Or] of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.[1]

footnotes.text: Of beliefs, opinions, customs, etc.

30:34.annotated: So that they will deny what We have granted them.[1] Then enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know.

footnotes.text: Or "So let them deny what We have granted them."

30:39.annotated: And whatever you give for interest [i.e., advantage] to increase within the wealth of people[1] will not increase with Allāh. But what you give in zakāh,[2] desiring the face [i.e., approval] of Allāh - those are the multipliers.[3]

footnotes.text: The phrase includes several connotations, among them:  a) that which is given as usury or interest, b) that which is given on the condition that it be repaid with interest, and c) a gift given with the intention of obtaining from the recipient greater benefit or a larger gift.
The meaning of ṣadaqah (voluntary charity) is included here.
Of their blessings on earth and their rewards in the Hereafter.

30:43.annotated: So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the correct religion before a Day comes from Allāh of which there is no repelling. That Day, they will be divided.[1]

footnotes.text: Into those destined for Paradise and those destined for Hell.

30:47.annotated: And We have already sent messengers before you to their peoples, and they came to them with clear evidences; then We took retribution from those who committed crimes, and incumbent upon Us was support[1] of the believers.

footnotes.text: i.e., aid or the bestowal of victory.

30:51.annotated: But if We should send a [bad] wind and they saw [their crops] turned yellow, they would remain thereafter disbelievers.[1]

footnotes.text: Denying and ungrateful for the previous favors of Allāh.

30:56.annotated: But those who were given knowledge and faith will say, "You remained the extent of Allāh's decree until the Day of Resurrection, and this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not used to know."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., acknowledge the truth.

30:59.annotated: Thus does Allāh seal the hearts of those who do not know.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those who do not wish to know the truth and refuse it.
See footnote to 2:1.

31:2.annotated: These are verses of the wise[1] Book,

footnotes.text: See footnote to 10:1.

31:6.annotated: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech[1] to mislead [others] from the way of Allāh without knowledge and who takes it [i.e., His way] in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.

footnotes.text: i.e., that which has no benefit.  Described by different ṣaḥābah as shirk (association with Allāh), misleading stories, frivolous songs, or music but includes all which distracts or diverts one from the Qur’ān and remembrance of Allāh.

31:15.annotated: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge,[1] do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 29:8.

31:16.annotated: [And Luqmān said], "O my son, indeed if it [i.e., a wrong] should be the weight of a mustard seed and should be within a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allāh will bring it forth. Indeed, Allāh is Subtle[1] and Aware.

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote of 6:103.

31:17.annotated: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] resolve.[1]

footnotes.text: For the reason that they are enjoined by Allāh.

31:18.annotated: And do not turn your cheek [in contempt] toward people[1] and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, Allāh does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.

footnotes.text: Rather, respect them by directing your face and attention to them.

31:27.annotated: And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea [was ink], replenished thereafter by seven [more] seas, the words[1] of Allāh would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allāh is Exalted in Might and Wise.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 18:109.

31:28.annotated: Your creation and your resurrection will not be but as that of a single soul.[1] Indeed, Allāh is Hearing and Seeing.

footnotes.text: The re-creation and resurrection of one or of all is accomplished with equal ease by Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

31:30.annotated: That is because Allāh is the True Reality, and that what they call upon[1] other than Him is falsehood, and because Allāh is the Most High, the Grand.

footnotes.text: In worship.

31:34.annotated: Indeed, Allāh [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs.[1] And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul perceives in what land it will die. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

footnotes.text: i.e., every aspect of the fetus' present and future existence.
See footnote to 2:1.

32:4.annotated: It is Allāh who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne.[1] You have not besides Him any protector or any intercessor; so will you not be reminded?

footnotes.text: See footnotes to 2:19 and 7:54.

32:9.annotated: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His [created] soul[1] and made for you hearing and vision and hearts [i.e., intellect]; little are you grateful.

footnotes.text: i.e., element of life.  See footnote to 15:29.

32:13.annotated: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word[1] from Me will come into effect [that] "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.

footnotes.text: Deserved by the evildoers.

32:16.annotated: Their sides part [i.e., they arise] from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.[1]

footnotes.text: In the cause of Allāh.

32:21.annotated: And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment[1] short of the greater punishment that perhaps they will return [i.e., repent].

footnotes.text: i.e., the disasters and calamities of this world.

32:23.annotated: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt over his meeting.[1] And We made it [i.e., the Torah] guidance for the Children of Israel.

footnotes.text: i.e., Muḥammad's meeting Moses on the night of al-Miʿrāj (ascent).

32:28.annotated: And they say, "When will be this conquest,[1] if you should be truthful?"

footnotes.text: Or "decision," i.e., judgement.

33:3.annotated: And rely upon Allāh; and sufficient is Allāh as Disposer of affairs.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote in 3:173.

33:4.annotated: Allāh has not made for a man two hearts in his interior. And He has not made your wives whom you declare unlawful[1] your mothers. And He has not made your claimed [i.e., adopted] sons your [true] sons. That is [merely] your saying by your mouths, but Allāh says the truth, and He guides to the [right] way.

footnotes.text: By the expression "You are to me like the back of my mother."  Such an oath taken against approaching one's wife was a pre-Islāmic practice declared by Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) to be a sin requiring expiation as described in 58:3-4.

33:5.annotated: Call them[1] by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allāh. But if you do not know their fathers - then they are [still] your brothers in religion and those entrusted to you. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred but [only for] what your hearts intended. And ever is Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: Those children under your care.

33:6.annotated: The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves,[1] and his wives are [in the position of] their mothers. And those of [blood] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allāh than the [other] believers and the emigrants, except that you may do to your close associates a kindness [through bequest]. That was in the Book[2] inscribed.

footnotes.text: He (ﷺ) is more worthy of their obedience and loyalty and is more concerned for them than they are for one another.
The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

33:8.annotated: That He may question the truthful about their truth.[1] And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: i.e., that He may ask the prophets what they conveyed to their people and what response they received.  "The truthful" may also refer to those who believed in the message conveyed by the prophets and imparted it to others.

33:13.annotated: And when a faction of them said, "O people of Yathrib,[1] there is no stability for you [here], so return [home]." And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed [i.e., unprotected]," while they were not exposed. They did not intend except to flee.

footnotes.text: The name by which al-Madīnah was known before the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ).

33:17.annotated: Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allāh[1] if He intends for you an ill or intends for you a mercy?" And they will not find for themselves besides Allāh any protector or any helper.

footnotes.text: i.e., prevent the will of Allāh from being carried out.

33:18.annotated: Already Allāh knows the hinderers[1] among you and those [hypocrites] who say to their brothers, "Come to us,"[2] and do not go to battle, except for a few,[3]

footnotes.text: Those who dissuade others from supporting the Prophet (ﷺ) in battle.
Rather than joining the Prophet (ﷺ).
Who went out of ulterior motives.

33:19.annotated: Indisposed[1] toward you. And when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes revolving like one being overcome by death. But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues, indisposed toward [any] good. Those have not believed, so Allāh has rendered their deeds worthless, and ever is that, for Allāh, easy.

footnotes.text: Literally, "stingy," i.e., unwilling to offer any help.

33:20.annotated: They think the companies have not [yet] withdrawn.[1] And if the companies should come [again], they would wish they were in the desert among the bedouins, inquiring [from afar] about your news. And if they should be among you, they would not fight except for a little.

footnotes.text: In their excessive fear the cowardly hypocrites could not believe the enemy forces had been defeated.

33:21.annotated: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of Allāh an excellent pattern[1] for anyone whose hope is in Allāh and the Last Day and [who] remembers Allāh often.

footnotes.text: An example to be followed.

33:26.annotated: And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture[1] from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts [so that] a party [i.e., their men] you killed, and you took captive a party [i.e., the women and children].

footnotes.text: The Jews of Banū Qurayẓah, who had violated their treaty with the Muslims.
