33:27.annotated: And He caused you to inherit their land and their homes and their properties and a land which you have not trodden.[1] And ever is Allāh, over all things, competent.

footnotes.text: i.e., that taken in subsequent conquests.

33:32.annotated: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allāh, then do not be soft in speech [to men],[1] lest he in whose heart is disease should covet, but speak with appropriate speech.

footnotes.text: The meaning has also been given as "You are not like any among women if you fear Allāh.  So do not be soft in speech..."

33:34.annotated: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allāh and wisdom.[1] Indeed, Allāh is ever Subtle[2] and Aware.

footnotes.text: The teachings of the Prophet (ﷺ) or his sunnah.
Refer to footnote of 6:103.

33:37.annotated: And [remember, O Muḥammad], when you said to the one on whom Allāh bestowed favor and you bestowed favor,[1] "Keep your wife and fear Allāh," while you concealed within yourself that which Allāh is to disclose.[2] And you feared the people,[3] while Allāh has more right that you fear Him.[4] So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort [i.e., guilt] concerning the wives of their claimed [i.e., adopted] sons when they no longer have need of them. And ever is the command [i.e., decree] of Allāh accomplished.

footnotes.text: Referring to the Prophet's freed slave, Zayd bin Ḥārithah.
i.e., Allāh's command to the Prophet (ﷺ) to marry Zaynab after Zayd divorced her.  This was to demonstrate that a man may marry a woman formerly married to his adopted son.
i.e., feared their saying that the Prophet (ﷺ) had married the (former) wife of his son (which is prohibited by Allāh in the case of a true, begotten son).
By making known His command.

33:38.annotated: There is not to be upon the Prophet any discomfort concerning that which Allāh has imposed upon him.[1] [This is] the established way of Allāh with those [prophets] who have passed on before. And ever is the command of Allāh a destiny decreed.

footnotes.text: Or permitted to him.

33:39.annotated: [Allāh praises] those who convey the messages of Allāh[1] and fear Him and do not fear anyone but Allāh. And sufficient is Allāh as Accountant.

footnotes.text: i.e., the prophets (peace be upon them all) and after them, the followers of the final prophet, Muḥammad (ﷺ), who honestly convey Allāh's message to the people.

33:43.annotated: It is He who confers blessing upon you,[1] and His angels [ask Him to do so] that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.

footnotes.text: i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) cares for you and covers you with His mercy.  An additional meaning is that He praises you in the presence of the angels.

33:50.annotated: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their due compensation[1] and those your right hand possesses from what Allāh has returned to you [of captives] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet [and] if the Prophet wishes to marry her; [this is] only for you, excluding the [other] believers. We certainly know what We have made obligatory upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess, [but this is for you] in order that there will be upon you no discomfort [i.e., difficulty]. And ever is Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: i.e., bridal gifts (mahr).

33:51.annotated: You, [O Muḥammad], may put aside whom you will of them[1] or take to yourself whom you will. And any that you desire of those [wives] from whom you had [temporarily] separated - there is no blame upon you [in returning her]. That is more suitable that they should be content and not grieve and that they should be satisfied with what you have given them - all of them. And Allāh knows what is in your hearts. And ever is Allāh Knowing and Forbearing.

footnotes.text: Those mentioned in the previous verse as being lawful to the Prophet (ﷺ) or his wives to which he was married.

33:52.annotated: Not lawful to you, [O Muḥammad], are [any additional] women after [this], nor [is it] for you to exchange them for [other] wives, even if their beauty were to please you, except what your right hand possesses. And ever is Allāh, over all things, an Observer.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to verse 4:1.

33:55.annotated: There is no blame upon them [i.e., women] concerning their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their brothers' sons or their sisters' sons or their women or those their right hands possess [i.e., slaves].[1] And fear Allāh. Indeed Allāh is ever, over all things, Witness.

footnotes.text: It is permissible for a woman to appear before these people without complete covering and to be alone with them.  The brothers of both parents (uncles) are included as "fathers" or "parents," according to ḥadīth.

33:59.annotated: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments.[1] That is more suitable that they will be known[2] and not be abused. And ever is Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.[3]

footnotes.text: The jilbāb, which is defined as a cloak covering the head and reaching to the ground, thereby covering the woman's entire body.
As chaste believing women.
Or "and Allāh was Forgiving and Merciful" of what occurred before this injunction or before knowledge of it.

33:60.annotated: If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease[1] and those who spread rumors in al-Madīnah do not cease, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little,

footnotes.text: Referring here to those who commit adultery or fornication.

33:67.annotated: And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries,[1] and they led us astray from the [right] way.

footnotes.text: Also interpreted to mean "our noble ones and our elders [i.e., distinguished scholars]."

33:72.annotated: Indeed, We offered the Trust[1] to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.[2]

footnotes.text: The acceptance of obligations and obedience to Allāh.
Coveting its reward while forgetting the penalty for failure to keep his commitment.

33:73.annotated: [It[1] was] so that Allāh may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the men and women who associate others with Him and that Allāh may accept repentance from the believing men and believing women. And ever is Allāh Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: The reason for which mankind was permitted to carry the Trust.

34:3.annotated: But those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. [Allāh is] the Knower of the unseen." Not absent from Him is an atom's weight[1] within the heavens or within the earth or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register -

footnotes.text: Or "the weight of a small ant."

34:5.annotated: But those who strive against Our verses [seeking] to cause failure[1] - for them will be a painful punishment of foul nature.

footnotes.text: i.e., to undermine their credibility in order to defeat the Prophet (ﷺ).

34:13.annotated: They made for him what he willed of elevated chambers,[1] statues,[2] bowls like reservoirs, and stationary kettles. [We said], "Work, O family of David, in gratitude." And few of My servants are grateful.

footnotes.text: Described by commentators as palaces, dwellings, or places of prayer.
Which were not prohibited until the time of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).

34:14.annotated: And when We decreed for him [i.e., Solomon] death, nothing indicated to them [i.e., the jinn] his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff.[1] But when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment.[2]

footnotes.text: Upon which he was leaning at the time of his death.  A termite continued to gnaw into the stick until it collapsed under his weight.
i.e., hard labor.  This verse is evidence that the jinn do not possess knowledge of the unseen, which belongs exclusively to Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

34:16.annotated: But they turned away [refusing], so We sent upon them the flood of the dam,[1] and We replaced their two [fields of] gardens with gardens of bitter fruit, tamarisks and something of sparse lote trees.

footnotes.text: i.e., caused by a break in their dam.  Another meaning is "the overwhelming flood."

34:18.annotated: And We placed between them and the cities which We had blessed[1] [many] visible cities. And We determined between them the [distances of] journey,[2] [saying], "Travel between them by night or by day in safety."

footnotes.text: In the lands of what is now southern Syria and Palestine.
i.e., We placed the intermediate settlements at calculated distances for the convenience of travelers.

34:19.annotated: But [insolently] they said, "Our Lord, lengthen the distance between our journeys," and wronged themselves, so We made them narrations[1] and dispersed them in total dispersion. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.

footnotes.text: Stories related to others as lessons or examples.

34:20.annotated: And Iblees had already confirmed through them[1] his assumption,[2] so they followed him, except for a party of believers.

footnotes.text: i.e., the people of Saba’ or mankind in general.
That mankind could readily be misled by him.

34:21.annotated: And he had over them no authority except [it was decreed] that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is thereof in doubt. And your Lord, over all things, is Guardian.[1]

footnotes.text: Protecting and preserving the existence and attributes of His creations.

34:23.annotated: And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits. [And those wait] until, when terror is removed from their hearts,[1] they will say [to one another], "What has your Lord said?" They will say, "The truth." And He is the Most High, the Grand.

footnotes.text: i.e., the hearts of the angels who will be permitted to intercede.

34:26.annotated: Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge."[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "Opener," i.e., He who decides and lays open all matters in truth and justice and who opens the way to victory, success, relief, knowledge and understanding.

34:28.annotated: And We have not sent you except comprehensively[1] to mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. But most of the people do not know.

footnotes.text: Literally, "inclusively, without exception."

34:31.annotated: And those who disbelieve say, "We will never believe in this Qur’ān nor in that before it." But if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, refuting each others' words...[1] Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "If not for you, we would have been believers."

footnotes.text: Having been left to the imagination, the conclusion of this sentence is estimated to be "...you would see a dreadful sight."

34:35.annotated: And they[1] said, "We are more [than the believers] in wealth and children, and we are not to be punished."

footnotes.text: The affluent ones in general or the people of Makkah specifically.

34:38.annotated: And the ones who strive against Our verses to cause [them] failure[1] - those will be brought into the punishment [to remain].

footnotes.text: See footnote to 34:5.

34:49.annotated: Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither begin [anything] nor repeat [it]."[1]

footnotes.text: This expression alludes to complete inability, meaning that falsehood was abolished.

34:51.annotated: And if you could see[1] when they are terrified but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a place nearby.

footnotes.text: i.e., have a glimpse of the Hereafter.

34:52.annotated: And they will [then] say, "We believe in it!" But how for them will be the taking[1] [of faith] from a place far away?[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "taking of something within easy reach," in other words, "How can they expect to obtain faith at this point?"
i.e., their former life on earth, wherein they had every opportunity but which is now gone, never to return.

34:53.annotated: And they had already disbelieved in it before and would assault[1] the unseen from a place far away.[2]

footnotes.text: Verbally, by conjecture and denial.
i.e., a position far from truth.

34:54.annotated: And prevention will be placed between them and what they desire,[1] as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt [i.e., denial].

footnotes.text: Meaning the attainment of faith and its benefits or entrance into Paradise.

35:10.annotated: Whoever desires honor [through power] - then to Allāh belongs all honor.[1] To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it.[2] But they who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it will perish.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 4:139.
For acceptance by Allāh, meaning that righteous deeds are confirmation and proof of what is uttered by the tongue.

35:14.annotated: If you invoke them, they do not hear your supplication; and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association.[1] And none can inform you like [one] Aware [of all matters].

footnotes.text: Of them with Allāh or your worship of them.

35:21.annotated: Nor are the shade and the heat,[1]

footnotes.text: Of the sun or of a scorching wind.

35:22.annotated: And not equal are the living and the dead. Indeed, Allāh causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves.[1]

footnotes.text: The four comparisons given by Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) in verses 19-22 are those of the believer and unbeliever, various kinds of misbelief and (true) belief, Paradise and Hellfire, and those receptive to guidance and those unreceptive.

35:30.annotated: That He may give them in full their rewards and increase for them of His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., He gives much in return for little and multiplies rewards.

35:32.annotated: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen of Our servants;[1] and among them is he who wrongs himself [i.e., sins], and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by permission of Allāh. That [inheritance] is what is the great bounty.

footnotes.text: The followers of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).

35:36.annotated: And for those who disbelieve will be the fire of Hell. [Death] is not decreed for them[1] so they may die, nor will its torment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one.

footnotes.text: Or "They are not killed."

35:37.annotated: And they will cry out therein, "Our Lord, remove us;[1] we will do righteousness - other than what we were doing!" But did We not grant you life enough for whoever would remember therein to remember, and the warner had come to you? So taste [the punishment], for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.

footnotes.text: The implication is "Return us to the previous world."

35:40.annotated: Say, "Have you considered[1] your 'partners' whom you invoke besides Allāh? Show me what they have created from the earth, or have they partnership [with Him] in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are [standing] on evidence therefrom? [No], rather, the wrongdoers do not promise each other except delusion."[2]

footnotes.text: Understood to mean "Tell me about..."
By telling their followers that the so-called deities will intercede for them with Allāh.

35:41.annotated: Indeed, Allāh holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing[1] and Forgiving.

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote in 2:225.

35:43.annotated: [Due to] arrogance in the land and plotting of evil; but the evil plot does not encompass except its own people. Then do they await except the way [i.e., fate] of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way [i.e., established method] of Allāh any change, and you will never find in the way of Allāh[1] any alteration.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., in His punishment of those who deny the prophets.
Or "transfer" of punishment to others in place of them.
See footnote to 2:1.
See footnote to 10:1.

36:19.annotated: They said, "Your omen [i.e., fate] is with yourselves. Is it[1] because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."

footnotes.text: Your threat against us.

36:26.annotated: It was said, "Enter Paradise."[1] He said, "I wish my people could know

footnotes.text: An abrupt transfer to the Hereafter conveys the meaning that the man met a violent death at the hands of the disbelievers and so was martyred for the cause of Allāh.

36:29.annotated: It was not but one shout,[1] and immediately they were extinguished.

footnotes.text: From Gabriel or a blast from the sky.

36:31.annotated: Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them - that they to them[1] will not return?

footnotes.text: i.e., to those living presently in the world.

36:35.annotated: That they may eat of His fruit.[1] And their hands have not produced it,[2] so will they not be grateful?

footnotes.text: i.e., that which Allāh has produced for them.
An alternative meaning is "And [eat from] what their hands have produced [i.e., planted and harvested]."  Both are grammatically correct.

36:36.annotated: Exalted is He who created all pairs[1] - from what the earth grows and from themselves and from that which they do not know.

footnotes.text: Or "all species."

36:37.annotated: And a sign for them is the night. We remove[1] from it the [light of] day, so they are [left] in darkness.

footnotes.text: Literally, "strip" or "peel."  Sunlight projected onto the earth is removed from it as the earth turns and night approaches.

36:41.annotated: And a sign for them is that We carried their forefathers[1] in a laden ship.

footnotes.text: Usually meaning "descendants" or "offspring," the word "dhurriyyah" is used here to denote forefathers (their being the offspring of Noah), who were saved from the flood.

36:45.annotated: But when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you;[1] perhaps you will receive mercy..."[2]

footnotes.text: Of sins or of life in this world and the Hereafter.
The conclusion of this sentence is understood to be "...they ignored the warning."

36:49.annotated: They do not await except one blast[1] which will seize them while they are disputing.

footnotes.text: Literally, "cry" or "shriek," meaning the first blast of the Horn which will strike dead every living thing on the earth without warning.

36:51.annotated: And the Horn will be blown;[1] and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten.

footnotes.text: For the second time, signaling the Resurrection.

36:59.annotated: [Then He will say], "But stand apart today, you criminals.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., remove yourself from the ranks of the believers to be distinguished from them.

36:64.annotated: [Enter to] burn therein today for what you used to deny."[1]

footnotes.text: Or "because you used to disbelieve."

36:66.annotated: And if We willed, We could have obliterated their eyes, and they would race to [find] the path, and how could they see?[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) could have left man without means of guidance in the life of this world, although in His mercy He did not.

36:67.annotated: And if We willed, We could have deformed them, [paralyzing them] in their places so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.[1]

footnotes.text: He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) could have prevented man from taking any action to benefit himself in this world or the Hereafter, yet He did not.

36:68.annotated: And he to whom We grant long life We reverse in creation;[1] so will they not understand?

footnotes.text: In his physical and mental capacity.

36:70.annotated: To warn whoever is alive[1] and justify the word [i.e., decree] against the disbelievers.

footnotes.text: In heart and mind, i.e., the believers.

36:71.annotated: Do they not see that We have created for them from what Our hands[1] have made, grazing livestock, and [then] they are their owners?

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:19.

36:75.annotated: They are not able to help them, and they [themselves] are for them soldiers in attendance.[1]

footnotes.text: Maintaining and protecting their "gods."  Another interpretation is that they (i.e., the gods) will be soldiers set against them in Hellfire.

36:77.annotated: Does man not consider that We created him from a [mere] sperm-drop - then at once[1] he is a clear adversary?

footnotes.text: i.e., as soon as he becomes self-sufficient.

36:78.annotated: And he presents for Us an example[1] and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?"

footnotes.text: Attempting to establish the finality of death.

37:3.annotated: And those who recite the message,[1]

footnotes.text: To the prophets or among themselves.  Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) swears by these three kinds of angels to the fact mentioned in the following verse.

37:5.annotated: Lord of the heavens and the earth and that between them and Lord of the sunrises.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., each point or place of sunrise.

37:8.annotated: [So] they may not listen to the exalted assembly [of angels] and are pelted from every side,[1]

footnotes.text: By flaming meteors.

37:22.annotated: [The angels will be ordered], "Gather those who committed wrong, their kinds,[1] and what they used to worship

footnotes.text: Those similar to them in evil deeds.  Another possible meaning is "their wives."

37:28.annotated: They will say, "Indeed, you used to come at us from the right."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., from our position of strength, oppressing us.  Or from where we would have grasped the truth, preventing us.

37:42.annotated: Fruits;[1] and they will be honored

footnotes.text: Meaning everything delicious.

37:48.annotated: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances,[1] with large, [beautiful] eyes,

footnotes.text: i.e., chaste and modest, looking only at their mates.

37:54.annotated: He will say,[1] "Would you [care to] look?"

footnotes.text: To his companions in Paradise.

37:55.annotated: And he will look and see him[1] in the midst of the Hellfire.

footnotes.text: The companion who had tried to dissuade him from belief on earth.

37:91.annotated: Then he turned to their gods and said, "Do you not eat?[1]

footnotes.text: Consume the offerings placed before them.

37:102.annotated: And when he reached with him [the age of] exertion,[1] he said, "O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I [must] sacrifice you, so see what you think." He said, "O my father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allāh wills, of the steadfast."

footnotes.text: i.e., the ability to work and be of assistance.

37:103.annotated: And when they had both submitted[1] and he put him down upon his forehead,

footnotes.text: To the command of Allāh.

37:107.annotated: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) sent a huge ram to be sacrificed in place of Ishmael.

37:112.annotated: And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet from among the righteous.[1]

footnotes.text: This verifies that the firstborn son who was to be sacrificed was Ishmael and not Isaac, as claimed by the Jews and Christians.

37:125.annotated: Do you call upon Baʿl[1] and leave the best of creators -

footnotes.text: The name of a great idol worshipped by the people and said to mean "lord."
Ilyāseen is said by some commentators to be a plural form, meaning "Elias and those who followed him."

37:141.annotated: And he drew lots[1] and was among the losers.

footnotes.text: To determine who would be cast overboard in order to save the other passengers.  Having been overloaded, the ship was on the verge of sinking.

37:142.annotated: Then the fish swallowed him, while he was blameworthy.[1]

footnotes.text: For having given up hope on his people prematurely and having left them without permission from Allāh.

37:144.annotated: He would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected.[1]

footnotes.text: Meaning that the belly of the fish would have become his grave.

37:146.annotated: And We caused to grow over him a gourd vine.[1]

footnotes.text: Which is known to give cooling shade and to be a repellent of flies.

37:147.annotated: And We sent him[1] to [his people of] a hundred thousand or more.

footnotes.text: i.e., returned him thereafter.

37:149.annotated: So inquire of them, [O Muḥammad], "Does your Lord have daughters while they have sons?[1]

footnotes.text: The people of Makkah claimed that the angels were daughters of Allāh, yet they preferred sons for themselves.

37:156.annotated: Or do you have a clear authority?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., evidence.

37:163.annotated: Except he who is to [enter and] burn in the Hellfire.[1]

footnotes.text: Due to his disbelief and evil deeds.

37:164.annotated: [The angels say],[1] "There is not among us any except that he has a known position.[2]

footnotes.text: Refuting what the disbelievers had said about them.
For worship.  Or "an assigned task" to perform.

37:167.annotated: And indeed, they [i.e., the disbelievers] used to say,[1]

footnotes.text: Before the revelation of the Qur’ān.

37:170.annotated: But they disbelieved in it,[1] so they are going to know.

footnotes.text: i.e., in their own message, the Qur’ān.

37:173.annotated: And [that] indeed, Our soldiers [i.e., the believers] will be those who overcome.[1]

footnotes.text: If not in this world, then definitely in the Hereafter.

38:1.annotated: Ṣād.[1] By the Qur’ān containing reminder...[2]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.
The completion of the oath is understood to be that the Qur’ān is inimitable and thus a miracle from Allāh.

38:6.annotated: And the eminent among them went forth, [saying], "Continue, and be patient over [the defense of] your gods. Indeed, this is a thing intended.[1]

footnotes.text: Planned by Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) in order to gain influence and prestige for himself.

38:7.annotated: We have not heard of this in the latest religion.[1] This is not but a fabrication.

footnotes.text: Referring to Christianity or possibly the pagan religion of the Quraysh.

38:9.annotated: Or do they have the depositories of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote of verse 3:8.

38:10.annotated: Or is theirs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through [any] ways of access.[1]

footnotes.text: To oversee the affairs of their dominion.

38:12.annotated: The people of Noah denied before them, and [the tribe of] ʿAad and Pharaoh, the owner of stakes,[1]

footnotes.text: By which he tortured people.

38:13.annotated: And [the tribe of] Thamūd and the people of Lot and the companions of the thicket [i.e., people of Madyan]. Those are the companies.[1]

footnotes.text: That were defeated, among whom will be the disbelievers of Quraysh and others.

38:15.annotated: And these [disbelievers] await not but one blast [of the Horn]; for it there will be no delay.[1]

footnotes.text: Or "respite."  More literally, "a period between two milkings of a she-camel," which also alludes to the meanings of "return" or "repetition."

38:24.annotated: [David] said, "He has certainly wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes. And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds - and few are they." And David became certain that We had tried him, and he asked forgiveness of his Lord[1] and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to Allāh].

footnotes.text: For his errors, such as fear and suspicion of the two men at the outset, any mistake in judgement he might have made, concealed feelings of partiality, etc.

38:33.annotated: [He said], "Return them to me," and set about striking[1] [their] legs and necks.

footnotes.text: With his sword as expiation.  Some commentaries have also suggested the meaning of "stroking" with the hand.

38:34.annotated: And We certainly tried Solomon and placed on his throne a body;[1] then he returned.[2]

footnotes.text: Said to be a devil or a lifeless body (one without capability), but Allāh alone knows.
To sovereignty and to Allāh in repentance.

38:44.annotated: [We said], "And take in your hand a bunch [of grass] and strike with it and do not break your oath."[1] Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one repeatedly turning back [to Allāh].

footnotes.text: At a point during his illness, Job became angry with his wife and swore that if he recovered, he would punish her with one hundred lashes.  According to Allāh's instruction, the oath was fulfilled by striking her once with one hundred blades of grass.

38:52.annotated: And with them will be women limiting [their] glances[1] and of equal age.

footnotes.text: To their mates alone.

38:62.annotated: And they will say, "Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the worst?[1]

footnotes.text: They are referring to the believers.

38:65.annotated: Say, [O Muḥammad], "I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except Allāh, the One, the Prevailing,[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnotes in 12:39.

38:66.annotated: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might,[1] the Perpetual Forgiver."[2]

footnotes.text: Honored for absolute power associated with wisdom and justice.
Who continually conceals sins and faults.

38:72.annotated: So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul,[1] then fall down to him in prostration."

footnotes.text: See footnote to 15:29.

38:74.annotated: Except Iblees;[1] he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:34.

38:75.annotated: [Allāh] said, "O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands?[1] Were you arrogant [then], or were you [already] among the haughty?"

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:19.

39:3.annotated: Unquestionably, for Allāh is the pure religion.[1] And those who take protectors besides Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allāh in position." Indeed, Allāh will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allāh does not guide he who is a liar and [confirmed] disbeliever.

footnotes.text: i.e., acceptable to Allāh is that none be associated with Him in worship and obedience.

39:4.annotated: If Allāh had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He; He is Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnotes in 12:39.

39:5.annotated: He created the heavens and earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnotes in 38:66.

39:6.annotated: He created you from one soul. Then He made from it its mate, and He produced for you from the grazing livestock eight mates.[1] He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses.[2] That is Allāh, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him, so how are you averted?

footnotes.text: i.e., the belly, the womb, and the amniotic membrane.

39:8.annotated: And when adversity touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him [alone]; then when He bestows on him a favor from Himself, he forgets Him whom he called upon before,[1] and he attributes to Allāh equals to mislead [people] from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."

footnotes.text: Or "that for which he called upon Him before."

39:10.annotated: Say,[1] "O My servants who have believed, fear your Lord. For those who do good in this world is good, and the earth of Allāh is spacious. Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account [i.e., limit]."

footnotes.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) is instructed to say on behalf of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) to His believing servants.

39:17.annotated: But those who have avoided ṭāghūt,[1] lest they worship it, and turned back to Allāh - for them are good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants

footnotes.text: i.e., Satan or any false object of worship.

39:20.annotated: But those who have feared their Lord - for them are chambers,[1] above them chambers built high, beneath which rivers flow. [This is] the promise of Allāh. Allāh does not fail in [His] promise.

footnotes.text: i.e., elevated rooms, dwellings or palaces.

39:24.annotated: Then is he who will shield with his face[1] the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one secure from it]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, "Taste what you used to earn."

footnotes.text: Rather than his hands, which will be chained to his neck.

39:28.annotated: [It is] an Arabic Qur’ān, without any deviance[1] that they might become righteous.[2]

footnotes.text: From the truth.
Through consciousness of Allāh.

39:38.annotated: And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allāh." Say, "Then have you considered[1] what you invoke besides Allāh? If Allāh intended me harm, are they removers of His harm; or if He intended me mercy, are they withholders of His mercy?" Say, "Sufficient for me is Allāh; upon Him [alone] rely the [wise] reliers."

footnotes.text: i.e., "Tell me about..."

39:47.annotated: And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would [attempt to] ransom themselves thereby from the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allāh that which they had not taken into account.[1]

footnotes.text: Of His anger and punishment.

39:51.annotated: And the evil consequences of what they earned struck them. And those who have wronged of these [people] will be struck [i.e., afflicted] by the evil consequences of what they earned; and they will not cause failure.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., prevent Allāh from what He wills or escape from the punishment.

39:53.annotated: Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

footnotes.text: For those who repent and correct themselves.

39:56.annotated: Lest a soul should say,[1] "Oh, [how great is] my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allāh and that I was among the mockers."

footnotes.text: On the Day of Resurrection.

39:58.annotated: Or [lest] it say when it sees the punishment, "If only I had another turn[1] so I could be among the doers of good."

footnotes.text: At worldly life.

39:61.annotated: And Allāh will save those who feared Him by their attainment;[1] no evil will touch them, nor will they grieve.

footnotes.text: i.e., their success in the trials of worldly life and attainment of Paradise.

39:67.annotated: They have not appraised Allāh with true appraisal,[1] while the earth entirely will be [within] His grip[2] on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand.[3] Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.

footnotes.text: i.e., appreciation of His attributes.
Literally, "no more than a handful of His."
See footnote to 2:19.

39:70.annotated: And every soul will be fully compensated [for] what it did; and He is most knowing[1] of what they do.

footnotes.text: With no need for any record or witnesses, which are but means to establish proof to the soul itself in addition to its own knowledge of what it has done.

39:73.annotated: But those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein," [they will enter].[1]

footnotes.text: In such honor and joy that is beyond description - thus, the omission of this conclusion in the Arabic text.
See footnote to 2:1.

40:16.annotated: The Day they come forth nothing concerning them will be concealed from Allāh. To whom belongs [all] sovereignty this Day? To Allāh, the One, the Prevailing.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnotes in 12:39.

40:20.annotated: And Allāh judges with truth, while those they invoke[1] besides Him judge not with anything. Indeed, Allāh - He is the Hearing, the Seeing.

footnotes.text: In worship.

40:23.annotated: And We did certainly send Moses with Our signs and a clear authority[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., evidences from Allāh.

40:26.annotated: And Pharaoh said, "Let me kill Moses and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption[1] in the land."

footnotes.text: i.e., dissension or civil strife.

40:30.annotated: And he who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you [a fate] like the day of the companies[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the days on which Allāh sent His punishment upon those who rejected their prophets in former times.

40:32.annotated: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of Calling[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the Day of Judgement, when the criminals will cry out in terror, the people will call to each other (see 7:44-51), and the angels will call out the results of each person's judgement.

40:35.annotated: Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allāh without an authority[1] having come to them - great is hatred [of them] in the sight of Allāh and in the sight of those who have believed. Thus does Allāh seal over every heart [belonging to] an arrogant tyrant.

footnotes.text: i.e., evidence.

40:36.annotated: And Pharaoh said, "O Hāmān, construct for me a tower that I might reach the ways[1] -

footnotes.text: Means of ascent, pathways.

40:42.annotated: You invite me to disbelieve in Allāh and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge, and I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnotes in 38:66.

40:46.annotated: The Fire; they are exposed to it morning and evening.[1] And the Day the Hour appears [it will be said], "Make the people of Pharaoh enter the severest punishment."

footnotes.text: From the time of their death until the Day of Resurrection, when they will be driven into it.

40:55.annotated: So be patient, [O Muḥammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allāh is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin[1] and exalt [Allāh] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.

footnotes.text: What is intended is "fault" or "error" in judgement, since all prophets were protected by Allāh from falling into sin.  The implication is that all believers should seek forgiveness for their sins.

40:61.annotated: It is Allāh who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day giving sight.[1] Indeed, Allāh is the possessor of bounty for the people, but most of them are not grateful.

footnotes.text: i.e., making things visible.

40:65.annotated: He is the Ever-Living;[1] there is no deity except Him, so call upon Him, [being] sincere to Him in religion. [All] praise is [due] to Allāh, Lord of the worlds.

footnotes.text: Whose life is without beginning or end, and upon whom all created life depends.

40:67.annotated: It is He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot; then He brings you out as a child; then [He develops you] that you reach your [time of] maturity, then [further] that you become elders. And among you is he who is taken in death before [that], so that you reach a specified term;[1] and perhaps you will use reason.

footnotes.text: The time decreed for your death.

40:80.annotated: And for you therein are [other] benefits and that you may realize upon them a need which is in your breasts;[1] and upon them and upon ships you are carried.

footnotes.text: i.e., that you may use the animals to carry your loads to distant places, according to need.
See footnote to 2:1.

41:3.annotated: A Book whose verses have been detailed, an Arabic Qur’ān[1] for a people who know,

footnotes.text: i.e., revealed in the Arabic language.

41:5.annotated: And they say, "Our hearts are within coverings [i.e., screened] from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a partition, so work;[1] indeed, we are working."

footnotes.text: For your own religion or work against us.

41:10.annotated: And He placed on it [i.e., the earth] firmly set mountains over its surface, and He blessed it and determined therein its [creatures'] sustenance in four days without distinction[1] - for [the information of] those who ask.

footnotes.text: Also "four equal days" or "four days of completion."

41:11.annotated: Then He directed Himself[1] to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being],[2] willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly."

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:19.
Literally, "become" or "do [as commanded]."

41:12.annotated: And He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired [i.e., made known] in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps [i.e., stars, for beauty] and as protection.[1] That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.

footnotes.text: From the devils who attempt to steal information from the angels.

41:14.annotated: [That occurred] when the messengers had come to them before them and after them, [saying], "Worship not except Allāh." They said, "If our Lord had willed,[1] He would have sent down the angels, so indeed we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers."

footnotes.text: To send messengers.

41:22.annotated: And you were not covering [i.e., protecting] yourselves,[1] lest your hearing testify against you or your sight or your skins, but you assumed that Allāh does not know much of what you do.

footnotes.text: With righteousness or by fearing Allāh.

41:25.annotated: And We appointed for them companions[1] who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them [of sin], and the word [i.e., decree] has come into effect upon them among nations which had passed on before them of jinn and men. Indeed, they [all] were losers.

footnotes.text: In this world among the evil jinn and men.

41:26.annotated: And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur’ān and speak noisily[1] during [the recitation of] it that perhaps you will overcome."

footnotes.text: Other meanings include "speak improperly" and/or "make a clamor."  The purpose of this was to prevent the hearing or understanding of the Qur’ān.

41:29.annotated: And those who disbelieved will [then] say, "Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and men [so] we may put them under our feet[1] that they will be among the lowest."

footnotes.text: In the lowest depths of Hell.  Or "that we may step on them" in revenge.

41:37.annotated: And of His signs are the night and day and the sun and moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allāh, who created them, if it should be Him that you worship.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., Do not worship Allāh through His creations but worship Him directly and exclusively.

41:40.annotated: Indeed, those who inject deviation into Our verses[1] are not concealed from Us. So, is he who is cast into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do whatever you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.

footnotes.text: Through deviant recitations or interpretations.

41:41.annotated: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the message [i.e., the Qur’ān][1] after it has come to them...[2] And indeed, it is a mighty[3] Book.

footnotes.text: i.e., reject it or prefer deviant interpretation.
The conclusion is understood to be "...will have earned an indescribable punishment."
Inimitable, resistant to attack, protected by Allāh.

41:44.annotated: And if We had made it a foreign [i.e., non-Arabic] Qur’ān, they would have said, "Why are its verses not explained in detail [in our language]? Is it a foreign [recitation] and an Arab [messenger]?" Say, "It is, for those who believe, a guidance and cure." And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is upon them blindness. Those are being called from a distant place.[1]

footnotes.text: For all practical purposes, since they neither hear nor understand.

41:45.annotated: And We had already given Moses the Scripture, but it came under disagreement.[1] And if not for a word [i.e., decree][2] that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed they are, concerning it [i.e., the Qur’ān], in disquieting doubt.

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "he was opposed over it."
See footnote to 10:19.

41:50.annotated: And if We let him taste mercy from Us after an adversity which has touched him, he will surely say, "This is [due] to me,[1] and I do not think the Hour will occur; and [even] if I should be returned to my Lord, indeed, for me there will be with Him the best." But We will surely inform those who disbelieved about what they did, and We will surely make them taste a massive punishment.

footnotes.text: Because of my effort, knowledge, excellence, etc.

41:53.annotated: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.[1] But is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?[2]

footnotes.text: Or "that He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) is the Truth."
See footnote of 4:79.
See footnote to 2:1.

42:4.annotated: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:255.

42:5.annotated: The heavens almost break from above them,[1] and the angels exalt [Allāh] with praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on earth. Unquestionably, it is Allāh who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

footnotes.text: i.e., from the grandeur of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) above them.

42:7.annotated: And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur’ān that you may warn the Mother of Cities [i.e., Makkah] and those around it[1] and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt. A party will be in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.

footnotes.text: i.e., all other peoples.

42:8.annotated: And if Allāh willed, He could have made them [of] one religion, but He admits whom He wills[1] into His mercy. And the wrongdoers have not any protector or helper.

footnotes.text: i.e., those who desire His guidance and His acceptance of them.

42:10.annotated: And in anything over which you disagree - its ruling is [to be referred] to Allāh. [Say], "That is Allāh, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back."[1]

footnotes.text: In remembrance and repentance.

42:11.annotated: [He is] Creator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you from yourselves, mates, and among the cattle, mates; He multiplies you thereby. There is nothing like unto Him,[1] and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.[2]

footnotes.text: There is no similarity whatsoever between the Creator and His creation in essence, in attributes or in deed.
See footnotes to 17:1.

42:14.annotated: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word[1] that preceded from your Lord [postponing the penalty] until a specified time, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.

footnotes.text: Decree.  See footnote to 10:19.

42:15.annotated: So to that [religion of Allāh] invite, [O Muḥammad],[1] and remain on a right course as you are commanded and do not follow their inclinations but say, "I have believed in what Allāh has revealed of scripture [i.e., the Qur’ān], and I have been commanded to do justice among you. Allāh is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you your deeds.[2] There is no [need for] argument between us and you.[3] Allāh will bring us together, and to Him is the [final] destination."

footnotes.text: Another meaning understood from the Arabic is "So because of that [division and separation into sects], invite [them back to Allāh]..."
i.e., the consequences thereof.
Since the truth has been made clear and since those who refuse it do so only out of stubbornness or worldly interests.

42:16.annotated: And those who argue concerning Allāh after He has been responded to[1] - their argument is invalid with their Lord, and upon them is [His] wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.

footnotes.text: i.e., after people have accepted the truth from Allāh, in an attempt to turn the believers away from His religion of Islām.

42:18.annotated: Those who do not believe in it are impatient for it,[1] but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in extreme error.

footnotes.text: They had challenged the Prophet (ﷺ) to bring it on immediately.

42:19.annotated: Allāh is Subtle[1] with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might.

footnotes.text: See footnote in 12:100.

42:21.annotated: Or have they partners [i.e., other deities] who have ordained for them a religion to which Allāh has not consented? But if not for the decisive word,[1] it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: Decree.  See footnote to 10:19.

42:23.annotated: It is that of which Allāh gives good tidings to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, [O Muḥammad], "I do not ask you for it [i.e., this message] any payment [but] only good will through [i.e., due to] kinship." And whoever commits a good deed - We will increase for him good therein. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Appreciative.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote in 35:30.

42:24.annotated: Or do they say, "He has invented about Allāh a lie"? But if Allāh willed, He could seal over your heart.[1] And Allāh eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.

footnotes.text: i.e., He could make you forget the Qur’ān and deprive you of it.

42:31.annotated: And you will not cause failure [to Allāh][1] upon the earth. And you have not besides Allāh any protector or helper.

footnotes.text: i.e., escape from Him.

42:34.annotated: Or He could destroy them[1] for what they earned; but He pardons much.

footnotes.text: Meaning that Allāh could sink the ships by means of violent winds.

42:39.annotated: And those who, when tyranny strikes them, they retaliate [in a just manner].[1]

footnotes.text: Restoring their rights and not allowing aggressors to take advantage of them out of weakness.

42:43.annotated: And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of resolve.[1]

footnotes.text: On the part of those seeking the reward of Allāh.

42:47.annotated: Respond to your Lord before a Day comes from Allāh of which there is no repelling. No refuge will you have that Day, nor for you will there be any denial.[1]

footnotes.text: Of your sins or "disapproval" of your punishment.
See footnote to 2:1.

43:4.annotated: And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book[1] with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., the Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).
Also, "precise" or "specific."

43:8.annotated: And We destroyed greater than them[1] in [striking] power, and the example of the former peoples has preceded.

footnotes.text: The disbelievers of the Quraysh, who denied Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).

43:13.annotated: That you may settle yourselves upon their backs and then remember the favor of your Lord when you have settled upon them and say, "Exalted is He who has subjected this to us, and we could not have [otherwise] subdued it.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "made it a companion" or "made it compatible."

43:15.annotated: But they have attributed to Him from His servants a portion.[1] Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful.

footnotes.text: By claiming that He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) has a son or daughters, as it is said that a child is part of his parent.  This concept is totally incompatible with Allāh's unity and exclusiveness.

43:18.annotated: So is one brought up in ornaments while being during conflict unevident[1] [attributed to Allāh]?

footnotes.text: Not "obvious" or "distinct" in an argument.  Or not "seen," i.e., absent from battles.  The reference is to a daughter.

43:28.annotated: And he made it[1] a word remaining among his descendants that they might return [to it].

footnotes.text: i.e., his testimony that none is worthy of worship except Allāh.

43:29.annotated: However, I gave enjoyment to these [people of Makkah] and their fathers[1] until there came to them the truth and a clear Messenger.[2]

footnotes.text: The descendants of Abraham.
i.e., one who is obvious with a clear message, meaning Muḥammad (ﷺ).

43:31.annotated: And they said, "Why was this Qur’ān not sent down upon a great man from [one of] the two cities?"[1]

footnotes.text: Referring to Makkah and aṭ-Ṭā’if.

43:33.annotated: And if it were not that the people would become one community [of disbelievers],[1] We would have made for those who disbelieve in the Most Merciful - for their houses - ceilings and stairways of silver upon which to mount.

footnotes.text: Who assumed that Allāh's generosity to them was a sign of His approval or who would hasten to disbelief in order to obtain wealth.

43:44.annotated: And indeed, it is a remembrance[1] for you and your people, and you [all] are going to be questioned.

footnotes.text: i.e., an honor.  Or "a reminder."

43:52.annotated: Or am I [not] better than this one [i.e., Moses] who is insignificant and hardly makes himself clear?[1]

footnotes.text: That was true previous to his appointment as a prophet, at which time Allāh corrected his speech impediment.

43:57.annotated: And when the son of Mary was presented as an example,[1] immediately your people laughed aloud.

footnotes.text: Of a creation of Allāh which is being worshipped along with Him.

43:58.annotated: And they said, "Are our gods better, or is he?"[1] They did not present it [i.e., the comparison] except for [mere] argument. But, [in fact], they are a people prone to dispute.

footnotes.text: Implying that they must all be the same.

43:60.annotated: And if We willed, We could have made [instead] of you angels succeeding [one another][1] on the earth.

footnotes.text: Or "succeeding [you]."

43:61.annotated: And indeed, he [i.e., Jesus] will be [a sign for] knowledge of the Hour, so be not in doubt of it, and follow Me.[1] This is a straight path.

footnotes.text: i.e., follow the guidance and instruction of Allāh.

43:70.annotated: Enter Paradise, you and your kinds,[1] delighted."

footnotes.text: i.e., those like you.  Another meaning may be "your spouses," i.e., the righteous among them.

43:73.annotated: For you therein is much fruit[1] from which you will eat.

footnotes.text: Meaning everything delicious.

43:77.annotated: And they will call, "O Mālik,[1] let your Lord put an end to us!" He will say, "Indeed, you will remain."

footnotes.text: Addressing the keeper of Hell.

43:79.annotated: Or have they devised [some] affair?[1] But indeed, We are devising [a plan].

footnotes.text: Conspiracy against the Prophet (ﷺ).  The reference here is to the disbelievers of Makkah.

43:81.annotated: Say, [O Muḥammad], "If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of [his] worshippers."[1]

footnotes.text: Only supposing it were so, which it is not.

43:86.annotated: And those they invoke[1] besides Him do not possess [power of] intercession; but only those who testify to the truth [can benefit], and they know.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., worship.
That intercession is granted exclusively by permission of Allāh to those He wills.

43:87.annotated: And if you asked them[1] who created them, they would surely say, "Allāh." So how are they deluded?

footnotes.text: Those who associate others with Allāh.

43:88.annotated: And [Allāh acknowledges] his saying,[1] "O my Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe."

footnotes.text: i.e., the complaint of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) about his people.

43:89.annotated: So turn aside from them and say, "Peace."[1] But they are going to know.

footnotes.text: Meaning safety or security, i.e., "I will not harm you."  This was before permission was granted for armed struggle.
See footnote to 2:1.

44:3.annotated: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night.[1] Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].

footnotes.text: The Night of Decree (Qadr).  See sūrah 97.

44:4.annotated: Therein [i.e., on that night] is made distinct[1] every precise matter -

footnotes.text: Or "is separated" or "apportioned," from what is inscribed in the Preserved Slate.  The angels record and descend with whatever Allāh has decreed for the coming year.

44:18.annotated: [Saying], "Render to me the servants of Allāh.[1] Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger,"

footnotes.text: i.e., the Children of Israel.

44:20.annotated: And indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me.[1]

footnotes.text: To death.  Or "lest you assault me [with your tongues or harm me otherwise]."

44:24.annotated: And leave the sea in stillness.[1] Indeed, they are an army to be drowned."

footnotes.text: After it has parted, in order that the soldiers of Pharaoh would follow the Children of Israel and be drowned.

44:37.annotated: Are they better or the people of Tubbaʿ[1] and those before them? We destroyed them, [for] indeed, they were criminals.

footnotes.text: The tribe of Saba’.

44:41.annotated: The Day when no relation[1] will avail a relation at all, nor will they be helped -

footnotes.text: i.e., patron, protector or close associate.

44:49.annotated: [It will be said], "Taste! Indeed, you are the honored, the noble![1]

footnotes.text: As he had claimed upon the earth.  He is taunted with these words in Hell as a reminder and additional torment.
See footnote to 2:1.

45:10.annotated: Before them[1] is Hell, and what they had earned will not avail them at all nor what they had taken besides Allāh as allies. And they will have a great punishment.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 14:16.

45:14.annotated: Say, [O Muḥammad], to those who have believed that they [should] forgive those who expect not the days of Allāh [i.e., of His retribution] so that He may recompense a people[1] for what they used to earn.

footnotes.text: In the Hereafter, where those who forgive will be rewarded and those who earned evil will be punished.  This was at the outset of daʿwah (invitation to Allāh) before permission for jihād.

45:16.annotated: And We did certainly give the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgement[1] and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds.

footnotes.text: Understanding of the law.

45:21.annotated: Or do those who commit evils think We will make them like those who have believed and done righteous deeds - [make them] equal in their life and their death?[1] Evil is that which they judge [i.e., assume].

footnotes.text: Another meaning is "...[the evildoers being] equal in their life and their death," i.e., unresponsive to guidance.

45:23.annotated: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allāh has sent him astray due to knowledge[1] and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? So who will guide him after Allāh? Then will you not be reminded?

footnotes.text: This can refer to Allāh's knowledge of that person and of his preference for his own inclinations or to that person's knowledge of the truth while he refuses it.

45:24.annotated: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and live,[1] and nothing destroys us except time." And they have of that no knowledge; they are only assuming.

footnotes.text: i.e., some people die and others live, replacing them.

45:29.annotated: This, Our record, speaks about you in truth. Indeed, We were having transcribed[1] whatever you used to do."

footnotes.text: By recording angels.
See footnote to 2:1.

46:8.annotated: Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, you will not possess for me [the power of protection] from Allāh at all. He is most knowing of that in which you are involved.[1] Sufficient is He as Witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

footnotes.text: Of false implications and suggestions.

46:9.annotated: Say, "I am not something original among the messengers,[1] nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow that which is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner."

footnotes.text: i.e., I am neither the first messenger to be sent, nor do I bring something different from the other messengers.

46:10.annotated: Say, "Have you considered: if it [i.e., the Qur’ān] was from Allāh, and you disbelieved in it while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar[1] and believed while you were arrogant...?"[2] Indeed, Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people.

footnotes.text: Based upon information from the Torah.
The conclusion is estimated to be "...would you not then be the most unjust of people?" or "...in what condition would you then be?"

46:15.annotated: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning [period] is thirty months. [He grows] until, when he reaches maturity and reaches [the age of] forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me[1] to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims."

footnotes.text: Literally, "gather within me the utmost strength and ability."

46:17.annotated: But one who says to his parents, "Uff[1] to you; do you promise me that I will be brought forth [from the earth] when generations before me have already passed on [into oblivion]?" while they call to Allāh for help [and to their son], "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allāh is truth." But he says, "This is not but legends of the former peoples" -

footnotes.text: An expression of distaste and irritation.

46:21.annotated: And mention, [O Muḥammad], the brother of ʿAad,[1] when he warned his people in [the region of] al-Aḥqāf - and warners had already passed on before him and after him - [saying], "Do not worship except Allāh. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day."[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., the prophet Hūd.
Upon the earth.  It could also refer to "a tremendous Day," i.e., that of resurrection.

46:24.annotated: And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain!" Rather, it is that for which you were impatient:[1] a wind, within it a painful punishment,

footnotes.text: When you challenged your prophet.  See verse 22 of this sūrah.

46:28.annotated: Then why did those they took besides Allāh as deities by which to approach [Him][1] not aid them? But they had strayed [i.e., departed] from them. And that was their falsehood and what they were inventing.

footnotes.text: According to their claim.

46:31.annotated: O our people, respond to the Caller [i.e., Messenger] of Allāh[1] and believe in him; He [i.e., Allāh] will forgive for you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).

46:34.annotated: And the Day those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire [it will be said], "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny."[1]

footnotes.text: Or "because you used to disbelieve."

46:35.annotated: So be patient, [O Muḥammad], as were those of determination among the messengers and do not be impatient for them.[1] It will be - on the Day they see that which they are promised - as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?

footnotes.text: i.e., for Allāh's punishment of the disbelievers.

47:1.annotated: Those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allāh - He will waste their deeds.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., cause them to be lost or make them worthless, earning no reward.

47:3.annotated: That is because those who disbelieve follow falsehood, and those who believe follow the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allāh present to the people their comparisons.[1]

footnotes.text: So that they may know the results of their choice.

47:4.annotated: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure [their] bonds,[1] and either [confer] favor[2] afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens.[3] That [is the command]. And if Allāh had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself], but [He ordered armed struggle] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allāh - never will He waste their deeds.

footnotes.text: i.e., take those remaining as captives.
i.e., release them without ransom.
i.e., its armor, machinery, etc., meaning "until the war is over."

47:10.annotated: Have they not traveled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them? Allāh destroyed [everything] over them,[1] and for the disbelievers is something comparable.

footnotes.text: i.e., destroyed them and all they owned.

47:15.annotated: Is the description of Paradise, which the righteous are promised, wherein are rivers of water unaltered,[1] rivers of milk the taste of which never changes, rivers of wine delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey, in which they will have from all [kinds of] fruits and forgiveness from their Lord... [Are its inhabitants] like those who abide eternally in the Fire and are given to drink scalding water that will sever their intestines?

footnotes.text: In taste or smell, neither stagnant nor polluted.

47:16.annotated: And among them, [O Muḥammad], are those who listen to you, until when they depart from you, they say to those who were given knowledge,[1] "What has he said just now?" Those are the ones of whom Allāh has sealed over their hearts and who have followed their [own] desires.

footnotes.text: From among the Prophet's companions.

47:17.annotated: And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness.[1]

footnotes.text: Taqwā, meaning piety, consciousness and fear of Allāh, and care to avoid His displeasure.

47:19.annotated: So know, [O Muḥammad], that there is no deity except Allāh and ask forgiveness for your sin[1] and for the believing men and believing women. And Allāh knows of your movement and your resting place.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 40:55.

47:20.annotated: Those who believe say, "Why has a sūrah[1] not been sent down?" But when a precise sūrah is revealed and battle is mentioned therein, you see those in whose hearts is disease [i.e., hypocrisy] looking at you with a look of one overcome by death. And more appropriate for them[2] [would have been]

footnotes.text: i.e., one in which permission is given the believers to fight their enemies.
The words "awlā lahum" can also be interpreted as "woe to them!"  In that case, the following verse would begin, "[Better for them would have been] obedience and good words."

47:22.annotated: So would you perhaps, if you turned away,[1] cause corruption on earth and sever your [ties of] relationship?

footnotes.text: From Islām or from jihād (struggling in the cause of Allāh).

47:26.annotated: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allāh sent down,[1] "We will obey you in part of the matter." And Allāh knows what they conceal.

footnotes.text: i.e., the Jews of Madīnah.

48:1.annotated: Indeed, We have given you, [O Muḥammad], a clear conquest[1]

footnotes.text: Ibn Masʿūd said, "You [people] consider the conquest to be that of Makkah, but we consider it to be the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyyah."  Al-Bukhārī reported a similar quotation from al-Barā’ bin ʿĀzib.  Although initially regarded by the companions as a setback, the treaty, in effect, served to promote the spread of Islām, which led to the conquest of Makkah two years later.

48:10.annotated: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, [O Muḥammad] - they are actually pledging allegiance to Allāh. The hand[1] of Allāh is over their hands.[2] So he who breaks his word only breaks it to the detriment of himself. And he who fulfills that which he has promised Allāh - He will give him a great reward.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:19.
Meaning that He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) accepted their pledge.

48:11.annotated: Those who remained behind[1] of the bedouins will say to you, "Our properties and our families occupied us, so ask forgiveness for us." They say with their tongues what is not within their hearts. Say, "Then who could prevent Allāh at all if He intended for you harm or intended for you benefit? Rather, ever is Allāh, of what you do, Aware.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 9:81.

48:15.annotated: Those who remained[1] behind will say when you set out toward the war booty to take it, "Let us follow you." They wish to change the words of Allāh. Say, "Never will you follow us. Thus did Allāh say before." So they will say, "Rather, you envy us." But [in fact] they were not understanding except a little.[2]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 9:81.
i.e., they only understood the material aspects of life.

48:16.annotated: Say to those who remained behind of the bedouins, "You will be called to [face] a people of great military might; you may fight them, or they will submit.[1] So if you obey, Allāh will give you a good reward; but if you turn away as you turned away before, He will punish you with a painful punishment."

footnotes.text: To Allāh in Islām.

48:18.annotated: Certainly was Allāh pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you, [O Muḥammad], under the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, so He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with an imminent conquest[1]

footnotes.text: That of Khaybar, which preceded the conquest of Makkah.

48:21.annotated: And [He promises] other [victories] that you were [so far] unable to [realize] which Allāh has already encompassed.[1] And ever is Allāh, over all things, competent.

footnotes.text: i.e., prepared for you or decreed.

48:25.annotated: They are the ones who disbelieved and obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām while the offering[1] was prevented from reaching its place of sacrifice. And if not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know - that you might trample [i.e., kill] them and there would befall you because of them dishonor without [your] knowledge - [you would have been permitted to enter Makkah]. [This was so] that Allāh might admit to His mercy whom He willed. If they had been apart [from them], We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with painful punishment

footnotes.text: i.e., seventy camels intended for sacrifice and feeding of the poor.

48:27.annotated: Certainly has Allāh showed to His Messenger the vision [i.e., dream] in truth. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, if Allāh wills, in safety, with your heads shaved and [hair] shortened,[1] not fearing [anyone]. He knew what you did not know and has arranged before that a conquest near [at hand].

footnotes.text: i.e., having completed the rites of ʿumrah.

48:29.annotated: Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allāh; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating [in prayer], seeking bounty from Allāh and [His] pleasure. Their sign is in their faces from the effect of prostration [i.e., prayer]. That is their description in the Torah. And their description in the Gospel is as a plant which produces its offshoots and strengthens them so they grow firm and stand upon their stalks, delighting the sowers - so that He [i.e., Allāh] may enrage by them[1] the disbelievers. Allāh has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds among them forgiveness and a great reward.

footnotes.text: The given examples depict the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions.

49:1.annotated: O you who have believed, do not put [yourselves] before Allāh and His Messenger[1] but fear Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Hearing and Knowing.

footnotes.text: Rather, wait for instruction and follow the way of the Prophet (ﷺ).

49:13.annotated: O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous[1] of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

footnotes.text: Literally, "he who has the most taqwā," i.e., consciousness and fear of Allāh, piety and righteousness.

49:14.annotated: The bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not [yet] believed; but say [instead], 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts. And if you obey Allāh and His Messenger, He will not deprive you from your deeds[1] of anything. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful."

footnotes.text: i.e., the reward thereof.
See footnote to 2:1.
See footnote to 38:1.

50:12.annotated: The people of Noah denied before them,[1] and the companions of the well[2] and Thamūd

footnotes.text: i.e., before the disbelievers of Makkah.
See footnote to 25:38.

50:16.annotated: And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer[1] to him than [his] jugular vein.

footnotes.text: In absolute knowledge of everything about him.  "We" has also been interpreted to mean the angels who are mentioned in the following verse.

50:17.annotated: When the two receivers [i.e., recording angels] receive,[1] seated on the right and on the left.

footnotes.text: And record each word and deed.

50:21.annotated: And every soul will come, with it a driver and a witness.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., one angel driving the soul to the Judgement and one to testify as to its deeds.

50:22.annotated: [It will be said], "You were certainly in unmindfulness of this, and We have removed from you your cover,[1] so your sight, this Day, is sharp."

footnotes.text: Of heedlessness, or that which had sealed your hearing, your vision and your heart from guidance.

50:41.annotated: And listen on the Day when the Caller[1] will call out from a place that is near -

footnotes.text: An angel who will call out Allāh's command for the Resurrection.

50:45.annotated: We are most knowing of what they say, and you are not over them a tyrant.[1] But remind by the Qur’ān whoever fears My threat.

footnotes.text: Forcing people to belief or submission.
Explained as tracks, layers or orbits.

51:8.annotated: Indeed, you are in differing speech.[1]

footnotes.text: About Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) and the Qur’ān.
Or "May they be destroyed" or "cursed."

51:17.annotated: They used to sleep but little of the night,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., spending a portion of the night in prayer and supplication.

51:24.annotated: Has there reached you the story of the honored guests of Abraham?[1] -

footnotes.text: Who were angels given honored positions by Allāh.

51:28.annotated: And he felt from them apprehension.[1] They said, "Fear not," and gave him good tidings of a learned boy.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 11:70.

51:32.annotated: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those who defied Lot (upon him be peace).

51:36.annotated: And We found not within them other than a [single] house of Muslims.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., Lot and his family, excepting his wife.

51:38.annotated: And in Moses [was a sign], when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., evidences.

51:41.annotated: And in ʿAad [was a sign], when We sent against them the barren wind.[1]

footnotes.text: Barren of any benefit, i.e., evil.

51:47.annotated: And the heaven We constructed with strength,[1] and indeed, We are [its] expander.

footnotes.text: Literally, "hands."

51:50.annotated: So flee to Allāh.[1] Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.

footnotes.text: i.e., turn to Allāh and take refuge in Him from disbelief and sin, thereby escaping His punishment.

51:53.annotated: Did they suggest it to them?[1] Rather, they [themselves] are a transgressing people.

footnotes.text: i.e., Did the former disbelievers pass on these words to the Makkans so that they repeat the same expressions?

51:58.annotated: Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider,[1] the firm possessor of strength.

footnotes.text: Providing everything required by His creations during their decreed existence.  His provision includes guidance.
Interpreted as the Preserved Slate or possibly the Qur’ān.
The house of worship for the angels in the seventh heaven, comparable to the Kaʿbah on earth.

52:6.annotated: And [by] the sea set on fire,[1]

footnotes.text: On the Day of Resurrection.  Or "the sea which has overflowed."

52:10.annotated: And the mountains will pass on, departing[1] -

footnotes.text: Becoming dust and moving as clouds.

52:21.annotated: And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith - We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds.[1] Every person, for what he earned, is retained.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., the reward thereof.
i.e., subject or held responsible.  Literally, "a hostage."

52:28.annotated: Indeed, we used to supplicate[1] Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, the Merciful."

footnotes.text: i.e., worship.

52:30.annotated: Or do they say [of you], "A poet for whom we await a misfortune of time"?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., some accident or inevitable death.

52:32.annotated: Or do their minds[1] command them to [say] this, or are they a transgressing people?
