footnotes.text: In this expression is also a subtle allusion to the leaders of the Quraysh, who considered themselves to be great minds.

52:44.annotated: And if they were to see a fragment from the sky falling,[1] they would say, "[It is merely] clouds heaped up."

footnotes.text: Marking the onset of Allāh's punishment, as they had requested.

52:47.annotated: And indeed, for those who have wronged is a punishment[1] before that, but most of them do not know.

footnotes.text: If not in this world, in the grave.

53:6.annotated: One of soundness.[1] And he rose to [his] true form[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., strength of body and of mind.
Gabriel appeared to Muḥammad (ﷺ) at the outset of his prophethood in the angelic form in which Allāh originally created him.

53:7.annotated: While he was in the higher [part of the] horizon.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., in the sky, above the eastern horizon.

53:10.annotated: And he revealed to His Servant[1] what he revealed [i.e., conveyed].

footnotes.text: i.e., to the Servant of Allāh, Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).

53:11.annotated: The heart[1] did not lie [about] what it saw.

footnotes.text: i.e., mind or perception (of the Prophet [ﷺ]).

53:13.annotated: And he certainly saw him in another descent[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., on another occasion.  During his ascent into the heavens (al-Miʿrāj), the Prophet (ﷺ) also saw Gabriel in his true form.

53:16.annotated: When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered [it].[1]

footnotes.text: Then and there he (ﷺ) saw Gabriel in angelic form.

53:20.annotated: And Manāt, the third - the other one?[1]

footnotes.text: The three names given in this and the previous verse are those of well-known "goddesses" which were worshipped by the pagan Arabs before the spread of Islām.

53:22.annotated: That, then, is an unjust division.[1]

footnotes.text: According to their own standards.

53:35.annotated: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees?[1]

footnotes.text: Knows that his provision will be exhausted if he spends on the poor, while Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) has promised otherwise.

53:49.annotated: And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius[1].

footnotes.text: A star worshipped by some of the pagan Arabs.

53:53.annotated: And the overturned towns[1] He hurled down.

footnotes.text: Whose inhabitants defied Prophet Lot.

53:54.annotated: And covered them by that which He covered.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., a rain of stones.
Additional meanings are "singing [with expanded chest]," "heedless," or "lost in vain amusements."

54:1.annotated: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two].[1]

footnotes.text: This was a sign given by Allāh to Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) when the Quraysh challenged him to show them a miracle.

54:2.annotated: And if they see a sign [i.e., miracle], they turn away and say, "Passing magic."[1]

footnotes.text: Or "Continuing magic."

54:6.annotated: So leave them, [O Muḥammad]. The Day the Caller[1] calls to something forbidding,

footnotes.text: Said to be an angel announcing the account and judgement.

54:16.annotated: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning.[1]

footnotes.text: To those after them, who were expected to derive a lesson from previous occurrences.

54:20.annotated: Extracting the people[1] as if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted.

footnotes.text: From their hiding places.

54:24.annotated: And said, "Is it one human being[1] among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness.

footnotes.text: i.e., the prophet Ṣāliḥ.

54:27.annotated: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as trial for them, so watch them and be patient.[1]

footnotes.text: This and the following verse are an address to Ṣāliḥ (upon him be peace).

54:28.annotated: And inform them that the water is shared between them,[1] each [day of] drink attended [by turn].

footnotes.text: i.e., between the tribe of Thamūd and the she-camel - a day for each to drink.

54:29.annotated: But they called their companion,[1] and he dared[2] and hamstrung [her].

footnotes.text: i.e., the worst and most despicable among them.
Or "he took," referring to his sword or to the she-camel.

54:45.annotated: [Their] assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat].[1]

footnotes.text: This foretold event took place on the day of Badr.

54:47.annotated: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness.[1].

footnotes.text: Or "in blazing fires."

54:48.annotated: The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces [it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar."[1]

footnotes.text: One of the proper names of Hell.

54:51.annotated: And We have already destroyed your kinds,[1] so is there any who will remember?

footnotes.text: i.e., those similar to you in attitude and behavior when they rejected Allāh's messengers.

54:55.annotated: In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.[1]

footnotes.text: Who accomplishes whatever He wills whenever He wills.

55:6.annotated: And the stars and trees prostrate.[1]

footnotes.text: They submit obediently to the laws of Allāh.  See 22:18.  An additional meaning of "najm" is vegetation of a kind without a trunk, stalk or stem.

55:13.annotated: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "you two," addressing the species of mankind and jinn.

55:17.annotated: [He is] Lord of the two sunrises and Lord of the two sunsets.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the points of sunrise in the east and sunset in the west in both summer and winter.

55:19.annotated: He released the two seas,[1] meeting [one another];

footnotes.text: Two bodies of water or two sea waters of distinct characteristics.

55:27.annotated: And there will remain the Face[1] of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:19.

55:29.annotated: Whoever is within the heavens and earth asks Him; every day He is in [i.e., bringing about] a matter.[1]

footnotes.text: For each of His creatures.

55:31.annotated: We will attend to you, O prominent beings.[1]

footnotes.text: Specifically two:  mankind and jinn.

55:35.annotated: There will be sent upon you a flame of fire and smoke,[1] and you will not defend yourselves.

footnotes.text: Another possible meaning is liquefied brass or copper.

55:37.annotated: And when the heaven is split open and becomes rose-colored like oil[1] -

footnotes.text: Or "like a tanned skin."

55:39.annotated: Then on that Day none will be asked about his sin among men or jinn.[1]

footnotes.text: Once they have been condemned to the Fire.

55:46.annotated: But for he who has feared the position of his Lord[1] are two gardens -

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "the standing [for account] before his Lord."

55:56.annotated: In them are women limiting [their] glances,[1] untouched[2] before them by man or jinnī -

footnotes.text: To their own mates, i.e., being chaste and modest.
Literally, they have not been caused to bleed by loss of virginity.

55:58.annotated: As if they were rubies and coral.[1]

footnotes.text: In purity, color and beauty.

56:3.annotated: It will bring down [some] and raise up [others].[1]

footnotes.text: According to their deeds rather than wealth and social position, as is the case in this world.

56:8.annotated: Then the companions of the right - what are the companions of the right?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those given their records in their right hand and who are destined for Paradise.

56:9.annotated: And the companions of the left - what are companions of the left?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those given their records in their left hand and who are destined for Hell.
The words can also be understood as a complete sentence, i.e., "The forerunners [in good deeds] are the forerunners [in entering Paradise]."

56:46.annotated: And they used to persist in the great violation,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., shirk (association with Allāh) or disbelief.

56:58.annotated: Have you seen that which you emit?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., semen, which contains the potential for human life.

56:61.annotated: In that We will change your likenesses and produce you in that [form] which you do not know.[1]

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning has also been given:  "...in that We will replace the likes of you [with others upon the earth] and create you [in the Hereafter] in that which you do not know."

56:65.annotated: If We willed, We could make it [dry] debris, and you would remain in wonder,[1]

footnotes.text: At what had happened or remain in a state of shock.  Another meaning is "in regret".

56:73.annotated: We have made it a reminder[1] and provision for the travelers,[2]

footnotes.text: Of the great fire of Hell.
In the form of flints or other means by which to ignite fire.  Travelers are mentioned because of the special convenience to them, although it is a provision for all people in general.

56:75.annotated: Then I swear by the setting of the stars,[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) confirms absolutely by oath.
The Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ), which is with Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

56:87.annotated: Bring it back,[1] if you should be truthful?

footnotes.text: i.e., return the soul to the body, meaning that just as you cannot prevent death when it is decreed, you will not escape the recompense when it is decreed.

57:1.annotated: Whatever is in the heavens and earth exalts Allāh,[1] and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

footnotes.text: By praising Him and declaring Him far above and beyond any failure or imperfection.

57:3.annotated: He is the First[1] and the Last,[2] the Ascendant[3] and the Intimate,[4] and He is, of all things, Knowing.

footnotes.text: Before whom nothing existed.  Also, He who is supreme, foremost or uppermost.
Enduring eternally when nothing else remains.
Nothing being above Him.  Another meaning is "the Apparent," i.e., evident through His creation and revelation.
Nothing being nearer than Him by way of His knowledge.  Another meaning is "the Unapparent," i.e., concealed from man's physical senses.

57:4.annotated: It is He who created the heavens and earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne.[1] He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein; and He is with you[2] wherever you are. And Allāh, of what you do, is Seeing.

footnotes.text: See footnotes to 2:19 and 7:54.
In knowledge - observing and witnessing.

57:7.annotated: Believe in Allāh and His Messenger and spend out of that in which He has made you successive inheritors. For those who have believed among you and spent,[1] there will be a great reward.

footnotes.text: In ways pleasing to Allāh.

57:13.annotated: On the [same] Day the hypocrite men and hypocrite women will say to those who believed, "Wait for us that we may acquire some of your light." It will be said, "Go back behind you[1] and seek light." And a wall will be placed between them with a door, its interior containing mercy, but on the outside of it is torment.

footnotes.text: To where light was acquired, i.e., in the worldly life.

57:14.annotated: They [i.e., the hypocrites] will call to them [i.e., the believers], "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you afflicted yourselves[1] and awaited [misfortune for us] and doubted, and wishful thinking deluded you until there came the command of Allāh. And the Deceiver [i.e., Satan] deceived you concerning Allāh.

footnotes.text: By hypocrisy or by falling into temptations.

57:17.annotated: Know that Allāh gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. We have made clear to you the signs; perhaps you will understand.[1]

footnotes.text: That similarly, Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) can soften a heart after its hardness and guide one who had previously been astray.

57:19.annotated: And those who have believed in Allāh and His messengers - those are [in the ranks of] the supporters of truth and the martyrs, with their Lord. For them is their reward and their light.[1] But those who have disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire.

footnotes.text: Another accepted meaning is "And those who have believed in Allāh and His messengers - they are the supporters of truth.  And the martyrs, with their Lord, will have their reward and their light."

57:22.annotated: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register[1] before We bring it into being - indeed that, for Allāh, is easy -

footnotes.text: i.e., the Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

57:24.annotated: [Those] who are stingy and enjoin upon people stinginess. And whoever turns away[1] - then indeed, Allāh is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

footnotes.text: Refusing to spend for Allāh's cause or refusing obedience to Him.

57:29.annotated: [This is] so that the People of the Scripture may know that they are not able [to obtain] anything from the bounty of Allāh[1] and that [all] bounty is in the hand[2] of Allāh; He gives it to whom He wills. And Allāh is the possessor of great bounty.

footnotes.text: As long as they refuse to believe in the message of Allāh which was conveyed through Muḥammad (ﷺ).
See footnote to 2:19.

58:2.annotated: Those who pronounce ẓihār[1] among you [to separate] from their wives - they are not [consequently] their mothers. Their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them. And indeed, they are saying an objectionable statement and a falsehood. But indeed, Allāh is Pardoning and Forgiving.

footnotes.text: The saying by a husband to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother," meaning unlawful to approach.  This was a type of divorce practiced by the Arabs before the prophethood of Muḥammad (ﷺ).

58:4.annotated: And he who does not find [a slave] - then a fast for two months consecutively[1] before they touch one another; and he who is unable - then the feeding of sixty poor persons. That is for you to believe [completely] in Allāh and His Messenger; and those are the limits [set by] Allāh. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 4:92.

58:6.annotated: On the Day when Allāh will resurrect them all and inform them of what they did. Allāh had enumerated it, while they forgot it; and Allāh is, over all things, Witness.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 4:79.

58:7.annotated: Have you not considered that Allāh knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth? There are not three in a private conversation but that He is the fourth of them,[1] nor are there five but that He is the sixth of them - and no less than that and no more except that He is with them [in knowledge] wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did, on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed Allāh is, of all things, Knowing.

footnotes.text: Through His knowledge of them and their secrets.

58:8.annotated: Have you not considered those who were forbidden from private conversation [i.e., ridicule and conspiracy] and then return to that which they were forbidden and converse among themselves about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with that [word] by which Allāh does not greet you[1] and say among themselves, "Why does Allāh not punish us for what we say?" Sufficient for them is Hell, which they will [enter to] burn, and wretched is the destination.

footnotes.text: This is in reference to the Jews who would greet the Muslims with the words "Death be upon you," rather than "Peace."

58:10.annotated: Private conversation is only from Satan that he may grieve those who have believed,[1] but he will not harm them at all except by permission of Allāh. And upon Allāh let the believers rely.

footnotes.text: The reference may be to the sinful type of conversation, as mentioned in the previous verses, or to the practice of two persons speaking in confidence in the presence of a third, which might lead him to assume that he is the subject of their conversation.  Such behavior was prohibited by the Prophet (ﷺ) in narrations of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

58:11.annotated: O you who have believed, when you are told, "Space yourselves" in assemblies, then make space; Allāh will make space for you.[1] And when you are told, "Arise,"[2] then arise; Allāh will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees. And Allāh is Aware of what you do.

footnotes.text: In His mercy, in Paradise, or in everything good.
To prayer, to battle, or to good deeds.

58:18.annotated: On the Day Allāh will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you and think that they are [standing] on something.[1] Unquestionably, it is they who are the liars.

footnotes.text: They assume that their lies will be believed and that they will escape detection as they did in worldly life.

58:22.annotated: You will not find a people who believe in Allāh and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose Allāh and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kindred. Those - He has decreed within their hearts faith and supported them with spirit[1] from Him. And We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Allāh is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him - those are the party of Allāh. Unquestionably, the party of Allāh - they are the successful.

footnotes.text: i.e., "that which gives life," explained as the guidance of the Qur’ān or victory over their opponents.

59:1.annotated: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allāh,[1] and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 57:1.

59:2.annotated: It is He who expelled the ones who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture[1] from their homes at the first gathering.[2] You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allāh; but [the decree of] Allāh came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts [so] they destroyed their houses by their [own] hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision.

footnotes.text: Referring to the Jews of Banun-Naḍeer, who broke their pact with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ).
This was the first tme they had ever been gathered and expelled.

59:6.annotated: And what Allāh restored [of property] to His Messenger from them - you did not spur for it [in an expedition] any horses or camels,[1] but Allāh gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allāh is over all things competent.

footnotes.text: Meaning that they went through no hardship (i.e., war) to obtain it.

59:7.annotated: And what Allāh restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns - it is for Allāh and for the Messenger and for [his] near relatives[1] and orphans and the needy and the [stranded] traveler[2] - so that it will not be a perpetual distribution among the rich from among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And fear Allāh; indeed, Allāh is severe in penalty.

footnotes.text: Those of Banū Hāshim and Banū Muṭṭalib, whom he (ﷺ) had prohibited from accepting zakāh.

This ruling concerning properties abandoned by an enemy without a war effort differs from that in Sūrah al-Anfāl, verse 41, which refers to spoils of war in which four fifths is distributed among those who fought in Allāh's cause.

59:9.annotated: And [also for] those who were settled in the Home [i.e.,al-Madīnah] and [adopted] the faith before them.[1] They love those who emigrated to them and find not any want in their breasts of what they [i.e., the emigrants] were given but give [them] preference over themselves, even though they are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful.

footnotes.text: Before the settlement of the emigrants (Muhājireen) among the Anṣār, for whom a share is delegated as well.

59:22.annotated: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.[1] He is the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

footnotes.text: See footnotes to 6:73.

59:23.annotated: He is Allāh, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign,[1] the Pure,[2] the Perfection,[3] the Grantor of Security,[4] the Overseer,[5] the Exalted in Might,[6] the Compeller,[7] the Superior.[8] Exalted is Allāh above whatever they associate with Him.

footnotes.text: And owner of everything in existence.
i.e., transcendent above any aspect belonging to His creation.  Also, the possessor and grantor of blessings.
Literally, "Free" from any imperfection.  Also, "Peace" or "Soundness."
And safety, i.e., reassurance that His promise is always fulfilled.  Also, He who bestows faith.
i.e., who observes, guards and protects.  Also, "the Criterion."
Refer to footnote in 2:129.

Whose irresistible force is without limitation; the one above all things who compels the creation to be as He wills it.  Also, "the Amender" or "the Rectifier" who repairs, restores, completes or sets something right once again, out of His mercy.
Supreme, complete and perfect in His essence, attributes and actions.

59:24.annotated: He is Allāh, the Creator,[1] the Producer,[2] the Fashioner;[3] to Him belong the best names.[4] Whatever is in the heavens and earth is exalting Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.[5]

footnotes.text: i.e., He who destined existence for His creation.
i.e., He who brings His creation into existence.
i.e., He who gives every creation its particular form.
Refer to the final paragraphs of the "Introduction" for a brief discussion of these attributes.
Refer to footnote in 6:18.

60:1.annotated: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies,[1] extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth, having driven out the Prophet and yourselves [only] because you believe in Allāh, your Lord. If you have come out for jihād [i.e., fighting or striving] in My cause and seeking means to My approval, [take them not as friends]. You confide to them affection [i.e., instruction], but I am most knowing of what you have concealed and what you have declared. And whoever does it among you has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.

footnotes.text: i.e., close associates and friends.

60:4.annotated: There has already been for you an excellent pattern[1] in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than Allāh. We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allāh alone" - except for the saying of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I have not [power to do] for you anything against Allāh. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have returned, and to You is the destination.

footnotes.text: An example to be followed.

60:7.annotated: Perhaps Allāh will put, between you and those to whom you have been enemies among them, affection. And Allāh is competent,[1] and Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: To accomplish this or whatever He should will.

60:9.annotated: Allāh only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion - [forbids] that you make allies[1] of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.

footnotes.text: See footnote to verse 1 of this sūrah.

60:10.annotated: O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants, examine [i.e., test] them. Allāh is most knowing as to their faith. And if you know them to be believers, then do not return them to the disbelievers; they are not lawful [wives] for them, nor are they lawful [husbands] for them. But give them [i.e., the disbelievers] what they have spent.[1] And there is no blame upon you if you marry them when you have given them their due compensation [i.e., mahr]. And hold not to marriage bonds with disbelieving women, but ask for what you have spent and let them [i.e., the disbelievers] ask for what they have spent.[2] That is the judgement of Allāh; He judges between you. And Allāh is Knowing and Wise.

footnotes.text: For marriage, i.e., compensate their loss.

When a disbelieving wife chose to join the disbelievers, a Muslim husband could demand in return the equivalent of her mahr.  Likewise, the disbelievers had a similar right when a believing woman joined the Muslims.  This and the following verses were revealed subsequent to the Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyyah.

60:11.annotated: And if you have lost any of your wives to the disbelievers and you subsequently obtain [something],[1] then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent. And fear Allāh, in whom you are believers.

footnotes.text: From the side of the disbelievers, i.e., war booty or a believing woman seeking refuge with the Muslims.

60:12.annotated: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging to you that they will not associate anything with Allāh, nor will they steal, nor will they commit unlawful sexual intercourse, nor will they kill their children, nor will they bring forth a slander they have invented between their arms and legs,[1] nor will they disobey you in what is right - then accept their pledge and ask forgiveness for them of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: This is an allusion to pregnancy and childbirth, i.e., to falsely attribute a child (whether adopted or born of adultery) to a woman's husband.

61:1.annotated: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts Allāh,[1] and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 57:1.

61:6.annotated: And [mention] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O Children of Israel, indeed I am the messenger of Allāh to you confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger to come after me, whose name is Aḥmad."[1] But when he came to them with clear evidences, they said, "This is obvious magic."[2]

footnotes.text: Another name of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ).
i.e., fraud or deception.

62:1.annotated: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allāh,[1] the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.[2]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 57:1.
Refer to footnote in 6:18.

62:5.annotated: The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it on[1] is like that of a donkey who carries volumes [of books].[2] Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allāh. And Allāh does not guide the wrongdoing people.

footnotes.text: i.e., neglected their responsibility towards it by not putting its teachings into practice.
But does not benefit from their contents.

63:4.annotated: And when you see them, their forms please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech. [They are] as if they were pieces of wood propped up[1] - they think that every shout is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allāh destroy them; how are they deluded?

footnotes.text: i.e., bodies with empty minds and empty hearts.

64:1.annotated: Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allāh.[1] To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs [all] praise, and He is over all things competent.

footnotes.text: See footnote to 57:1.

64:9.annotated: The Day He will assemble you for the Day of Assembly - that is the Day of Deprivation.[1] And whoever believes in Allāh and does righteousness - He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great attainment.

footnotes.text: "At-Taghābun" suggests having been outdone by others in the acquisition of something valued.  That Day, the disbelievers will suffer the loss of Paradise to the believers.

64:17.annotated: If you loan Allāh a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allāh is [most] Appreciative[1] and Forbearing,[2]

footnotes.text: Who gives much in return for little.
Refer to footnote in 2:225.

65:1.annotated: O Prophet, when you [Muslims] divorce women, divorce them for [the commencement of] their waiting period and keep count of the waiting period,[1] and fear Allāh, your Lord. Do not turn them out of their [husbands'] houses, nor should they [themselves] leave [during that period] unless they are committing a clear immorality. And those are the limits [set by] Allāh. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allāh has certainly wronged himself. You know not; perhaps Allāh will bring about after that a [different] matter.[2]

footnotes.text: See rulings in 2:228-233.  A wife should not be divorced except after the completion of her menstrual period but before sexual intercourse has occurred, or else during a confirmed pregnancy.  The pronouncement of divorce begins her waiting period (ʿiddah).
Such as regret or renewed desire for the wife.

65:2.annotated: And when they have [nearly] fulfilled their term, either retain them according to acceptable terms or part with them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for [the acceptance of] Allāh. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allāh and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allāh - He will make for him a way out[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., relief from distress.

65:4.annotated: And those who no longer expect menstruation among your women - if you doubt, then their period is three months, and [also for] those who have not menstruated. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth.[1] And whoever fears Allāh - He will make for him of his matter ease.

footnotes.text: The ruling concerning pregnancy applies also in the case of the husband's death.

65:6.annotated: Lodge them[1] [in a section] of where you dwell out of your means and do not harm them in order to oppress them.[2] And if they should be pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. And if they breastfeed for you, then give them their payment and confer among yourselves in the acceptable way; but if you are in discord, then there may breastfeed for him [i.e., the father] another woman.[3]

footnotes.text: During their waiting period (referring to wives whose divorce has been pronounced).
So that they would be forced to leave or to ransom themselves.

65:10.annotated: Allāh has prepared for them a severe punishment; so fear Allāh, O you of understanding who have believed. Allāh has sent down to you a message [i.e., the Qur’ān].[1]

footnotes.text: Some scholars have interpreted "dhikr" here as "a reminder," meaning the Messenger (ﷺ), since he is mentioned in the following verse.

65:12.annotated: It is Allāh who has created seven heavens and of the earth, the like of them.[1] [His] command descends among them so you may know that Allāh is over all things competent and that Allāh has encompassed all things in knowledge.

footnotes.text: i.e., a similar number:  seven.

66:2.annotated: Allāh has already ordained for you [Muslims] the dissolution of your oaths.[1] And Allāh is your protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise.

footnotes.text: By means of a kaffārah (expiation).  This is required when one is unable to fulfill an oath or when one has taken an oath which would not be pleasing to Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).  See 5:89.

66:5.annotated: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorced you [all], would substitute for him wives better than you - submitting [to Allāh], believing, devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipping, and traveling[1] - [ones] previously married and virgins.

footnotes.text: Emigrating for the cause of Allāh.  Another meaning is "given to fasting."

66:8.annotated: O you who have believed, repent to Allāh with sincere repentance. Perhaps[1] your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow [on] the Day when Allāh will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."

footnotes.text: i.e., it is expected or promised.

66:10.annotated: Allāh presents an example of those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants but betrayed them,[1] so they [i.e., those prophets] did not avail them from Allāh at all, and it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."

footnotes.text: In the matter of religion.

67:3.annotated: [And] who created seven heavens in layers.[1] You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks?

footnotes.text: i.e., one covering or fitting over the other.

67:4.annotated: Then return [your] vision twice again.[1] [Your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued.

footnotes.text: i.e., repeatedly.

67:5.annotated: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps [i.e., stars] and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils[1] and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze.

footnotes.text: Thereby driving them from the heavens and preventing them from eavesdropping.  See 72:8-9.

67:11.annotated: And they will admit their sin, so [it is] alienation[1] for the companions of the Blaze.

footnotes.text: From all good and from Allāh's mercy.

67:14.annotated: Does He who created not know,[1] while He is the Subtle, the Aware?

footnotes.text: Another accepted meaning is "Does He not know those whom He created...?"

67:15.annotated: It is He who made the earth tame[1] for you - so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision - and to Him is the resurrection.

footnotes.text: i.e., stable and subservient.

67:16.annotated: Do you feel secure that He who is above[1] would not cause the earth to swallow you and suddenly it would sway?[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "in ascendancy" or "over the heaven."
In a circular motion, as in an earthquake.

67:27.annotated: But when they see it[1] approaching, the faces of those who disbelieve will be distressed, and it will be said, "This is that for which you used to call."[2]

footnotes.text: The punishment of which they were warned.
When they challenged their prophets, saying, "Bring on the punishment, if you are truthful."

67:28.annotated: Say, [O Muḥammad], "Have you considered:[1] whether Allāh should cause my death and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?"

footnotes.text: i.e., inform me.

68:1.annotated: Nūn.[1] By the pen and what they inscribe,

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:1.

68:13.annotated: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., claiming a particular lineage falsely.  The description given in these verses is of al-Waleed bin al-Mugheerah (see also 74:11-25) or possibly, as asserted by Ibn Katheer, al-Akhnas bin Shurayq.

68:16.annotated: We will brand him upon the snout.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "trunk," meaning the nose of an elephant or pig.
i.e., without conceding that nothing can be accomplished unless Allāh wills, saying, "...if Allāh wills" ("in-shā’-Allāh").  See 18:23-24.

68:25.annotated: And they went early in determination, [assuming themselves] able.[1]

footnotes.text: To carry out their plan, confident of their ability.

68:28.annotated: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allāh]?'"[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., remember or mention Him by saying, "...if Allāh wills."  An additional meaning is "praise" or "thank" Him for His bounty.

68:32.annotated: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."[1]

footnotes.text: Of His mercy, forgiveness and bounty.

68:41.annotated: Or do they have partners?[1] Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful.

footnotes.text: i.e., those to whom they attribute divinity other than Allāh or partners from among themselves.

68:42.annotated: The Day the shin will be uncovered[1] and they are invited to prostration but they [i.e., the disbelievers] will not be able,

footnotes.text: i.e., when everyone will find before him great difficulty.  In accordance with authentic ḥadīths, "the shin" might also refer to that of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā), before which every believer will prostrate on the Day of Judgement.  See footnote to 2:19.

68:43.annotated: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.[1]

footnotes.text: During worldly life.

68:44.annotated: So leave Me, [O Muḥammad], with [the matter of] whoever denies this statement [i.e., the Qur’ān]. We will progressively lead them [to punishment] from where they do not know.[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh will increase His favors to them in this world by way of trial, whereby they will sink deeper into sin and thus into destruction.

68:49.annotated: If not that a favor [i.e., mercy] from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.[1]

footnotes.text: But instead, Allāh accepted his repentance and provided means for his recovery.  See 37:139-148.

69:6.annotated: And as for ʿAad, they were destroyed by a screaming,[1] violent wind

footnotes.text: Or "cold."

69:9.annotated: And there came Pharaoh and those before him and the overturned cities[1] with sin.

footnotes.text: Those to which Lot was sent (see 11:82-83) or generally, all cities which were destroyed due to their denial of a messenger from Allāh.

69:11.annotated: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you [i.e., your ancestors] in the sailing ship[1]

footnotes.text: Which was constructed by Noah.

69:16.annotated: And the heaven will split [open], for that Day it is infirm.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., weak, enfeebled and unstable.

69:18.annotated: That Day, you will be exhibited [for judgement]; not hidden among you is anything concealed.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., any person or any secret you might attempt to conceal.

69:24.annotated: [They will be told], "Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forth[1] in the days past."

footnotes.text: Literally, "advanced" in anticipation of reward in the Hereafter.

69:27.annotated: I wish it [i.e., my death] had been the decisive one.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., ending life rather than being the gateway to eternal life.

69:29.annotated: Gone from me is my authority."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., I have no valid excuse to stand on.

69:45.annotated: We would have seized him by the right hand;[1]

footnotes.text: Another interpretation is "by [Our] right hand," i.e., Allāh would have exacted revenge with might and power.

69:46.annotated: Then We would have cut from him the aorta.[1]

footnotes.text: Causing immediate death.

70:1.annotated: A supplicant asked for a punishment bound to happen[1]

footnotes.text: In the Hereafter.  Disbelievers had challenged the Prophet (ﷺ) by invoking Allāh to bring on His punishment.  See 8:32.

70:8.annotated: On the Day the sky will be like murky oil,[1]

footnotes.text: Or "molten metal."

70:9.annotated: And the mountains will be like wool,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., in the process of disintegration.

70:15.annotated: No![1] Indeed, it is the Flame [of Hell],

footnotes.text: An emphatic refusal meaning "It is not to be."
This refers to the skin of the head or of the body or to the body extremities - which will be burned away.

70:24.annotated: And those within whose wealth is a known right[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., a specified share, meaning the obligatory zakāh.

70:30.annotated: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess,[1] for indeed, they are not to be blamed -

footnotes.text: i.e., female slaves.

70:35.annotated: They will be in gardens,[1] honored.

footnotes.text: In Paradise.

70:37.annotated: [To sit] on [your] right and [your] left in separate groups?[1]

footnotes.text: They sat at a distance in order to oppose and mock the Prophet (ﷺ), claiming that they would enter Paradise before the believers.

70:39.annotated: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., a liquid disdained.  So how can they expect to enter Paradise except by the will of their Creator?

70:40.annotated: So I swear by the Lord of [all] risings and settings[1] that indeed We are able

footnotes.text: i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā), who determines the point at which the sun, moon and stars rise and set according to season and every position of observation.

70:43.annotated: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., just as they used to race, whenever an idol was newly appointed, to be the first of its worshippers.

71:7.annotated: And indeed, every time I invited them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments,[1] persisted, and were arrogant with [great] arrogance.

footnotes.text: Refusing to look or listen.

71:14.annotated: While He has created you in stages?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., in various progressive states and conditions.  See also 22:5 and 23:12-14 in reference to development of the embryo.

71:15.annotated: Do you not consider how Allāh has created seven heavens in layers[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 67:3.

71:23.annotated: And said, 'Never leave your gods and never leave Wadd or Suwāʿ or Yaghūth and Yaʿūq and Nasr.'[1]

footnotes.text: These were the names of specific idols named after pious men of earlier generations.

72:4.annotated: And that our foolish one [i.e., Iblees][1] has been saying about Allāh an excessive transgression.

footnotes.text: A plural form may also be understood, i.e., "the foolish ones among us."

72:9.annotated: And we used to sit therein in positions for hearing,[1] but whoever listens now will find a burning flame lying in wait for him.

footnotes.text: Before the prophethood of Muḥammad (ﷺ) the jinn used to collect information by eavesdropping on the angels and then pass it on to fortunetellers and soothsayers.

72:11.annotated: And among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] not so; we were [of] divided ways.[1]

footnotes.text: In opinion, belief and religious practice.

72:13.annotated: And when we heard the guidance [i.e., the Qur’ān], we believed in it. And whoever believes in his Lord will not fear deprivation or burden.[1]

footnotes.text: In regard to his account in the Hereafter.  Nothing of his good will be diminished, nor will the evil of another be placed upon him.

72:14.annotated: And among us are Muslims [in submission to Allāh], and among us are the unjust.[1] And whoever has become Muslim - those have sought out the right course.

footnotes.text: i.e., those who deviate from the truth and act tyrannically.

72:17.annotated: So We might test them therein. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord[1] He will put into arduous punishment.

footnotes.text: i.e., refuses obedience to Him.

72:18.annotated: And [He revealed] that the masjids[1] are for Allāh, so do not invoke[2] with Allāh anyone.

footnotes.text: The term "masjid" here includes every place of worship or the earth in general.
Or "worship."

72:19.annotated: And that when the Servant [i.e., Prophet] of Allāh stood up supplicating Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass."[1]

footnotes.text: Crowding on top of each other in the manner of locusts in order to hear him (ﷺ).  "They" may refer to the jinn or to the disbelievers among the Arabs.

72:27.annotated: Except whom He has approved of messengers, and indeed, He sends before him [i.e., each messenger] and behind him observers[1]

footnotes.text: Guardian angels to protect the messenger and the message.

72:28.annotated: That he [i.e., Muḥammad (ﷺ)] may know[1] that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord; and He has encompassed whatever is with them and has enumerated all things in number.

footnotes.text: This phrase may also be read:  "So He [i.e., Allāh] may make evident."

73:1.annotated: O you who wraps himself [in clothing][1]

footnotes.text: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) addresses the Prophet (ﷺ), who was asleep, wrapped in his garments.

73:5.annotated: Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the revelation, which when descending on the Prophet (ﷺ) bore down upon him with a great weight.  Another meaning is "important ordinances."

73:6.annotated: Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for concurrence [of heart and tongue][1] and more suitable for words.[2]

footnotes.text: Another accepted interpretation of the same words is "Indeed, arising at night is more difficult...," meaning that it will only be done by sincere believers and not others.
i.e., for recitation of the Qur’ān and for hearing and understanding it.

73:9.annotated: [He is] the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of [your] affairs.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., trust in Allāh and rely upon Him.

73:17.annotated: Then how can you fear, if you disbelieve, a Day that will make the children white-haired?[1]

footnotes.text: Another meaning is "How can you avoid [punishment]" on such a Day?

73:18.annotated: The heaven will break apart therefrom;[1] ever is His promise fulfilled.

footnotes.text: From the terror of that Day.

73:20.annotated: Indeed, your Lord knows, [O Muḥammad], that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allāh determines [the extent of] the night and the day. He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to do it[1] and has turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur’ān. He has known that there will be among you those who are ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of Allāh and others fighting for the cause of Allāh. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakāh and loan Allāh a goodly loan.[2] And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allāh. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.

footnotes.text: Allāh has known that if they were to continue in such long periods of worship each night, the people would be caused much hardship.
In the form of charities and contributions to His cause.

74:1.annotated: O you who covers himself [with a garment],[1]

footnotes.text: Referring to the Prophet (ﷺ).
Specifically, idols or generally, bad conduct and morals.

74:6.annotated: And do not confer favor to acquire more[1].

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "Do not consider any favor you have conferred to be great."

74:11.annotated: Leave Me with the one I created alone[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., without wealth or children.  The reference is to al-Waleed bin al-Mugheerah, who after inclining toward the Qur’ān, denied it publicly in order to win the approval of the Quraysh.
About what he would say concerning the Qur’ān and how he might discredit the Prophet (ﷺ).

74:26.annotated: I will drive him into Saqar.[1]

footnotes.text: One of the proper names of Hell.

74:37.annotated: To whoever wills among you to proceed[1] or stay behind.

footnotes.text: To righteousness by acceptance of the warning.

74:38.annotated: Every soul, for what it has earned, will be retained[1].

footnotes.text: i.e., subject or held responsible.

74:39.annotated: Except the companions of the right,[1].

footnotes.text: i.e., the righteous who receive their records in their right hands.

74:52.annotated: Rather, every person among them desires that he[1] would be given scriptures spread about.[2]

footnotes.text: Instead of Muḥammad (ﷺ).
i.e., made public.  Much of their refusal of his message was due to envy and jealousy of the Prophet (ﷺ).

75:2.annotated: And I swear by the reproaching soul[1] [to the certainty of resurrection].

footnotes.text: i.e., that of the believer, which blames him when he falls into sin or error.

75:5.annotated: But man desires to continue in sin.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "to sin ahead of him."  This refers to the disbeliever, who denies the Day of Account.

75:13.annotated: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead[1] and kept back.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., his deeds, which await him in the Hereafter.
i.e., that which he did not do or which he delayed.

75:14.annotated: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,[1]

footnotes.text: As described in 36:65 and 41:20-23.
The people of Paradise will actually see their Creator in the Hereafter.

75:26.annotated: No! When it [i.e., the soul] has reached the collar bones[1]

footnotes.text: At the time it is about to leave the body when one is on the verge of death.

75:29.annotated: And the leg is wound about the leg,[1]

footnotes.text: From the difficulties the person faces at death or his sudden awareness of the realities of both this world and the Hereafter.  It may also refer to his shrouding after death.

75:30.annotated: To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "driving" or "herding" or "the place to which one is driven."

75:36.annotated: Does man think that he will be left neglected?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., to no end, without responsibility, or without being returned to the Creator for judgement.

76:2.annotated: Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture[1] that We may try him; and We made him hearing and seeing.

footnotes.text: i.e., a combination of the male and female substance, within the womb.

76:5.annotated: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup [of wine] whose mixture is of Kāfūr,[1]

footnotes.text: A sweet-smelling spring in Paradise.

76:8.annotated: And they give food in spite of love for it[1] to the needy, the orphan, and the captive,

footnotes.text: The meaning here may also be "out of love for Him," i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

76:27.annotated: Indeed, these [disbelievers] love the immediate and leave behind them[1] a grave Day.

footnotes.text: i.e., neglect.  The meaning may also be "leave ahead of them."
To Allāh's human messengers.

77:11.annotated: And when the messengers' time has come...[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., when they are gathered to witness concerning their nations.  The sentence's conclusion is understood to be "...the promised judgement will then take place."

77:12.annotated: For what Day was it postponed?[1]

footnotes.text: "It" may refer to either the aforementioned occurrences collectively or to the testimony of the messengers.

77:15.annotated: Woe,[1] that Day, to the deniers.

footnotes.text: i.e., death and destruction.
i.e., the Resurrection.
To stabilize the land and balance the earth.

78:10.annotated: And made the night as clothing[1].

footnotes.text: Covering you in darkness and providing rest.
In proportion to and comparable with their crimes.

78:30.annotated: "So taste [the penalty], and never will We increase you except in torment."[1]

footnotes.text: This announcement will be made to the companions of Hell.

78:31.annotated: Indeed, for the righteous is attainment[1] -

footnotes.text: Of security, success and reward, including escape and safety from Hell.
Of wine which is delicious and does not intoxicate.

78:36.annotated: [As] reward from your Lord, [a generous] gift [made due by] account,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., as a result of both their own righteous deeds and the limitless generosity of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) . Another meaning is "a gift calculated [to be adequate]."

78:37.annotated: [From] the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Most Merciful. They possess not from Him [authority for] speech.[1]

footnotes.text: None of Allāh's creatures can plead with Him on the Day of Judgement except by His permission.

78:39.annotated: That is the True [i.e., certain] Day; so he who wills may take to his Lord a [way of] return.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., a direct route through correct beliefs and righteous deeds.

78:40.annotated: Indeed, We have warned you of an impending punishment on the Day when a man will observe what his hands have put forth[1] and the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish that I were dust!"

footnotes.text: i.e., the deeds he did in this world, which await him in the Hereafter.

79:1.annotated: By those [angels] who extract with violence[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those who tear out the souls of those destined for Hell.

79:2.annotated: And [by] those who remove with ease[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those angels who ease out the souls of those destined for Paradise.

79:3.annotated: And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming[1]

footnotes.text: Speeding to execute Allāh's commands.

79:4.annotated: And those who race each other in a race[1]

footnotes.text: Racing to deliver the souls of the believers to Paradise.
According to Allāh's decree.
Those of the disbelievers who denied the Resurrection.
Those of the disbelievers.

79:11.annotated: Even if we should be decayed bones?"[1]

footnotes.text: The disbelievers say this in ridicule of the warning.

79:12.annotated: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., "If that were so, we would not be able to escape punishment."

79:20.annotated: And he showed him the greatest sign,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the miracle of his staff becoming a great snake.

79:22.annotated: Then he turned his back, striving [i.e., plotting].[1]

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "running [from the snake]."

79:25.annotated: So Allāh seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression].[1].

footnotes.text: i.e., for Pharaoh's setting himself up as a deity and for his previous oppression of the people and denial of Moses.

79:29.annotated: And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., created the day from within the surrounding darkness.

79:34.annotated: But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the Day of Resurrection.

79:40.annotated: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord[1] and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,

footnotes.text: See footnote to 55:46

79:42.annotated: They ask you, [O Muḥammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "resting" or "establishment."

79:43.annotated: In what [position] are you that you should mention it?[1]

footnotes.text: Meaning that Muḥammad (ﷺ) had no knowledge of it, so how could he inform them?

79:44.annotated: To your Lord is its finality.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., its destination and termination. And to Him belongs ultimate knowledge of it.

79:46.annotated: It will be, on the Day they see it,[1] as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.

footnotes.text: i.e., the Hour, the Resurrection.

80:2.annotated: Because there came to him the blind man,[1] [interrupting].

footnotes.text: ʿAbdullāh, the son of Umm Maktūm.

80:3.annotated: But what would make you perceive, [O Muḥammad], that perhaps he might be purified[1]

footnotes.text: As a result of what he learns from you.

80:5.annotated: As for he who thinks himself without need,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., without need of faith or need of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) . Here it is in reference to a certain influential member of the Quraysh whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had hoped to bring to Islām.

80:7.annotated: And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified.[1]

footnotes.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) was responsible only for conveying the message, not for ultimate guidance.

80:12.annotated: So whoever wills may remember it.[1]

footnotes.text: The revelation. Or "Him," i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) .

80:17.annotated: Destroyed [i.e., cursed] is man;[1] how disbelieving is he.

footnotes.text: i.e., those who deny Allāh's message.

80:19.annotated: From a sperm-drop He created him and destined for him;[1]

footnotes.text: His proportions, provisions, life span, etc.

80:20.annotated: Then He eased the way for him;[1]

footnotes.text: Into this world (i.e., his birth) . It may also refer to life itself, which has been made easier by Allāh's guidance.

80:21.annotated: Then He causes his death and provides a grave for him.[1]

footnotes.text: To conceal his decaying body.

80:33.annotated: But when there comes the Deafening Blast[1]

footnotes.text: The piercing blast of the Horn which signals resurrection. Aṣ-Ṣākhkhah is also a name for the Day of Resurrection.

80:37.annotated: For every man, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., to occupy him. He will be concerned only with himself, thus forgetting all others.

81:4.annotated: And when full-term she-camels[1] are neglected

footnotes.text: Those ten months pregnant and nearing delivery. This verse alludes to distraction from the most valued of possessions.

81:6.annotated: And when the seas are filled with flame[1]

footnotes.text: Or "when the seas have overflowed [into each other]."

81:7.annotated: And when the souls are paired[1]

footnotes.text: With another like soul. It can also mean "joined" (with their groups or sects) .

81:10.annotated: And when the pages[1] are spread [i.e., made public]

footnotes.text: On which are recorded the deeds of all people.

81:14.annotated: A soul will [then] know what it has brought [with it].[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., all of one's deeds from worldly life, which have accompanied the soul to the Hereafter.

81:17.annotated: And by the night as it closes in[1]

footnotes.text: An alternative meaning is "as it departs."

81:22.annotated: And your companion [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) ] is not [at all] mad.[1]

footnotes.text: Literally, "possessed by jinn."

81:23.annotated: And he has already seen him [i.e., Gabriel] in the clear horizon.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the eastern horizon, where the sun rises. See footnote to 53:6

81:24.annotated: And he [i.e., Muḥammad (ﷺ)] is not a withholder of [knowledge of] the unseen.[1]

footnotes.text: Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) did not withhold that knowledge of the unseen which Allāh had revealed to him in the Qur’ān.
In your denial of the Qur’ān and in your accusations against the Prophet (ﷺ) . The meaning is essentially "Surely, you have strayed far from Allāh's path."

82:10.annotated: And indeed, [appointed] over you are keepers,[1]

footnotes.text: Angels who preserve the deeds of men in records.

83:1.annotated: Woe to those who give less [than due],[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those who cheat people by giving them less than what they paid for when weighing or measuring - an amount so little as to hardly be noticed.

83:9.annotated: It is [their destination[1] recorded in] a register inscribed.

footnotes.text: The lowest depths of Hell.

83:14.annotated: No! Rather, the stain has covered their hearts of that which they were earning.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., their sins.

83:15.annotated: No! Indeed, from their Lord, that Day, they will be partitioned.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., they will not be able to see Him.

83:20.annotated: It is [their destination[1] recorded in] a register inscribed

footnotes.text: The highest elevations of Paradise.

83:25.annotated: They will be given to drink [pure] wine[1] [which was] sealed.

footnotes.text: Which is delicious and does not intoxicate.

83:26.annotated: The last of it[1] is musk. So for this let the competitors compete.

footnotes.text: i.e., its lingering odor.

83:27.annotated: And its mixture is of Tasneem,[1]

footnotes.text: The highest spring in Paradise and the most favored drink of its inhabitants.

83:34.annotated: So Today[1] those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers,

footnotes.text: On the Day of Judgement.

84:2.annotated: And has listened [i.e., responded][1] to its Lord and was obligated [to do so]

footnotes.text: It will have heard Allāh's command and will have inclined immediately to compliance and willing obedience.

84:3.annotated: And when the earth has been extended[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., stretched flat and spread out.

84:4.annotated: And has cast out that within it[1] and relinquished [it].

footnotes.text: Of the dead and all else buried therein.

84:6.annotated: O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion[1] and will meet it.[2]

footnotes.text: i.e., striving throughout your life until you meet your Lord, hastening toward death.
i.e., you will find all that you intended and accomplished awaiting you in the Hereafter. Another meaning is "And will meet Him [i.e., your Lord]" and be recompensed in full by Him.

84:19.annotated: [That] you will surely embark upon [i.e., experience] state after state.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., various stages, both in this life and in the Hereafter.

85:4.annotated: Destroyed [i.e., cursed] were the companions of the trench[1]

footnotes.text: Or "May they be destroyed" or "cursed." The "companions of the trench" (or ditch) were agents of a tyrannical king who refused to allow his people to believe in Allāh. Their evil deed in obedience to their ruler earned for them the curse of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) .

85:7.annotated: And they, to what they were doing against the believers, were witnesses. [1]

footnotes.text: After casting the believers into a trench filled with fire, they sat at its edge, watching them burn to death. This event occurred before the time of Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ) .

85:9.annotated: To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allāh, over all things, is Witness.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 4:79

85:10.annotated: Indeed, those who have tortured[1] the believing men and believing women and then have not repented will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire.

footnotes.text: Or, in this instance, the literal meaning of "burned" is also appropriate.

85:20.annotated: While Allāh encompasses them from behind.[1]

footnotes.text: See footnote to 2:19
Whose light pierces through the darkness.

86:9.annotated: The Day when secrets will be put on trial,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., exposed, examined and judged.

86:11.annotated: By the sky which sends back[1]

footnotes.text: Rain, heat, sound waves, etc.
With plant growth or from geological rifts.

86:17.annotated: So allow time for the disbelievers. Leave them awhile.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., Do not be in haste for revenge, for you will see what will become of them.

87:8.annotated: And We will ease you toward ease.[1]

footnotes.text: To the path of Allāh's religion, which is easy and natural, or toward Paradise, by giving opportunities for righteous deeds.

87:9.annotated: So remind, if the reminder should benefit;[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., wherever it will be heard and understood.

Another accepted meaning is "They were working hard and exhausted," i.e., doing deeds during worldly life which did not benefit them since they were not accompanied by faith or done for the acceptance of Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) .

88:11.annotated: Wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., any insult, falsehood, immorality, idle or vain talk, etc.
Usually interpreted as the first ten nights of the month of Dhul-Ḥijjah.

89:5.annotated: Is there [not] in [all] that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?[1]

footnotes.text: Based upon the following verses, what has been sworn to by Allāh is that He will certainly punish the disbelievers.
Another name for the first people of ʿAad, to whom Prophet Hūd was sent.
Supporting their tents or buildings.

89:10.annotated: And [with] Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?[1]

footnotes.text: By which he tortured people.

89:15.annotated: And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."[1]

footnotes.text: He is proud rather than grateful, attributing the favor to his own merit.

89:17.annotated: No![1] But you do not honor the orphan

footnotes.text: It is not like you imagine. Rather, Allāh tries people through prosperity and hardship and rewards both gratitude and patience with honor in the Hereafter.

89:19.annotated: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,[1]

footnotes.text: Not caring whether it is lawful or unlawful.

89:22.annotated: And your Lord has come[1] and the angels, rank upon rank,

footnotes.text: To pass judgement. See footnote to 2:19

89:24.annotated: He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."[1]

footnotes.text: The everlasting life of the Hereafter.

90:3.annotated: And [by] the father[1] and that which was born [of him],

footnotes.text: Said to be Adam (upon him be peace) .

90:10.annotated: And have shown him the two ways?[1]

footnotes.text: Of good and evil.

90:11.annotated: But he has not broken through the difficult pass.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the steep incline or obstacle. In other words, he has not spent in the cause of Allāh but only boasts of spending in front of others.

90:18.annotated: Those are the companions of the right.[1]

footnotes.text: Or "the companions of good fortune," i.e., those who receive their records in their right hands and proceed to Paradise.

90:19.annotated: But they who disbelieved in Our signs - those are the companions of the left.[1]

footnotes.text: Or "the companions of ill fortune," i.e., those who receive their records in their left hands and proceed to Hell.

90:20.annotated: Over them will be fire closed in.[1]

footnotes.text: The cover over Hell will be sealed and locked, containing its fire and its inhabitants.

91:3.annotated: And [by] the day when it displays it[1]

footnotes.text: The earth. Also interpreted as the sun. The same applies to the following verse.

91:7.annotated: And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., balanced and refined it, creating in it sound tendencies and consciousness.

91:12.annotated: When the most wretched of them was sent forth.[1]

footnotes.text: To hamstring the she-camel which had been sent by Allāh as a sign to them.

91:14.annotated: But they denied him and hamstrung[1] her. So their Lord brought down upon them destruction for their sin and made it equal [upon all of them].

footnotes.text: And then killed.

91:15.annotated: And He does not fear the consequence thereof.[1]

footnotes.text: Allāh is not asked about what He does, but His servants will be asked. See 21:23

92:1.annotated: By the night when it covers[1]

footnotes.text: With darkness.

92:11.annotated: And what will his wealth avail him when he falls?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., when he dies or is destroyed. It can also mean when he falls into the Hellfire.

92:19.annotated: And not [giving] for anyone who has [done him] a favor to be rewarded[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., without intending reciprocation for some benefit to himself.

93:2.annotated: And [by] the night when it covers with darkness,[1]

footnotes.text: And becomes still.

93:10.annotated: And as for the petitioner,[1] do not repel [him].

footnotes.text: Anyone who seeks aid or knowledge.

94:1.annotated: Did We not expand for you, [O Muḥammad], your breast?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., enlighten, assure and gladden your heart with guidance.

94:2.annotated: And We removed from you your burden[1]

footnotes.text: By forgiving any errors which you may have committed previously or might commit consequently. "Burden" can also refer to the anxiety experienced by the Prophet (ﷺ) at the beginning of his mission.

95:1.annotated: By the fig and the olive[1]

footnotes.text: Referring to the places known for their production, i.e., Damascus and Jerusalem, respectively. It could also refer to the fig and olive trees or to the fruits themselves.

95:4.annotated: We have certainly created man in the best of stature;[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., upright, symmetrical, and balanced in form and nature.

95:5.annotated: Then We return him to the lowest of the low,[1]

footnotes.text: This can refer to the depths of Hell, to decrepit old age or to immorality.

95:7.annotated: So what yet causes you to deny the Recompense?[1]

footnotes.text: More literally, "What makes you lie concerning it?"

96:15.annotated: No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock[1]

footnotes.text: It may also mean "slap him" or "blacken his face at the forelock."

96:18.annotated: We will call the angels of Hell.[1]

footnotes.text: Those who push the wicked into the Fire.

97:4.annotated: The angels and the Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] descend therein by permission of their Lord for every matter.[1]

footnotes.text: Bringing the exact measures apportioned for everything by Allāh in the course of the coming year.

97:5.annotated: Peace it is[1] until the emergence of dawn.

footnotes.text: Upon the believers.

98:1.annotated: Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists were not to be parted [from misbelief][1] until there came to them clear evidence

footnotes.text: i.e., from their erroneous beliefs and superstitions.

98:2.annotated: A Messenger from Allāh, reciting purified[1] scriptures

footnotes.text: i.e., containing no falsehood.

98:4.annotated: Nor did those who were given the Scripture become divided[1] until after there had come to them clear evidence.

footnotes.text: Into sects and denominations.

99:2.annotated: And the earth discharges its burdens[1]

footnotes.text: See verse 84:4

99:3.annotated: And man says,[1] "What is [wrong] with it?" -

footnotes.text: In terror and amazement.

99:6.annotated: That Day, the people will depart[1] separated [into categories] to be shown [the result of] their deeds.

footnotes.text: From the place of Judgement to their final abode. Another interpretation is "emerge separately" (from the graves) .

99:7.annotated: So whoever does an atom's weight[1] of good will see it,

footnotes.text: Or "the weight of a small ant."
i.e., the horses of those fighting for Allāh's cause as they race to attack the enemy.

100:2.annotated: And the producers of sparks [when] striking[1]

footnotes.text: Their hoofs while galloping over rocky terrain.
While the enemy is unaware.

100:5.annotated: Arriving thereby in the center[1] collectively,

footnotes.text: i.e., penetrating into the enemy ranks during a surprise attack.

100:7.annotated: And indeed, he is to that a witness.[1]

footnotes.text: Through his speech and his actions.

100:10.annotated: And that within the breasts is obtained,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., when all secrets are made known.

100:11.annotated: Indeed, their Lord with them, that Day, is [fully] Aware.[1]

footnotes.text: Fully acquainted and familiar with everything about each one of them.

101:4.annotated: It is the Day when people will be like moths, dispersed,[1]

footnotes.text: The people will be as such after having been expelled from their graves.

101:5.annotated: And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., beginning to disintegrate.

101:9.annotated: His refuge[1] will be an abyss.[2]

footnotes.text: Literally, "mother" (a man's original refuge) , which will envelop him as in an embrace.
i.e., the pit of Hellfire.
i.e., remain in them temporarily, meaning until the Day of Resurrection.

102:5.annotated: No! If you only knew with knowledge of certainty...[1]

footnotes.text: The conclusion of this verse is estimated to be "...you would not have been distracted from preparing for the Hereafter."

102:7.annotated: Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., with actual eyesight.

102:8.annotated: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the comforts of worldly life and whether you were grateful to Allāh for His blessings.
An oath in which Allāh swears by time throughout the ages.

104:2.annotated: Who collects wealth and [continuously] counts it.[1]

footnotes.text: Rather than spending in the way of Allāh.

104:4.annotated: No! He will surely be thrown into the Crusher.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., Hellfire, which crushes and destroys all that enters it.

104:7.annotated: Which mounts directed at the hearts.[1]

footnotes.text: Covering them and penetrating them.
Interpreted to be either columns of fire or columns of iron to which are chained the inmates of Hell.

105:1.annotated: Have you not considered, [O Muḥammad], how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the army under the command of Abrahah al-Ashram which was accompanied by a huge elephant and came with the intention of destroying the Kaʿbah at Makkah.

105:2.annotated: Did He not make their plan into misguidance?[1]

footnotes.text: Causing them to perish.

105:5.annotated: And He made them like eaten straw.[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., husks which have been chewed by cattle. This event took place in the year of the Prophet's birth.

106:1.annotated: For the accustomed security of the Quraysh[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the honor and reputation Allāh had given them as guardians of the Holy Kaʿbah, which allowed them to travel without fear of being harmed.

106:2.annotated: Their accustomed security [in] the caravan of winter and summer[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the trading caravans that traveled south in winter and north in summer.

106:3.annotated: Let them worship the Lord of this House,[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., the Kaʿbah.

107:5.annotated: [But] who are heedless of their prayer[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., the hypocrites who are unconcerned if they miss prayers when no one sees them.

108:3.annotated: Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off.[1]

footnotes.text: From all good in this world and the Hereafter.

110:1.annotated: When the victory of Allāh has come and the conquest,[1]

footnotes.text: The conquest of Makkah.

110:3.annotated: Then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord and ask forgiveness of Him. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of Repentance.[1]

footnotes.text: Refer to footnote of 2:37

111:1.annotated: May the hands of Abū Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.[1]

footnotes.text: Abū Lahab (the Prophet's uncle) , who was an enemy of Islām.

111:4.annotated: And his wife [as well] - the carrier of firewood.[1]

footnotes.text: She used to put thorns in the Prophet's path and slander him (ﷺ) . The word "firewood" was used by the Arabs to allude to slander and backbiting.
Alone, without another, indivisible with absolute and permanent unity and distinct from all else. The one and only true deity, unique in His essence, attributes and deeds.

He who is absolute, perfect, complete, essential, self-sufficient and sufficient to meet the needs of all creation; the one eternally and constantly required and sought, depended upon by all existence and to whom all matters will ultimately return.

113:4.annotated: And from the evil of the blowers in knots[1]

footnotes.text: i.e., those who practice magic.

114:4.annotated: From the evil of the retreating whisperer[1] -

footnotes.text: i.e., a devil who makes evil suggestions to man but disappears when one remembers Allāh.

114:6.annotated: From among the jinn and mankind".[1]

footnotes.text: Evil prompters may be from men as well as from jinn.
